P2100.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit/Open
P2100.description: P2100 reports an electrical fault in the drive circuit of the first electronic throttle motor, usually an open line. Ford's 2012 summary uses it for an open circuit or a short to power or ground (no MIL, wrench lamp). GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 checks the bank 1 H-bridge three ways: open load above 200 kOhm, driver overtemperature and short to ground below 0.5 Ohm, each in one trip. Ford's 2024 summary even uses P2100 as the base code for several throttle faults with failure-type bytes. Ducati reports P2100 for the front-bank throttle motor of its V4. The throttle springs to limp position, so the engine runs with little power. Wrong position is P2101; low/high circuit are P2102/P2103; the B actuator is P210A.

causes.label: Moisture or corrosion in the throttle body or ECU connector
Broken or chafed motor wire between ECU and throttle body
Open winding or worn brushes in the throttle motor
Damaged H-bridge output stage in the engine control unit

symptoms: Throttle held in limp position, very low power
Engine or ETC warning lamp on
Little or no response to the accelerator pedal

P2101.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.description: Here the controller compares where throttle A should be with where its position sensors say it is. GM's 2018 table 18OBDG03A flags a gap of more than 10 percent between measured and modelled position after 15 counts at 12.5 ms each, classed by GM as Type A with immediate MIL; the 2006/2007 tables used 8.4 percent. VW's 2014 data book accepts 4-50 percent deviation or a drive duty cycle above 80 percent. Ford sets it with MIL and wrench lamp; Mercedes-AMG M177 engines show it with corroded throttle connector pins, and GM issued field bulletins for the LGZ V6 and 2017 V8 trucks. Causes are mostly mechanical or contact problems, not a dead circuit (P2100). Expect reduced power or limp mode.

causes.label: Carbon or ice makes the throttle plate stiff or sticky
High resistance at the throttle connector pins
Worn gear train or weak motor inside the throttle body
Deformed inlet duct or leak at the throttle body

symptoms: Reduced engine power message or limp mode

P2102.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.description: P2102 means the output stage for throttle motor A sees a voltage or current that points to a short toward ground or an overloaded driver. GM lists P2100-P2103 together in its 2018 calibration as faults that limit engine power and default the throttle authority; a Bosch-based GM ECM of 2012 assigns its output-stage checks (short circuit, overtemperature or overcurrent, open load) to this group with about 0.1 s detection. Apart from such tables, no maker publicly documents P2102 on its own; many current ECUs report the same fault under P2100 with a failure-type byte. CARB requires circuit faults of output components to be detected. The throttle drops to limp position and power is cut. The high-side counterpart is P2103.

causes.label: Motor wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Shorted winding or jammed motor drawing excess current
Water in the throttle connector bridging terminals
Faulty throttle driver in the engine control unit

symptoms: Limp mode with throttle at fixed opening

P2103.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit High
P2103.description: P2103 is the high-side fault of the throttle A drive: the output stage sees a voltage that suggests a short to battery, or on some layouts the supply relay of the throttle motor stays energized when it should be off. GM groups P2100-P2103 as power-limiting faults (18OBDG03A), and its Bosch-based 2012 ECM ties a power-stage short circuit to this range with about 0.1 s detection. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander list files P2100 and P2103 under the short name ETC MOT PWR, i.e. the supply of the throttle control motor, stored after one trip. The throttle is de-energized and power limited. Low-side faults are P2102, open circuit P2100.

causes.label: Motor wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Throttle motor relay sticking on (where fitted)
Damaged or wet throttle connector
Internal fault in the ECU throttle driver

symptoms: Limp mode with very limited power
Engine may not start or stalls

P2104.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Idle
P2104.description: P2104 is a status code: it does not name a broken part but records that the throttle control has switched into a forced-idle failure mode. In Ford's 2012 summary this happens on second-generation ETC systems when two or three accelerator pedal sensor tracks are lost, so the computer can no longer read driver demand; the engine then holds a raised idle and ignores the pedal, with MIL and wrench lamp. The actual cause is stored alongside it, usually a pedal sensor code such as P2122-P2128 or P2138. CARB counts such default modes as malfunctions whenever they can raise emissions. Repair means fixing the causal code, then clearing P2104. Related states are limited power (P2106), limited rpm (P2110) and shutdown (P2105).

causes.label: Failure of two or more accelerator pedal sensor tracks
Pedal sensor wiring or shared 5 V reference fault
ECU input or software fault

symptoms: Engine stays at raised idle, pedal has no effect
Engine and ETC/wrench warning lamps on
Car can only creep to a safe place

P2105.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Engine Shutdown
P2105.description: P2105 is the most severe throttle failure mode: the controller has decided that throttle control can no longer be trusted and stops the engine. In Ford's 2012 summary the trigger is a serious processor fault found by the separate monitoring processor (Ford calls it the Quizzer); all injectors are switched off and the wrench lamp comes on. Ford sets it without MIL, arguing that a shutdown cannot raise emissions, which matches the CARB idea of emissions-neutral default actions. The cause sits in the engine computer, its supply or a companion code such as P0606 or P2107. For the driver the engine dies or will not keep running. Milder states are forced idle (P2104), limited power (P2106) and limited rpm (P2110).

causes.label: Monitoring processor detects an internal ECU fault
Unstable ECU supply or ground connection
ECU software fault cured by reprogramming

symptoms: Engine shuts off or will not keep running
Wrench or ETC warning lamp, often without MIL

P2106.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited Power
P2106.description: P2106 tells you the throttle control is running in a reduced-power fallback. Ford's 2012 summary lists the reasons on second-generation ETC: loss of the MAF signal, one throttle position sensor, crank position or transmission speed sensors, a stuck throttle or a throttle motor circuit fault; it sets with MIL and wrench lamp, and a crank sensor code (P0320/P0322) also adds P2106. VW's 2014 data book uses it when an internal plausibility check of the engine computer fails. So P2106 almost always appears with another code that names the real defect, and that one is repaired first. The driver notices weak acceleration and a capped top speed. Forced idle is P2104, limited rpm P2110, shutdown P2105.

causes.label: Failed input such as MAF, throttle position or crank sensor
Sticking throttle or fault in the throttle motor circuit
Failed internal check or software in the engine computer

P2107.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Module Processor
P2107.description: P2107 concerns the processor that runs throttle A control, which in most cars sits inside the engine computer rather than in a separate box. Ford's summaries define it as an internal processor fault or lost communication with the main CPU, detected within 60 ms, with MIL after two drive cycles and the ETC lamp at once; from 2024 Ford reports the same check as P2108 with a failure-type byte. Ford names P2107 with P2111/P2112 as the codes that catch a throttle unable to hold cold-start idle. FCA lists it in a 2022 PCM software update for the Jeep Gladiator 3.6L. Check supply, grounds and software before blaming the module. The B counterpart is P211E; module performance is P2108.

causes.label: ECU software fault fixed by a reflash
Voltage dips or poor ECU ground
Internal hardware failure of the engine computer

symptoms: Engine and ETC warning lamps on

P2108.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Module Performance
P2108.description: P2108 marks a performance problem of the control function for throttle A, as opposed to a pure processor fault (P2107). VW's 2014 Touareg data book gives a concrete case: the time for the throttle to close below a reference point of 11.56 percent must not exceed 0.60 s. Ford's 2024-2025 summary uses P2108 as the base code for its throttle processor test, so P2107 there appears as P2108 with failure-type byte 49 (60 ms, MIL). Usage therefore differs by maker. Check the throttle body for deposits and the ECU for software updates, then supply and grounds. Symptoms range from a warning lamp to reduced power. The B counterpart is P211F; mechanical return problems also show up as P2119.

causes.label: Throttle closes too slowly (deposits, weak spring)
ECU software issue needing an update
Supply voltage or ground problem at the ECU

symptoms: Unstable idle after lifting off the pedal

P2109.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2109.description: P2109 flags an implausible rest reading on position signal A: with the throttle or pedal resting on its lower mechanical stop, the minimum learned at key-on falls outside the window the calibration accepts. Ford names its first throttle body sensor TP A, so on such layouts the code concerns the throttle. Subaru documents P2109: bulletin 09-102-23 traces it on the 2022 WRX to a throttle plate that has frozen shut and supplies new ECM software, and 09-97-22 adds improved detection logic for 2020-2022 Legacy and Outback. A Delphi patent describes several learn attempts before an obstruction is reported. Circuit faults on A have their own codes (P0120-P0123); P2113-P2117 run the same check for letters B to F. Expect a warning lamp and possibly limp mode.

causes.label: Ice or carbon holding the throttle plate off its rest stop
ECM software with oversensitive detection (update available)
Rest position not relearned after cleaning or replacing the throttle body
Sensor A worn or drifted at the closed end of its track

symptoms: Engine warning lamp, often after a cold or wet night
Reduced power until the fault clears

P210A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
P210A.description: Throttle actuator B only exists on engines with two electronic throttles, typically one per cylinder bank. P210A reports an electrical fault, mainly an open line, in the drive of that second motor. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 checks the bank 2 H-bridge just like bank 1: open load above 200 kOhm (0.8 s), driver overtemperature and short to ground below 0.5 Ohm, each one trip. Ducati links P210A to the rear-bank throttle motor of its V4 and points to moisture in the ECU connector. Ford's 2024 summary uses P210A as base code for all faults of its second throttle body. The engine runs on reduced power. Bank 1 is P2100; low/high circuit faults are P210C/P210D, position errors P210B.

causes.label: Moisture or corrosion in the throttle B or ECU connector
Broken motor wire to throttle body B
Open winding in throttle motor B
Faulty bank 2 output stage in the ECU

symptoms: Reduced power, one bank breathing poorly

P210B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P210B.description: P210B is the position-control check for the second throttle on twin-throttle engines. The controller compares the commanded opening of throttle B with the measured one; GM's 23OBDG07 table flags a deviation beyond a rate-dependent limit for 0.5 s, one trip. Ford lists P210B with MIL and wrench lamp for its dual-throttle applications (2020-2023) and from 2024 shows it as P210A with byte 95, the type Ford describes as cross-wired on the A side. Mercedes-AMG M177 V8s store it as throttle actuator 2 signal above limit, together with P2101; the bulletin blames high resistance in the connector pins of both actuators. Bank 1 counterpart is P2101; an open circuit is P210A, motor current P211C.

causes.label: High resistance at throttle B connector pins
Deposits or ice making throttle B sluggish
Motor leads swapped after repair work
Worn gears or motor in throttle body B

symptoms: Engine warning lamp and reduced power
Uneven running between the two banks

P210C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
P210C.description: P210C is reserved for a low-side fault in the drive circuit of the second throttle motor, for example a grounded motor lead or an overloaded output stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Makers with two throttles report such faults differently: GM's 23OBDG07 table files a bank 2 short to ground below 0.5 Ohm and driver overtemperature under P210A, and Ford's 2024 summary hangs all throttle B faults on P210A with failure-type bytes. CARB requires circuit faults of output devices to be detected, so where P210C is used it behaves like its bank 1 sibling P2102. Expect the second throttle to be switched off, rough running and reduced power. High-side faults would be P210D, open circuit P210A.

causes.label: Throttle B motor wire shorted to ground
Shorted or jammed throttle motor B
Faulty bank 2 throttle driver in the ECU

P210D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
P210D.description: P210D covers the high-side fault of the second throttle drive: a voltage on the motor B circuit that suggests a short to battery, or a supply that stays live when the stage should be off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. On twin-throttle engines that publish their logic, GM (23OBDG07) and Ford (2024) collect the electrical faults of throttle B under P210A, so P210D will rarely be seen. The CARB rule for output components still applies: an electrical fault in an actuator that affects emissions must be detected and stored. If it appears, treat it like P2103 for bank 1: inspect wiring and connector of throttle B for chafing to a positive feed, then the motor and the ECU output. The engine runs on reduced power.

causes.label: Throttle B motor wire shorted to battery voltage
Damaged or wet connector at throttle body B
Faulty bank 2 output stage in the ECU

P210E.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
P210E.description: P210E compares two redundant position signals, C and F, and sets when their voltages stop agreeing within the permitted tolerance. Which physical tracks carry these letters is up to the manufacturer: GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 uses C for the first sensor of a second throttle body, while Ford's summaries assign D, E and F to the three tracks of its pedal, so a C/F pair only arises on unusual layouts. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The same kind of check is documented under P2138: GM's 2023 table flags the D/E pedal pair at a difference of 0.12-0.18 V, the 2014 VW Touareg at 0.14-0.26 V. A single drifting track, contact resistance or a shared ground fault is the usual cause; the ECU then trusts neither signal fully and limits power.

causes.label: One sensor track worn or drifted, so the pair no longer agrees
Corrosion or water in the connector shifting one signal
Fault in a shared ground or 5 V reference line
Faulty input stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Engine or throttle warning lamp on
Hesitant or delayed response to the pedal

P210F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P210F.description: P210F is a status code for the second throttle: the controller has capped engine speed because control of throttle B is no longer reliable. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Its bank 1 sibling P2110 is well described: in Ford's 2012 summary it follows the loss of both throttle position sensors or a fault found by the throttle plate controller, sets the MIL and wrench lamp and enforces an rpm limit with fuel and spark. P210F would play the same role on engines with two throttles; the root cause is stored as a separate code such as P210A, P210B or a throttle B sensor fault, and that is what gets repaired. CARB treats such fallback modes as malfunctions when they can raise emissions. Expect a hard rev limit.

causes.label: Electrical or mechanical fault of throttle B (see companion code)
Loss of the position signals of throttle B
ECU software reacting too strictly

symptoms: Engine will not rev past a fixed limit

P2110.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P2110.description: P2110 records that engine speed has been capped because throttle A can no longer be controlled safely. Ford's 2012 summary sets it on second-generation ETC when both throttle position sensors fail or Ford's throttle plate controller (TPPC) reports a fault, with MIL and wrench lamp; rpm is then capped by a pedal-dependent limit enforced through fuel and spark. FCA uses it widely: a Ram 1500 3.6L bulletin (09-023-23) pairs it with throttle icing (P2072, P2118), and Jeep Renegade/Fiat 500X PCM updates cure false settings. Repair the companion code first. Bank B counterpart is P210F; other fallback states are P2104-P2106.

causes.label: Ice on the throttle plate after a cold soak
Loss of both throttle position sensor signals
PCM software setting the code falsely (update available)
Worn or faulty electronic throttle body

symptoms: Engine will not rev beyond a low limit
Stop/start disabled or hard start in frost

P2111.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Stuck Open
P2111.description: P2111 means throttle A stays more open than commanded. Ford defines it precisely: the actual throttle angle exceeds the desired angle by more than 6 degrees for about 500 ms, with MIL after two drive cycles and the ETC lamp at once; it also catches a throttle that cannot bring cold-start idle down. Ford's 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries keep it with MIL, the latter as P2100 byte 72. Ford's SSM 50203 links it to moisture that freezes downstream of the throttle plate on the Ranger (2019-2021) and Bronco (2021). Carbon or a deformed plate can also hold the throttle off its seat. The opposite fault is P2112; bank B is P211A.

causes.label: Water or ice in the intake behind the throttle
Carbon build-up holding the plate open
Broken return spring or worn gear in the throttle body
PCM calibration needing an update

symptoms: High idle speed or engine hard to slow down
Loss of power in freezing weather

P2112.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Stuck Closed
P2112.description: P2112 is the mirror image of P2111: throttle A opens less than commanded. Ford sets it when the actual angle stays more than 6 degrees below the desired angle for about 500 ms (MIL after two drive cycles, ETC lamp at once) and lists it in its 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries. Ford's SSM 50203 names it for Ranger/Bronco with ice behind the throttle. Mazda uses the number differently: its bulletins for the CX-9 and Mazda3 describe P2112 as a throttle motor current fault set after cold starts below freezing, cured by draining condensate or a PCM update. Ice, thick carbon or a jammed gear are the usual causes; the engine may idle poorly or lack power.

causes.label: Frozen condensate locking the throttle plate
Heavy carbon restricting plate movement
Jammed gear or weak motor in the throttle body
PCM logic needing an update

symptoms: Lack of power after a cold start
Low or unstable idle, possible stalling

P2113.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
P2113.description: The engine computer checks whether position signal B reports a plausible value when the throttle or pedal rests against its lower mechanical stop. At key-on many systems learn this minimum and compare it with a tolerance window; a reading outside that window sets the code. Ford and GM label their second throttle position sensor as B, so on those layouts B means the throttle body, but neither maker publishes P2113 itself. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Subaru uses the A version (P2109). Ice, coking or a bent stop are typical triggers. P0220-P0223 cover the B circuit, P2109 and P2114-P2117 the other letters. The driver may see a warning lamp and reduced power.

causes.label: Carbon deposits or ice keep the throttle plate off its rest stop
Position sensor B worn or drifted at the low end of its track
Minimum position not relearned after cleaning or part replacement
Corroded connector shifting the sensor B signal

symptoms: Engine or ETC warning lamp on

P2114.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
P2114.description: This code reports that position signal C does not show a believable value while its throttle or pedal sits on the lower stop. The controller learns or expects a minimum reading within a tolerance band and flags a fault when the learned value falls outside it. Letter C is rarely assigned: Ford and GM use A/B for the throttle and D/E/F for the pedal, so C appears only on layouts with a third sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the logic follows the A version P2109 (Subaru) and the Delphi minimum-learn patent. P2113 and P2115-P2117 are the same test for other letters, P2136/P2137 compare C against A or B. Expect a warning lamp and possibly limited power.

causes.label: Position sensor C worn or drifted near its rest position
Deposits, ice or a damaged stop prevent the rest position
Rest position not relearned after repair
Connector or wiring fault shifting the C signal

symptoms: Engine or ETC warning lamp on

P2115.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor D Minimum Stop Performance
P2115.description: Here the controller judges position signal D at the released (minimum) end of travel. On Ford and GM drive-by-wire systems D is the first accelerator pedal sensor, so the code means the pedal's idle reading is outside the expected window, for example because the pedal does not return fully or its sensor track has shifted. No manufacturer documents P2115 publicly; Ford and GM publish only circuit and correlation codes for D (P2120-P2123, P2138). P2116 and P2117 are the E and F counterparts, P2109 and P2113 refer to A and B. The engine may not return to idle cleanly, and the ECU may limit pedal response.

causes.label: Pedal blocked by floor mat or weak return spring
Worn pedal sensor track D at the idle end
Aftermarket pedal tuning module or wrong pedal part
Corroded or loose pedal connector

symptoms: Engine does not drop to normal idle when the pedal is released

P2116.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor E Minimum Stop Performance
P2116.description: The code covers the rest-position check of signal E. Ford, GM and Mitsubishi assign E to the second accelerator pedal sensor, which on many pedals runs at roughly half the voltage of sensor D (GM: APP 2 between 0.16 and 2.3 V). If the reading with the pedal released lies outside the learned or calibrated window, P2116 can be stored. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Circuit faults of the same sensor are reported separately (P2125, P2127-P2129) and disagreement between D and E as P2138; P2115 and P2117 handle D and F. Typical effects are a warning lamp, an unsteady idle and limited throttle response.

causes.label: Pedal held off its stop by floor mat or sticking pivot
Worn or contaminated sensor track E
Moisture or corrosion at the pedal connector

P2117.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor F Minimum Stop Performance
P2117.description: P2117 is the minimum-stop check for signal F. Ford lists F as the third accelerator pedal sensor on its older Gen2 throttle systems (circuit codes P2132/P2133, range P2131), while most current pedals carry only D and E, so the code can only occur on three-track pedals. The ECU flags it when the F reading at the released position lies outside the expected band. No manufacturer documents P2117 publicly. Siblings are P2115 (D) and P2116 (E); P2139 and P2140 compare F with D or E. A sticking pedal or a worn track usually lies behind it, with a warning lamp and reduced pedal response as the visible result.

causes.label: Pedal does not return fully to its stop
Worn third sensor track F
Poor contact at the pedal connector

P2118.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.description: P2118 looks at how much current throttle motor A needs. A healthy throttle moves with modest current; a high or abnormal draw means the motor is fighting resistance. Ford lists P2118 with MIL and wrench lamp in its 2020-2023 summary (2024: P2100 byte 1D). The best-known trigger is a frozen throttle plate: Kia's 2022-2023 Carnival 3.5L bulletin describes limp-home mode after a cold soak and a revised ECM logic, Ram 1500 3.6L trucks get a de-icing kit (P2072, P2110, P2118), and Hyundai changed its hybrid ECM logic for what it calls ETC target position failure. Unlike P2101 (position error) or P2119 (spring return), this code points at the load on the motor. Bank B is P211C.

causes.label: Ice on the throttle plate after a cold soak
Carbon or sludge loading the motor
Worn throttle motor or gear train
ECM logic too sensitive (software update available)

symptoms: Limp-home mode after a cold start
No start or poor idle in frost

P2119.title: Throttle Actuator A Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P2119.description: This is a mechanical performance check of the electronic throttle body. GM calls it Throttle Closed Position Performance: after the motor is de-energized the return springs must bring the plate into its default (limp) position, e.g. 1.32-1.90 V on TP sensor 1 in GM's 2006 tables; 15 failed samples in a row set it. A Bosch-based GM ECM times the spring return at key-on (fault above 0.56 s). Toyota, Lexus, Ford (Ranger/Bronco, ice behind the throttle) and Mitsubishi use the code too. Unlike P2101 (position error while driven) or P2118 (motor current), P2119 points at a sticking or iced plate or a weak spring; the engine may enter limp mode.

causes.label: Carbon deposits make the throttle plate stick
Water or ice in the intake behind the throttle body
Weak return spring or worn gear in the throttle body
ECM software that sets the code falsely (update available)

P211A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
P211A.description: P211A means the second throttle on a twin-throttle engine stays further open than requested. Ford documents it in its 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries for applications with an ETB B, with MIL and wrench lamp and detection within 5 seconds; in 2024 it is shown as P210A with failure-type byte 72, matching P2111/P2100-72 for throttle A. For the A throttle Ford uses a 6-degree gap between desired and actual angle, and the B check is built the same way. With one bank getting extra air, idle rises and the engine runs unevenly; the controller usually limits power. Look for ice, carbon or a broken return spring at throttle body B. Bank 1 counterpart is P2111, stuck closed P211B.

causes.label: Ice or carbon holding throttle B open
Broken return spring or gear in throttle body B
Faulty throttle motor B or its position sensor

P211B.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
P211B.description: P211B is set when throttle B on a twin-throttle engine opens less than the controller asks for. Ford lists it for its dual-throttle applications in the 2020-2023 summary and in 2024 as P210A with failure-type byte 73, each with MIL, wrench lamp and detection in under 5 seconds; the A-side logic it mirrors is P2112, where actual angle trailing the target by more than 6 degrees counts as a fault. One bank is then starved of air: the engine feels weak, may stumble at idle and often drops into limp mode. Ice after a frosty night, heavy carbon or a jammed gear train in throttle body B are the usual suspects. The opposite direction is P211A, position control errors P210B.

causes.label: Frozen condensate locking throttle B
Heavy carbon restricting throttle B
Jammed gear or weak motor in throttle body B

P211C.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P211C.description: P211C evaluates the current drawn by the second throttle motor. If throttle B needs clearly more current than expected to reach or hold its position, something is loading it mechanically or the motor itself is degrading. Ford names P211C first in its list for the second throttle body of twin-throttle engines (2020-2023) and in 2024 as P210A byte 1D, each with MIL, wrench lamp and detection within 5 seconds. The bank 1 version P2118 is known mostly from frozen throttle plates after cold soaks, as Kia and Ram bulletins show, so the same check applies to throttle B. Unlike P210B (position error) or P211D (spring and body check), the trigger here is motor load. The car usually goes into reduced power.

causes.label: Ice or condensate binding throttle B
Carbon build-up increasing motor load
Worn motor or gears in throttle body B

P211D.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P211D.description: P211D is the mechanical check of throttle body B, the twin of P2119. GM's 23OBDG07 table describes four spring tests for bank 2: the opening and closing springs must bring the de-energized plate back to the defined limp position within set times (about 0.2-0.36 s per path), checked during offset learning and also at cold temperatures, each failing in one trip. Ford lists P211D with MIL and wrench lamp for its second throttle (2020-2023; 2024 as P210A byte 92). A sticking plate, a weak spring or ice keep the throttle from returning, so the safe fallback position cannot be guaranteed and power is limited. Position errors in operation are P210B, motor current P211C, stuck positions P211A/P211B.

causes.label: Weak or broken return spring in throttle body B
Deposits or ice slowing the plate
Throttle adaptation not completed after service

P211E.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
P211E.description: P211E is the processor fault for the control of throttle B on engines with two electronic throttles. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The A version P2107 is well described: Ford treats it as an internal processor fault or lost link to the main CPU, detected in 60 ms, with MIL and an ETC lamp, and from 2024 reports it under P2108. Twin-throttle systems published by GM and Ford drive both throttles from the one engine computer and do not show a separate P211E. CARB requires on-board computers and their outputs to be monitored. If it appears, check ECU supply, grounds and software level before replacing hardware. Expect limp mode. Module performance for B is P211F.

causes.label: Control unit software fault (reflash)
Voltage dips or poor ground at the control unit
Internal hardware failure of the control unit

symptoms: Engine and ETC warning lamps on

P211F.title: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
P211F.description: P211F covers a performance fault of the control function for throttle B, as distinct from a processor fault (P211E). No manufacturer documents this code publicly. For the A side, VW's 2014 data book gives a measurable example under P2108: the throttle must close below a reference point of 11.56 percent within 0.60 s. Ford uses P2108 from 2024 as base code for its processor test, which shows how differently makers fill this slot. On a twin-throttle engine P211F would apply the same kind of check to the second throttle. CARB requires such control functions to be monitored when they affect emissions. Check throttle body B for deposits and the ECU for updates; reduced power is likely.

causes.label: Throttle B responds or closes too slowly
Control unit software needing an update
Supply or ground problem at the control unit

P2120.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit
P2120.description: P2120 is the general circuit check for signal D, which GM, Ford and VW all use for the first accelerator pedal track. GM's 2007 tables call it APP Sensor 1 Circuit: the ECM watches sensor 1 for steady or intermittent opens and shorts within its 0.325-4.75 V window and counts failures every 12.5 ms, setting the code at 19 of 39 counts. GM PIP3783D lists P2120 among the pedal codes on 2007-2014 full-size trucks and SUVs and blames weak pin grip in the inline connectors C109 and C205. Ford's 2024 summary uses P2120 as the base code whose failure types 16 and 17 replace P2122 and P2123. Range/Performance is P2121, low and high voltage P2122/P2123, dropouts P2124. With one track lost, the ECU cuts power.

causes.label: Poor terminal tension or corrosion at pedal, inline or ECM connectors
Open or short in the sensor 1 signal, reference or ground wire
Internal fault in the pedal sensor, such as a cracked solder joint
ECM input fault

symptoms: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Fault often intermittent and hard to reproduce

P2121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance
P2121.description: P2121 means pedal signal D is electrically intact but implausible. Ford's 2012 OBD summary sets it only on second-generation ETC systems, whose pedals carry three tracks D, E and F: if sensor D disagrees with the others by more than 1.1 degrees, the PCM stores P2121 without MIL but with the wrench lamp, and pedal response becomes rate-limited using the healthy tracks. Mitsubishi lists P2121 for the accelerator pedal sensor on the 2022 Outlander as a one-trip code that turns the MIL on. Newer Ford and GM systems with two tracks report such disagreement as P2138 instead. Circuit faults on D are P2120 and P2122-P2124; P2126 is the same check for track E. The car stays drivable but reacts softly to the pedal.

causes.label: Worn or dirty track D giving an offset reading
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Shared reference or ground line shifting one signal

symptoms: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Idle may rise when the brake is not pressed

P2122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
P2122.description: P2122 sets when pedal track D falls below its lower voltage limit, typically from a short to ground, a missing 5 V reference or a broken signal wire. Limits differ by maker: Ford uses 0.25 V and since 2020 lights both MIL and wrench lamp (in 2012 only the wrench lamp); GM's 2007 tables use 0.325 V with 19 of 39 counts at 12.5 ms (Type A), GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 0.28 V for 0.2 s; the 2014 VW Passat flags anything under 0.61 V. GM bulletin 14636 extended coverage on 2009-2011 Impala and 2009 LaCrosse pedals with broken solder joints that set this and related codes. P2123 is the high counterpart, P2120 the general circuit code, P2127 the low fault on track E. The ECU limits power and pedal response.

causes.label: Track D signal wire shorted to ground or chafed
Open or shorted 5 V reference feed to the pedal
Pedal sensor fault such as a cracked solder joint
Corroded terminals with high resistance

symptoms: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Pedal feels dead or reacts only slowly

P2123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit High
P2123.description: P2123 is the high-voltage fault on pedal track D, usually an open sensor ground or a short to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage. GM's 2007 tables set it above 4.75 V (19 of 39 counts, Type A), a Bosch-based GM ECM from 2012 above 4.824 V lasting 0.2 s, and the 2014 VW Touareg above 4.89 V; Ford uses 4.75 V. A track pinned near the supply rail would read like a fully pressed pedal, so the controller rejects it, carries on with track E and caps engine output. GM PIP3783D lists the code among the very intermittent pedal faults on 2007-2014 full-size trucks and advises wiggling the harness and testing terminal tension. P2122 is the low counterpart, P2120 the general circuit code, P2128 the high fault on track E.

causes.label: Open or high-resistance ground return of the pedal sensor
Track D signal shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage
Internal pedal sensor fault
Loose or spread terminals at pedal or inline connector

symptoms: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Limited throttle opening despite full pedal
Fault may appear and vanish with harness movement

P2124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Intermittent
P2124.description: P2124 covers brief dropouts or spikes on pedal track D that come and go too quickly to count as a steady low or high fault. Ford documents it: special service messages 46829 (2015-2017 F-150) and 46880 (2017 Super Duty built up to late August 2017) tie P2124, alongside other pedal codes and wrench, ABS, airbag and hill descent lamps, to a pedal harness routed behind the bracket between brake booster and brake pedal, where it gets pinched and damaged. GM publishes no separate intermittent code for track D and catches such glitches through the 19-of-39 counter of P2120, P2122 and P2123. Inspect the harness while moving the pedal slowly. Effects range from a passing warning lamp to sudden loss of pedal response.

causes.label: Pedal harness pinched or chafed by a misrouted path
Loose terminal or weak pin tension at the pedal connector
Worn spot on track D inside the pedal sensor

symptoms: Warning lamps that come and go, sometimes several at once
Brief loss of pedal response while driving
Reduced power mode after repeated dropouts

P2125.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit
P2125.description: P2125 reports a general electrical fault in signal circuit E. GM uses it as Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor 2 Circuit: the ECM looks for a continuous or intermittent open or short in the sensor 2 circuit with a counter at 12.5 ms per count (19 of 39 counts). In GM's 2006 tables sensor 2 is valid between about 0.16 and 2.3 V. GM bulletin 14636 lists P2125 among the pedal codes caused by a broken solder joint inside the pedal (2009-2011 Impala, LaCrosse). Range/Performance is P2126, explicit low or high voltage P2127/P2128, dropouts P2129, and the D/E comparison P2138. With one pedal track lost the ECU usually limits engine power.

causes.label: Internal fault in the pedal sensor (e.g. cracked solder joint)
Open or short in the sensor 2 wiring or 5 V reference
Loose or corroded pedal or inline connector
ECM input fault

symptoms: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Traction control may be switched off

P2126.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
P2126.description: Signal E is electrically intact but its value does not fit the situation. Ford's 2012 OBD summary uses P2126 for the second pedal sensor on Gen2 throttle systems: it sets when sensors D and E disagree by more than 1.1 degrees, as a non-MIL fault with the wrench lamp. Mitsubishi lists P2126 as accelerator pedal sensor E on the 2022 Outlander. Many newer systems report the same disagreement as P2138 instead. P2125 is the general circuit fault, P2127/P2128 are voltage below or above limits, P2129 covers dropouts. The vehicle usually stays drivable with softened pedal response; on Ford the MIL stays off and only the wrench lamp lights.

causes.label: Worn or dirty sensor track E giving offset readings
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Shared reference or ground circuit shifting one signal

symptoms: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Idle may be raised when braking

P2127.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P2127.description: P2127 reports that pedal track E reads below its lower limit. Because many pedals run the second track at roughly half the voltage of the first, the limit for E can sit lower than for D: GM's 2006 tables flag sensor 2 under 0.1625 V and the 2014 VW Passat under 0.27 V, against 0.61 V for track D. Full-scale designs use similar limits on both tracks: Ford 0.25 V, GM's 2023 table 0.28 V for 0.2 s, GM's Bosch-based 2012 ECM 0.625 V. Typical causes are a short to ground on the E signal wire, an open reference feed, or a worn spot at the closed end of the track. With E gone the ECU relies on track D alone and holds back torque. P2128 is the high fault on E, P2122 the low fault on D, P2125 the general E circuit code.

causes.label: Track E signal wire shorted to ground
Open 5 V reference feed for the second track
Worn track E at the closed-pedal end
Corroded or loose pedal connector

symptoms: Engine warning lamp, on newer Fords together with the wrench lamp
Reduced power and slower pedal response
Traction control may be switched off

P2128.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P2128.description: P2128 sets when pedal track E reads above its upper limit, typically from an open sensor ground, a short to 5 V or a broken track. Where E is a half-scale signal the limit lies far below the supply: GM's 2006 tables flag sensor 2 above 2.295 V and the 2014 VW Passat above 2.43 V. Pedals with two full-scale tracks use about 4.75 V (Ford, GM 2007, 19 of 39 counts) or 4.824 V for 0.2 s (GM's Bosch-based 2012 ECM). Since both tracks often share one ground, an open ground can set P2128 together with P2123. With E rejected the ECU steers on track D only and limits output; Ford's 2020-2023 summary lights MIL and wrench lamp. P2127 is the low fault on E, P2123 the high fault on D, P2138 the D/E comparison.

causes.label: Open or high-resistance ground of the pedal sensor
Track E signal shorted to the 5 V reference
Broken track or solder joint inside the pedal sensor

symptoms: Engine warning lamp and reduced power message
Weak acceleration even with the pedal fully pressed
Often stored together with P2123 if the ground is open

P2129.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
P2129.description: P2129 is meant for short dropouts or spikes in signal circuit E that do not last long enough for a steady low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM and Ford, which assign E to the second pedal sensor, catch such glitches inside their circuit codes instead: GM counts failures every 12.5 ms and flags the APP sensor 2 circuit after 19 of 39 counts (P2125/P2127/P2128), Ford uses 0.25/4.75 V limits. CARB requires circuit monitoring of input sensors; the code fits that duty. Check for loose pins and harness chafing with the pedal moved slowly. Effects range from a warning lamp to brief power cuts while driving.

causes.label: Loose terminal or poor pin tension at the pedal connector
Chafed harness making intermittent contact
Worn spot or cracked joint inside the pedal sensor

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief hesitation or power loss while driving
Reduced power mode after repeated dropouts

P212A.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit
P212A.description: P212A is the general circuit code for throttle position signal G, a letter that only comes into play on engines with more than one electronic throttle or extra position tracks. No manufacturer documents P212A publicly. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 assigns G to the second position sensor of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine, but reports its electrical faults through the separate codes P212C (below 0.195 V) and P212D (above 4.805 V), each after 0.14 s in one trip. CARB requires input components like this to be checked for circuit faults, and P212A is the catch-all slot for that duty. Check the connector, wiring and 5 V supply at the second throttle body. P212B covers plausibility, P212C-P212E low, high and intermittent faults.

causes.label: Open or short in the sensor G signal, supply or ground wire
Corroded or loose connector at the throttle body
Failed position sensor inside the throttle body

P212B.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P212B.description: P212B means throttle signal G is electrically valid but its value does not fit. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 applies it to sensor 2 of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine: the code sets when the angle derived from sensor 2 differs from that of sensor 1 by more than about 5-6.25 %, or from the angle modelled from manifold pressure by more than 9 %, in one trip; the 2024 table repeats the check. Nissan uses P212B on the 2021-2023 Rogue with the 1.5 L KR15DDT engine; bulletin NTB23-021 cures a lit MIL without drivability complaints by ECM reprogramming. Circuit faults are P212A and P212C-P212E. Depending on the cause the engine may run normally or limit power.

causes.label: ECM software setting the code without a real fault (update available)
Sensor G drifted or worn, disagreeing with its partner sensor
Deposits or sticking plate making the angle disagree with airflow
Contact resistance at the throttle body connector

symptoms: MIL on, often without noticeable driving problems
Reduced power if the plausibility fault persists

P212C.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Low
P212C.description: P212C sets when position signal G reads below its lower electrical limit. The letter G only comes into play on engines with more than one electronic throttle. GM's 2023 and 2024 OBD tables (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07) give it to the second position sensor in the bank 2 throttle body of a twin-throttle engine: a raw voltage under 0.195 V lasting 0.14 s while the ECU is running stores the code within one trip. Usual culprits are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost 5 V feed to that throttle body or a damaged sensor track. P212D is the matching high fault, P212A the general circuit code, P212B the plausibility check of G. Once a bank 2 signal is lost, the ECU typically restricts power.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor G shorted to ground
5 V reference to the bank 2 throttle body open or pulled low
Worn or damaged track of position sensor G inside the throttle body
Corroded or loose terminals at the bank 2 throttle connector

symptoms: Uneven idle or hesitation on one bank

P212D.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit High
P212D.description: P212D is the high-voltage fault on throttle position signal G. GM documents it in the 2023 and 2024 tables (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07) for sensor 2 of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine: once the raw voltage climbs above 4.805 V for 0.14 s, the code is stored in a single trip. A reading that close to the supply rail usually points to an open sensor ground, an interrupted signal line that the input pulls up, or a short to the 5 V reference or battery voltage. Because both sensors of one throttle often share their ground, P212D can appear alongside a high fault on the first sensor of that throttle. P212C is the low counterpart, P212A the general circuit code. Expect a warning lamp and reduced power.

causes.label: Open sensor ground at the bank 2 throttle body
Signal wire of sensor G shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Broken signal wire or pushed-back terminal
Internal fault in the position sensor of the bank 2 throttle

symptoms: Weak or delayed response to the accelerator

P212E.title: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
P212E.description: P212E is reserved for brief dropouts or spikes on throttle position signal G, the kind that clear again before a steady low or high fault can be confirmed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, which assigns G to sensor 2 of the bank 2 throttle body on a twin-throttle engine, reacts to such glitches with its range checks instead: P212C below 0.195 V and P212D above 4.805 V each need only 0.14 s. CARB requires input sensors to be monitored for circuit faults, which is the duty this slot covers. In practice the trigger is a loose terminal, a chafed wire near the engine or moisture in the connector. Check the harness while flexing it with the engine running. The fault may vanish between workshop visits.

causes.label: Loose or worn terminal at the bank 2 throttle connector
Harness chafed by engine movement, breaking contact now and then
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Momentary contact loss on the sensor track

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Fault often not present at the workshop

P212F.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F/G Voltage Correlation
P212F.description: P212F checks whether the two redundant signals F and G still agree in voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the letters make it an unusual pair: GM's 2004-2005 truck tables use F for the third accelerator pedal track, while GM's 2023 table assigns G to the second sensor of a bank 2 throttle body. A meaningful F/G comparison therefore needs a layout where both letters sit on the same component, for example a second throttle body with two tracks. Comparable checks are documented under P2135 and P2138, where GM and Ford store a fault when two tracks differ by a few percent or degrees. A drifting track, contact resistance or a shared ground fault are the plausible causes; the ECU then limits power.

causes.label: One sensor track worn or drifted so the pair disagrees
Contact resistance in the connector shifting one signal
Fault in a shared ground or 5 V reference line

symptoms: Engine or throttle warning lamp on

P2130.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P2130.description: P2130 is the general circuit code for signal F. GM used it on its 2004-2005 pickups and SUVs with a separate throttle actuator control module (TACM) and a pedal carrying three tracks, where F is APP sensor 3. The TACM flags a continuous or intermittent open or short when sensor 3 reads below 1.63 V or above 4.38 V, or when its learned rest voltage exceeds 4.28 V; each error adds 4 to a counter checked every 3 ms, passes subtract 1, and the code sets at 106. GM's 2004 tables rate it Type C, the 2005 tables Type A with immediate MIL. Ford's three-track pedals split the same duty into P2132 and P2133. Plausibility is P2131, dropouts P2134. With one track lost the other two still steer the engine, usually with reduced response.

causes.label: Poor terminal contact or corrosion at the pedal connector
Open or short in the signal, reference or ground wire of track F
Third track inside the pedal sensor worn or failed
Faulty input in the throttle actuator control module or ECM

symptoms: Softer or delayed response to the pedal
Reduced power message on some models

P2131.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
P2131.description: P2131 means pedal track F is electrically intact but disagrees with the rest of the pedal. Two makers document it for three-track pedals. GM's 2004-2005 truck tables scale APP sensor 3 to the range of the other tracks and set P2131 only when it strays more than 0.26 V from each of the other two sensors, so the majority vote singles out track F; the counter runs every 3 ms and trips at 167 (Type C in 2004, Type A in 2005). Ford's 2012 summary sets it on second-generation ETC when F departs from the others by over 1.1 degrees, lighting the wrench lamp without MIL. Circuit faults on F are P2130 and P2132-P2134. The car stays drivable; the ECU follows the two healthy tracks and softens pedal response.

causes.label: Worn or dirty track F giving an offset reading
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Bent pedal bracket or binding mechanism distorting one track

symptoms: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Often no noticeable change while driving

P2132.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Low
P2132.description: P2132 sets when signal F drops below its lower voltage limit. Ford uses it for the third accelerator pedal track of its second-generation electronic throttle: its 2012 OBD summary treats anything under 0.25 V as a continuity fault and lights only the wrench lamp, not the MIL. FCA's emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter lists P2132 among the codes that may appear after the engine control unit is reprogrammed. GM's TACM trucks of 2004-2005 fold low readings of sensor 3 into the general code P2130. Likely causes are a short to ground on the F signal, an open 5 V feed or wear at the closed end of the track. P2133 is the high fault on F, P2122 and P2127 the low faults on tracks D and E.

causes.label: Signal wire of track F shorted to ground
Open or weak 5 V reference to the pedal sensor
Track F worn at the rest position

symptoms: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
Idle may stay raised until the brake is pressed

P2133.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit High
P2133.description: P2133 is the high-voltage fault on signal F. In Ford's second-generation electronic throttle the third pedal track counts as failed once it rises above 4.75 V; the 2012 summary reports it with the wrench lamp and without MIL. FCA lists P2133 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter among the codes that can show up after the engine computer is reflashed. GM's 2004-2005 trucks with a TACM catch excessive readings of sensor 3 above 4.38 V under the general code P2130. A track pinned near the supply would mimic a pressed pedal, so the controller drops it and works with the remaining two. Typical causes are an open sensor ground or a short to 5 V. P2132 is the low counterpart, P2123 and P2128 the high faults on D and E.

causes.label: Open ground line of the pedal sensor
Signal wire of track F shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Internal break in track F of the pedal sensor

symptoms: Wrench or engine warning lamp on
May appear together with high faults on other tracks if the ground is open

P2134.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F Circuit Intermittent
P2134.description: P2134 targets short interruptions on signal F that are too brief or too irregular for a confirmed low or high fault. No manufacturer publishes a detection rule for it. FCA does name P2134 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter, among the codes that may appear once the engine control unit carries the new software. GM's 2004-2005 trucks with three-track pedals handle such glitches inside P2130, whose counter adds 4 for each faulty sample every 3 ms and removes 1 for each good one until it reaches 106. Ford reports problems on F only as P2131-P2133. Look for loose pins and chafing near the pedal while moving it slowly. Effects range from a passing warning lamp to brief hesitation.

causes.label: Loose or spread terminal at the pedal connector
Pedal harness pinched or chafed near the footwell bracket
Worn spot on track F causing momentary contact loss

symptoms: Warning lamp that appears and clears
Short hesitation when moving the pedal

P2135.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/B Voltage Correlation
P2135.description: P2135 compares the two position tracks of the electronic throttle, A and B, and sets when they no longer describe the same plate angle. GM's 2006-2007 tables allow a 7 % offset at closed throttle rising to 10 % at full opening and count failures every 12.5 ms until 19 of 39 have failed. Ford flags more than 7 degrees of disagreement; its 2012 and 2020-2023 summaries show only the wrench lamp, the 2024 summary also the MIL. Mitsubishi lists P2135 for the 2022 Outlander as a one-trip MIL code. Nissan bulletin NTB21-080 cures P2135 on the 2020-2021 Frontier without driveability complaints by ECM reprogramming. Mercedes traced it on AMG M177 V8s to high resistance in the throttle actuator pins. The ECU then limits throttle opening.

causes.label: Worn or contaminated position tracks in the throttle body
Raised contact resistance or corrosion at the throttle connector
ECM calibration prone to false detection (update available on some models)
Fault on the shared 5 V reference or ground of both tracks

symptoms: Engine warning lamp or wrench lamp on
Reduced engine power, limited throttle opening

P2136.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/C Voltage Correlation
P2136.description: P2136 reports that position signals A and C disagree. On engines with two electronic throttles, C typically belongs to the second throttle body: GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 assigns C to sensor 1 of the bank 2 throttle. Mercedes-Benz documents P2136 for its M177 twin-turbo V8 in AMG C63, GLC63, SL63 and related models: bulletin LI07.10-P-080384 lists it with P2135, the A/G and B/G checks and actuator faults, traces the set to increased electrical resistance in the connector pins of both throttle actuators, and replaces the connector sockets with coated terminals. FCA also lists the code in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter. Expect a warning lamp and possibly reduced power.

causes.label: Increased resistance in the throttle actuator connector pins
Position sensor in one throttle body drifted or worn
Carbon or ice making one throttle lag behind the other

P2137.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B/C Voltage Correlation
P2137.description: P2137 compares position signals B and C and sets when their voltages drift apart beyond the calibrated tolerance. No manufacturer publishes a detection rule for this pair; FCA merely lists P2137 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter among the codes that may surface after the ECU is reprogrammed. Where the letters are known, B is the second track of the main throttle and C a sensor on a second throttle body (GM 23OBDG07). The neighbouring pair A/C is documented by Mercedes on the M177 V8, where corroded or high-resistance actuator pins set it, which is the most likely pattern here too. Unlike P2135, which stays within one throttle, this check spans two components. Expect a warning lamp and possibly reduced power.

causes.label: High resistance or corrosion at a throttle connector
Track B or sensor C drifted or worn
Fault on a shared 5 V reference or ground

P2138.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/E Voltage Correlation
P2138.description: P2138 is the standard plausibility check of a two-track accelerator pedal: D and E are pedal sensors 1 and 2 at GM, Ford and VW. GM's 2007 tables set it when the tracks differ by more than 10 % or their learned rest values by over 5 % (Type A); the 2023 table uses 0.12-0.18 V for 0.25 s in one trip. Ford flags more than 0.9 degrees and since 2020 lights MIL and wrench lamp; the 2014 VW Passat allows 0.17-0.70 V. GM bulletin 07-06-04-019F blames water entering the instrument panel to body harness connector, and special coverage N182188250 covers a pedal sensor connection on the Malibu (2016-2018), LaCrosse (2017-2018) and Regal (2018). Single-track faults have their own codes (P2122-P2128). The ECU reduces power.

causes.label: Water or corrosion in a pedal or inline harness connector
Worn pedal sensor with one track drifting
Poorly crimped or loose terminals raising resistance
Aftermarket equipment tapped into pedal or 5 V reference circuits

symptoms: Engine warning lamp with reduced engine power message
Traction or stability control may be switched off on some models

P2139.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/F Voltage Correlation
P2139.description: P2139 compares signals D and F, in practice the first and third tracks of a three-track accelerator pedal. No manufacturer publishes a detection rule for this exact code; FCA only lists P2139 in emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter among codes that can appear after the ECU update. Makers with three-track pedals handle the comparison differently: GM's 2004-2005 trucks scale sensor 3 and test it against sensors 1 and 2 at 0.26 V, then blame the odd track through P2131 or P2126 instead of naming a pair, and Ford reports a deviating track F as P2131. A pair code like P2139 cannot say which of the two tracks is wrong, so check both with a scope while moving the pedal. Effects are a warning lamp and softened acceleration.

causes.label: Track D or F of the pedal sensor worn or drifted
Contact resistance at the pedal connector
Fault on a shared ground or 5 V reference

symptoms: Engine or wrench warning lamp on

P213A.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B/Open
P213A.description: P213A concerns the electrical drive of EGR throttle B, a second motor-driven regulating flap found on some diesel layouts. Such a flap closes partly so that pressure ahead of the intake falls below exhaust pressure and enough exhaust gas can be recirculated; it also cuts air at engine stop. The engine module watches the output stage of flap B and stores P213A when the circuit is open or the driver flags a fault it cannot assign to low or high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so thresholds are unknown; CARB treats the flap as an output component whose circuit must be monitored. Flap A reports the same fault as P0487. Expect the flap to rest in its spring position, reduced EGR and possibly a power limit.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or broken connector or wire at throttle B
Open winding in the throttle B actuator motor
Harness damaged by heat near the exhaust or EGR cooler
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P213B.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P213B.description: P213B is the functional check of EGR throttle B rather than an electrical one. The module compares the position it commands with the position the flap actually reaches, or judges whether the feedback is plausible; if the gap persists beyond a set time, P213B is logged. Regulating flaps sit in a stream of recirculated exhaust and crankcase vapour, so soot and oil deposits that make the blade stiff are the usual reason, followed by worn gears or a weak motor. No manufacturer documents P213B publicly; CARB requires output components to be checked for proper function, and EGR control to be monitored for reaching its limits. The same check for flap A is P0488; pure wiring faults on B appear as P213A, P213C or P213D. The driver notices hesitation, smoke or a power limit.

causes.label: Flap stiff or stuck from soot and oil deposits
Worn gear train or weak actuator motor
Implausible position feedback from the flap sensor
Outdated engine software or missing flap adaptation

symptoms: Hesitation, black smoke or reduced power
Clicking or humming from the flap

P213C.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B Low
P213C.description: P213C points to a low signal in the drive circuit of EGR throttle B: the output stage sees too little voltage where it expects supply potential, which almost always means a conductor of the flap motor is touching ground. Chafed harness sections near the exhaust, water in the connector or a motor winding shorted to its housing are typical. Depending on the bridge design the module either switches the output off or the motor stays partly energised. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so no threshold or debounce time can be given; CARB demands separate detection of circuit faults on output components. For throttle A the matching short-circuit code is P2141. An open circuit on B is P213A, a function fault P213B. The flap usually falls back to its rest position and EGR is limited.

causes.label: Chafed wire shorting to ground between module and flap
Water or corrosion in the flap connector
Actuator motor winding shorted to housing
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P213D.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit B High
P213D.description: P213D is the opposite electrical fault to P213C on EGR throttle B: the drive line carries voltage where the output stage expects ground, or the driver measures excessive current. A wire touching battery positive, a shorted motor winding that pulls too much current, or a mechanically blocked flap that overloads the motor are the usual triggers. The output stage switches off to protect itself, so the flap returns to its spring position and stops regulating. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P213D; CARB requires output circuits to be checked for faults in both directions. Throttle A reports the same high condition as P2142, while P213A covers an open circuit and P213B a flap that moves but misses its target. Drivers notice the warning lamp, sometimes reduced power.

causes.label: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Shorted turns in the actuator motor causing overcurrent
Flap mechanically blocked, motor overloaded
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Reduced power in some operating ranges

P213E.title: Fuel Injection System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213E.description: P213E records that the engine module stopped the engine on purpose because of a fault on the injection side – rail, high-pressure lines, pressure control or injectors. Continuing to run with an external leak, a rail pressure that can no longer be controlled or an injector that keeps delivering could cause a fire or engine damage. No manufacturer documents P213E publicly. The same reaction is documented on Saab's 9-5 V6 diesel under the older P0148: when the leak calculation exceeds 90 mm³ per crankshaft revolution the module stops the engine and the test only runs again in the next drive cycle. A code naming the root cause usually sits next to P213E; P213F is the counterpart for the fuel pump side. The car stalls or will not restart and should be checked before further use.

causes.label: External leak at rail, high-pressure line or injector seal
Injector stuck open or leaking heavily
Rail pressure control valve or sensor no longer controlling pressure
Engine software misjudging the fault, update available

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start again
Fuel smell or visible fuel leak
Check engine lamp with further fuel system codes

P213F.title: Fuel Pump System Fault - Forced Engine Shutdown
P213F.description: P213F is the supply-side twin of P213E: the engine module shut the engine down because the fuel pump system – electric lift pump, its relay or control module, or the engine-driven high-pressure pump – no longer behaves in a way it can accept. No manufacturer documents P213F publicly, so the trigger is not known in detail. How closely pumps are watched can be seen in Ford's 2023 diesel summary: the lift pump relay circuits are checked for open and shorts within 0.2 s, and the duty-cycle feedback of the pump must stay between 78 and 82 %. A deliberate shutdown goes further than those circuit codes and is normally stored together with them. Injection-side faults are logged as P213E instead. The engine stops or will not restart; towing is usually needed.

causes.label: Electric lift pump or its control module failed
Pump relay, fuse or wiring fault
Worn or seized high-pressure pump
Clogged filter or empty tank starving the pump

symptoms: No restart or very long cranking
Check engine lamp with fuel pump codes

P2140.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E/F Voltage Correlation
P2140.description: P2140 checks the second and third pedal tracks, E and F, against each other. As with P2139, no manufacturer explains its own trigger for this code, and FCA's emissions recall T21 for the 2004-2006 Dodge Sprinter just includes it in the list of codes that may follow the ECU reflash. GM's 2004-2005 trucks show what the comparison looks like in practice: their P2126 sets when sensor 2 differs from sensor 1 by more than 0.20 V and from the rescaled sensor 3 by more than 0.26 V, so the E-to-F term is part of a vote rather than a code of its own. Because track E is often scaled differently from F, a fault on a shared reference can shift one signal more than the other. Warning lamp and reduced pedal response follow.

causes.label: Track E or F of the pedal sensor worn or drifted
Shared 5 V reference or ground fault shifting one track
Contact resistance or moisture at the pedal connector

symptoms: Engine or wrench warning lamp on

P2141.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Low
P2141.description: P2141 flags a low signal in the drive circuit of EGR throttle A, the main diesel regulating flap that lowers intake pressure so exhaust gas can flow back. A wire of the flap motor touching ground, a winding shorted to the housing or a wet connector are the common reasons. Note how J2012 spreads flap A over two ranges: open circuit and range/performance sit at P0487 and P0488, low and high at P2141 and P2142; flap B uses P213A to P213D. P0489 sounds similar but concerns the EGR valve A drive, not the throttle. No manufacturer documents P2141 publicly, so no figures can be quoted; CARB requires circuit faults on output components to be reported. The module usually disables the flap, which then rests open, and EGR is reduced.

causes.label: Chafed wire shorting to ground between module and flap
Moisture or corrosion in the flap connector
Actuator motor winding shorted to housing
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P2142.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A High
P2142.description: P2142 reports a high signal or overcurrent in the drive circuit of EGR throttle A. Either a motor lead has contact with battery voltage, or the motor draws more current than the output stage allows – from shorted turns or because carbon has jammed the blade. The driver then shuts down for protection, the flap springs back to its rest position and EGR regulation is lost. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2142; CARB obliges the system to recognise circuit faults of output components in both directions. P2141 is the low counterpart, P0487 the open circuit and P0488 the function check of the same flap; flap B reports a high circuit as P213D. If the cause is mechanical, cleaning or replacing the flap removes it, a wiring short needs a harness repair.

causes.label: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Flap jammed by carbon, motor overloaded
Shorted turns in the actuator motor
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P2143.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit/Open
P2143.description: Vacuum-operated EGR valves are often run by a pair of solenoids: one feeds vacuum to the valve diaphragm to open it, the other – the vent solenoid – lets air in to release the vacuum and close the valve. Ford's EEC engine computers had separate outputs for EGR vent and EGR control, and a Kia diesel patent maps both solenoids by duty cycle, using the vent side whenever the measured EGR value is above target. P2143 means the module found the vent solenoid circuit open or otherwise faulty. Without a working vent the valve may close slowly or stay open longer than wanted, causing rough idle; many systems simply disable EGR. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2143. Shorts are reported separately as P2144 and P2145.

causes.label: Loose connector or broken wire at the vent solenoid
Open coil in the vent solenoid
Blown fuse or missing supply voltage to the solenoid
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Rough idle or stalling after deceleration

P2144.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit Low
P2144.description: P2144 reports a low signal in the circuit that drives the EGR vent solenoid – the valve that bleeds vacuum from a vacuum-operated EGR valve so it can close. With the usual low-side switching, a control wire touching ground keeps the solenoid energised regardless of the command. Whether that leaves the EGR valve unable to open or unable to close depends on the plumbing, but in both cases the EGR rate can no longer be controlled. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list includes P2144 with the warning lamp and a continuous test, though Ford gives no threshold; no other public manufacturer document names the code. P2143 covers an open circuit and P2145 the high fault of the same solenoid. Typical results are rough running, higher NOx or a failed EGR readiness test.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the vent solenoid coil
Corrosion bridging terminals in the connector
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Emissions test failure because of EGR

P2145.title: EGR Vent Control Circuit High
P2145.description: P2145 is the high fault in the vent solenoid circuit of the EGR system: the control line shows supply voltage while the module tries to pull it to ground, or the driver detects overcurrent through a shorted coil. The output then cannot switch the solenoid on, so the vent stays in its rest state – depending on design the EGR valve either cannot be released quickly or cannot be held, and the module normally stops using EGR. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list names P2145 alongside P2144, both with the warning lamp and a continuous test; thresholds are not given and no further manufacturer document is public. For the vent concept itself see Ford's separate vent and control outputs and Kia's duty-mapped vent solenoid. Open circuit is P2143, low fault P2144.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Shorted vent solenoid coil drawing excess current
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: EGR inactive, sometimes pinging under load on petrol engines

P2146.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2146.description: Direct-injection and common-rail injectors are fed by a high-side driver in the engine module, often shared by several injectors. P2146 is the open or general fault of the first such supply. GM's 2009 Duramax diesel pairs injectors 1 and 4 in group 1 and sets P2146 when the driver sees an open, short or missing load for 6 ms, type A. VW's 2014 TSI and VR6 engines check the high-side current: below 2.6 A or above 14.9 A. GM petrol direct injection assigns the code to a single cylinder, the high-side control line of cylinder 1; in the Saab 9-5 2.0T a supply fault shared by cylinders 1 and 4 sets P2146 and P2155 together, after 1 s, type B, and the injector is shut off. GM bulletin PIP4924D links it to chafed V6 injector harnesses. Expect misfire and rough running.

causes.label: Injector harness chafed through or wire open inside insulation
Loose, wet or corroded injector connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Faulty high-side driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Misfire on one or more cylinders
Rough running and loss of power

P2147.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2147.description: P2147 means the common feed of injector group A is pulled toward ground. GM documents it in detail for its 2018 Duramax diesels: the high-side line to injectors 1 and 4 (group 1 on both the 2.8 L four and the 6.6 L V8) shows 0.5 Ω or less to ground while the driver is switched on; with the engine running and more than 11 V, 5 failures in 10 samples at 100 ms set it, type A, lamp on the first trip (2025 tables: 4 of 8). Ford's 2023 diesels report a short of group A to ground or battery found by the driver chip after about 0.2 s. On GM petrol direct injection such as the Saab 9-5 2.0T the code stands for low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 1. Both injectors of the group usually stop, so two cylinders drop out. P2148 is the opposite fault.

causes.label: Injector supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of the group shorted internally to its body
Water in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Heavy loss of power, rough running

P2148.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2148.description: P2148 flags group A's injector supply as too high. On GM's 2018 Duramax the high-side terminal of injector 1 or 4 shows 0.5 Ω or less to supply potential while the driver is off; same 5-of-10 counting at 100 ms, type A. Ford's 2023 diesels give it a different meaning: the chip that produces the boosted injector voltage inside the module reports an internal fault – a pointer to the control unit rather than the harness. GM's petrol direct injection reads it as excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 1. Bulletins show software and hardware causes: Hino's 2016 J08 trucks set P2148 and P2151 falsely until the ECU is reprogrammed (SB-15-023), and GM PIP6034 replaces the PCM on 2024–25 2.5 L LK0 models. The low fault is P2147.

causes.label: Injector supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Internal fault of the injector boost circuit in the module
Software falsely detecting the fault, reprogramming available
Injector of the group with internal short

symptoms: Misfire and rough running on the affected cylinders
Often no drivability complaint when the cause is software

P2149.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2149.description: P2149 is the open or general fault of the second shared injector supply. Group membership depends on the engine: GM's 2009 Duramax places injectors 7 and 6 in group 2 (6 ms, type A), whereas GM's 2018 tables pair injectors 2 and 5 in the V8 – so the cylinders must be looked up for each engine. VW's 2014 TSI and VR6 engines use the same current window as for group A, under 2.6 A or above about 14.7–14.9 A. GM petrol direct injection treats P2149 as the high-side control line of cylinder 2: on the 2023–24 Corvette LT6 bulletin 24-NA-106 traces it, with rail pressure codes, to water entering a wrong 12-way connector on bank 2. A Mercedes M254 bulletin lists P2149 among faults caused by fuel boiling in the low-pressure system.

causes.label: Injector harness damaged or wire open
Water entering an injector harness connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Low rail pressure from fuel vapour triggering follow-up faults

symptoms: Misfire on the cylinders of group B

P214A.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High
P214A.description: P214A reports that the exhaust entering the SCR catalyst was hotter than a calibrated ceiling while no particulate filter regeneration was active. The reading normally comes from the temperature sensor between the filter and the urea mixing section. Heat at this point is a threat to the SCR coating: Navistar's patent US20190232224 states that vanadia sublimates above roughly 550 °C, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to shield vanadium catalysts from such temperatures. No manufacturer documents P214A publicly; Ram bulletins for the 6.7L Cummins name only the sibling P214D, and Ford flags aftertreatment overheating with P200C/P200E. P214B covers the same fault during regeneration, P214C the outlet side. Typical triggers are fuel or oil in the exhaust, overfuelling or a drifting sensor.

causes.label: Unburnt fuel or engine oil reaching the exhaust (leaking injector, turbocharger seal)
SCR inlet temperature sensor reading too high or wrongly placed after repair
Overfuelling from injection or air-path faults (boost leak, EGR fault)
Engine control software with outdated temperature model

symptoms: Reduced engine power to limit exhaust temperature
Further codes for exhaust temperature or SCR efficiency

P214B.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214B.description: P214B is limited to the regeneration phase. To burn soot out of the particulate filter, the engine control adds late injections or uses a separate exhaust fuel injector, and the oxidation catalyst converts that fuel into heat. The code sets when the gas leaving this hot zone arrives at the SCR inlet above the limit allowed during regeneration. Navistar's patent US20190232224 describes exactly this conflict: repeated regenerations push vanadium SCR material towards its sublimation point near 550 °C, so the layout and temperature control must keep the SCR below it. No manufacturer documents P214B publicly. Compared with P214A, suspicion falls on regeneration control: a dripping exhaust injector, excess post-injection or soot burning too fast. The control unit usually aborts the regeneration.

causes.label: Exhaust fuel injector leaking or over-dosing during regeneration
Heavily loaded filter burning off too quickly
Excess post-injection quantity from a worn engine injector
Exhaust temperature sensor upstream of the SCR reading too high

symptoms: Check engine light on, regeneration aborted
Filter warning or rising soot load because regeneration cannot finish
