P214C.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High
P214C.description: P214C looks at the downstream end of the SCR catalyst: the temperature measured behind it rose above the permitted maximum outside regeneration. California's OBD rule lists SCR intake and outlet temperature as separate data values a diesel must report, so both points are watched on their own. An outlet reading that climbs above the inlet value hints at heat produced inside or just ahead of the brick, for instance hydrocarbons burning on the SCR or soot glowing in a combined filter-SCR unit, but a faulty outlet sensor is just as likely. The material limit is the same as on the inlet side, which 40 CFR 1036.115 and Navistar's patent US20190232224 describe for vanadium catalysts. No manufacturer documents P214C publicly. P214A is the inlet counterpart, P214D the outlet fault during regeneration.

causes.label: SCR outlet temperature sensor faulty or reading too high
Hydrocarbons passing the oxidation catalyst and burning on the SCR
Fuel or oil entering the exhaust from the engine or turbocharger

symptoms: Implausible outlet temperature compared with the inlet value in live data

P214D.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
P214D.description: P214D sets when the temperature behind the SCR catalyst exceeds its limit while the particulate filter is regenerating. It is the only code of this group with public manufacturer evidence. Ram pickups with the 6.7L Cummins use it: bulletin 18-053-14 (2014 Ram 2500/3500) reprograms the PCM partly to prevent unnecessary MIL events from P214D, and STAR case S2625000004 (2025–2026 Ram 3500 to 5500) groups it with exhaust temperature sensor codes such as P242B and P2470–P2472, asks for a check of battery voltage first and stresses identifying each sensor by name. That points to sensor faults and calibration as frequent causes, besides genuine overheating from hydrocarbons burning on the hot SCR during regeneration. P214B is the inlet counterpart.

causes.label: Exhaust temperature sensor behind the SCR faulty, confused with another sensor or affected by low battery voltage
PCM software requiring an update (Ram 6.7L bulletins)
Regeneration fuel slipping through and burning on the SCR

P214E.title: Reductant Pump A Current Too High
P214E.description: P214E means the electronics driving the DEF (AdBlue) pump motor saw more current than the pump may draw. GM documents it on Duramax diesels: in the 2018 tables the DEF control module reports a motor high-current or current-limit error, and the ECM sets the code after 20 failed of 25 samples with the battery above 11 V; the 2025 tables use a hardware protection limit of 15 A plus separate motor current limits for pumping and for heating mode, in which the pump is driven to warm frozen fluid. Both are Type A, so the MIL comes on after one trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets P214E when the pump motor controller exceeds 15 A. GM bulletin 20-NA-039 traced P214E on the 2020 Silverado/Sierra 1500 3.0L to software. A seized or iced pump stops dosing; P2C11 is the low-current counterpart.

causes.label: Pump motor seized, worn or blocked by crystallised or frozen fluid
Short in the pump motor winding or supply wiring, often after water ingress
ECM or reductant control module software (GM 20-NA-039)
Faulty driver stage in the reductant control module

symptoms: Check engine light on after one trip
DEF system warning, possibly a countdown to speed limitation
Raised NOx emissions because dosing stops

P214F.title: Reductant Heater A Current Too High
P214F.description: P214F concerns heater A of the DEF system, which Ford and GM both assign to the heater inside the tank (heater circuit 1). The code says this element consumed more current or power than intended. Ford's 2023 diesel summary performs one check per heating cycle, right after a cold start, and decides within 2.2 s when tank heater power is higher than expected. GM's 2025 Duramax tables set P214F when heater 1 current passes 15 A in 40 consecutive 100 ms samples; that is Type A and lights the MIL after one trip; the 2015 tables detected a shorted tank heater through a conductance of at least 0.62 S, Type B. A shorted element, wet connector or chafed lead is the usual reason. Without tank heating, frozen DEF thaws late or not at all, so dosing and NOx reduction start late in winter. P21DD is the low-current counterpart.

causes.label: Tank heater element internally shorted (often replaced with the tank sender unit)
Water ingress or corrosion in the heater connector
Chafed heater wiring shorted to ground
Faulty heater driver in the reductant control module

symptoms: DEF system warning in cold weather
Delayed DEF dosing after cold starts

P2150.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2150.description: P2150 reports the common feed of injector group B shorted toward ground. In GM's 2018 Duramax tables group 2 holds injectors 2 and 3 on the 2.8 L four-cylinder but injectors 2 and 5 on the 6.6 L V8; the test is the same as for group A – 0.5 Ω or less to ground with the driver on, 5 failed samples out of 10, type A with lamp on the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesels flag a short of group B to ground or battery, detected by the driver chip in roughly 0.2 s. GM petrol direct injection, documented for the Saab 9-5 2.0T, uses P2150 for low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 2. Because both injectors of a diesel bank lose their feed, the engine runs on fewer cylinders. P2149 is the open circuit, P2151 the high fault of this group.

causes.label: Group B supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of group B shorted to its body
Moisture in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module

P2151.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2151.description: P2151 marks the group B injector supply as too high. GM's 2018 Duramax checks the high-side pins of the bank 2 injectors with the driver switched off and sets the code at 0.5 Ω or less to supply potential, 5 of 10 samples, type A. On Ford's 2023 diesels the same number stands for an internal fault reported by the boost voltage chip of the module, so a harness check alone rarely solves it. GM petrol direct injection uses it for excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 2. Bulletins point mostly to the control unit: Hino's 2016 J08 engines set P2148 and P2151 falsely and need new ECU software (SB-15-023), and GM PIP6034 replaces the PCM of 2024–25 Traverse, Acadia and Enclave with the 2.5 L LK0. P2150 is the low counterpart.

causes.label: Internal fault of the injector boost circuit in the module
Software falsely detecting the fault, reprogramming available
Group B supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector of group B with internal short

symptoms: Misfire on the group B cylinders
Sometimes no noticeable symptom besides the lamp

P2152.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2152.description: P2152 belongs to the third shared injector supply, so it appears only on engines with at least three injector groups or, at GM petrol engines, at least three cylinders. GM's 2009 Duramax puts injectors 2 and 5 into group 3 and flags an open, short or missing load after 6 ms, type A. VW's 2014 Touareg V6 TDI stores it when the diagnostic signal of the group C power stage fails, and the Passat VR6 allows a wider high-side window for this group, below 2.3 A or above 18.6 A. In GM petrol direct injection it covers the high-side control line of cylinder 3; GM bulletin PIP4924D lists it among injector codes on 3.0 L and 3.6 L V6 engines whose injector harness rubs through. Misfire on the related cylinders is the usual effect.

causes.label: Injector harness rubbed through at plenum, bolts or fuel line
Loose or corroded injector connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Faulty power stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Misfire on the group C cylinders

P2153.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2153.description: P2153 reports the third shared injector supply shorted toward ground. GM's 2018 Duramax tables use it only for the 6.6 L V8, where bank 3 feeds injectors 6 and 7; the four-cylinder 2.8 L has just two banks and never sets it. The criterion matches the other low codes – 0.5 Ω or less between a high-side pin and ground while the driver is on, 5 of 10 samples at 100 ms, type A. Ford lists group C among the injector driver checks of its 2023 diesels and flags shorts to ground or battery after about 0.2 s. On GM petrol direct injection, shown in the Saab 9-5 2.0T procedure, P2153 means low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 3, set after 1 s, type B. Open circuit and high fault of this group are P2152 and P2154.

causes.label: Group C supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of group C shorted to its body
Moisture in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Misfire on the group C cylinders

P2154.title: Fuel Injector Group C Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2154.description: P2154 is the high fault of injector supply group C. On GM's 2018 Duramax V8 it covers injectors 6 and 7: with the driver off, 0.5 Ω or less from a high-side pin to supply potential in 5 of 10 samples sets it, type A, one trip. Ford's 2023 diesels assign it to an internal error flagged by the module's high-voltage injector driver chip, a strong hint that the control unit itself is at fault. For GM petrol direct injection it means excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 3, and GM PIP6034 lists it with P2148, P2151 and P2157 on 2024–25 2.5 L LK0 crossovers, where an internal PCM hardware fault requires replacing the module. Group C exists only where an engine has a third bank or cylinder. The low and open faults are P2153 and P2152.

causes.label: Internal hardware fault of the injector driver in the module
Group C supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector of group C with internal short

symptoms: Misfire on the group C cylinders

P2155.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P2155.description: P2155 is the open or general fault of the fourth shared injector supply. On GM's 2009 Duramax V8 group 4 joins injectors 8 and 3; an open, short or missing load for 6 ms sets the code, type A. The Passat VR6 of 2014 runs four supply groups and checks group D against a high-side current window of under 2.6 A or above 14.9 A. GM petrol direct injection uses it for the high-side control line of cylinder 4. In the Saab 9-5 2.0T the supply lines are shared by cylinders 1 and 4, which is why a supply fault there stores P2146 and P2155 together (1 s, type B). The 2023–24 Corvette LT6 bulletin 24-NA-106 names P2155 among codes caused by water entering a wrong bank 2 connector. Rough running and misfire on the affected cylinders follow.

causes.label: Injector harness damaged or wire open
Water entering an injector harness connector
Open coil or piezo stack in an injector of the group
Faulty power stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Misfire on the group D cylinders

P2156.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P2156.description: P2156 reports the fourth shared injector supply shorted toward ground. GM's 2018 Duramax uses it only on the 6.6 L V8, where bank 4 combines injectors 3 and 8; the high-side pin reading 0.5 Ω or less to ground while switched on sets it after 5 of 10 samples, type A, lamp on the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary stops at group C, so the code does not appear there. On GM petrol direct injection, as in the Saab 9-5 2.0T, P2156 stands for low voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 4, set after 1 s and handled as type B. Since the diesel bank feeds two injectors, two cylinders cut out at once and the engine shakes noticeably. P2155 marks an open circuit and P2157 a high fault in the same group.

causes.label: Group D supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Injector of group D shorted to its body
Moisture in the injector harness connector
Faulty injector driver in the engine control module

P2157.title: Fuel Injector Group D Supply Voltage Circuit High
P2157.description: P2157 flags the group D injector supply as too high. GM's 2018 Duramax V8 tests the high-side pins of injectors 3 and 8 with the driver off; 0.5 Ω or less to supply potential in 5 of 10 samples sets it, type A, one trip, and the 2025 tables require 4 of 8. For GM petrol direct injection, documented in the Saab 9-5 2.0T procedure, it means excess voltage on the high-side control line of cylinder 4. GM's preliminary information PIP6034 for 2024–25 Traverse, Acadia and Enclave with the 2.5 L LK0 names P2157 alongside P2148, P2151 and P2154 and blames an internal PCM hardware fault – several high codes at once point to the module rather than to four separate wiring faults. P2156 is the low and P2155 the open circuit of this group.

causes.label: Internal hardware fault of the injector driver in the module
Group D supply wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector of group D with internal short

symptoms: Misfire on the group D cylinders
Several injector high codes stored together

P2158.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2158.description: P2158 reports an electrical fault in the circuit of a second vehicle speed signal, sensor B. P0500 is the matching code for sensor A. Which pickup carries the letter B is up to the manufacturer: a transmission output sensor, one of the ABS wheel sensors or another wheel. The only public manufacturer reference comes from Ducati: on the Scrambler 800 of model year 2021, P2158 stands for the front wheel speed sensor and P0500 for the rear one, and both could appear together with U0323 after fitting the accessory anti-theft kit, a case in which no sensor or ECU needs replacing. No car maker documents P2158 publicly. California's OBD rule names the vehicle speed sensor among input components to be checked for circuit faults. Speedometer, cruise control, ABS functions or shift timing may suffer.

causes.label: Speed sensor B defective or its tone ring damaged
Broken wire, corroded or loose connector in the sensor circuit
Retrofitted accessory interfering with the speed signal (Ducati anti-theft kit)

symptoms: Cruise control or ABS/traction functions unavailable

P2159.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2159.description: P2159 means the circuit of speed sensor B is electrically intact, but its signal does not fit: implausible jumps, dropouts or a value that disagrees with other speed sources. Two makers document it. Audi lists P2159 with fault environment code 8099 as a plausibility fault of speed sensor B on the 0B5 S tronic gearbox of the 2010–2014 RS5 and the S4, S5, S6 and S7; together with P0501 (sensor A) and gear selector codes it points to the gearbox-internal sensor module and its circuit board, which has to be replaced after case disassembly. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander engine control groups P2159 with P0500/P0501 as vehicle speed sensor faults, detected over two trips and lighting the MIL. P2158 is the pure circuit fault of the same sensor. Expect gearbox warnings, erratic shifting or a speedometer that jumps.

causes.label: Faulty speed sensor or transmission sensor module (Audi 0B5)
Damaged tone ring, wrong air gap or metal debris on the sensor tip
Intermittent contact in wiring or connector
Wrong tyre size or speed factor configured

symptoms: Check engine light or gearbox warning on
Erratic shifting or emergency gearbox mode

P215A.title: Vehicle Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215A.description: P215A compares the vehicle speed used by the powertrain with the speed derived from the ABS wheel sensors and sets when the two disagree. Volvo and Mack trucks document it most clearly: with I-Shift or mDRIVE gearboxes the code appears once the difference exceeds 12 km/h (7.5 mph), and the advice is to verify the speed factor and the tyre size stored in the brake controller before testing sensors. A Volvo case traced P215A with throttle dropouts to a loose ABS module ground. GM's 2025 brake module tables use P215A, Type B with MIL after two trips, both when more than two wheel sensor signals look suspect at the same time and when the spread between fastest and slowest wheel exceeds about 52 mph while moving. Speedometer loss, cruise or traction faults follow. P215B and P215C compare against the output shaft.

causes.label: Tyre size or speed factor not matching the vehicle (common after tyre or axle changes)
Faulty wheel speed sensor or damaged tone ring
Poor ABS module ground or wiring fault in the speed signal path
Fault in the transmission-side vehicle speed source

symptoms: ABS, traction or cruise control warnings, power dropouts

P215B.title: Vehicle Speed - Output Shaft Speed Correlation
P215B.description: P215B checks whether the vehicle speed, as the control unit has chosen it, matches the speed implied by the transmission output shaft. GM uses it widely in hybrids and EVs. The 2011 Volt tables set it, Type A with MIL after one trip, when wheel-based and output-shaft-based speed differ by more than 6.21 mph or when no secured speed source remains, counted over 400 of 800 samples of 25 ms. In the 2019 hybrid tables three sources are compared, output shaft, wheel sensors and motor speeds, and the code sets after 0.15 s when two of them disagree by more than 12.42 mph. GM bulletin 22-NA-089 links P215B on the 2017–2019 Bolt EV to a broken drive shaft washer damaging the wheel speed sensor, which is to be replaced. FCA lists P215B for the Pacifica Hybrid and fixes it with hybrid controller software.

causes.label: Damaged wheel speed sensor (GM Bolt EV broken anti-click washer)
Faulty transmission output speed sensor or its wiring
Hybrid or transmission control software (FCA Pacifica Hybrid)
Lost speed message from another module on the data bus

symptoms: Check engine light on after one trip
ABS, traction or stability lamps, systems switched off for the drive
Clicking noise from a front wheel (Bolt EV)

P215C.title: Output Shaft Speed - Wheel Speed Correlation
P215C.description: P215C compares the transmission output shaft speed with the output speed calculated back from the wheel sensors. Unlike P215B it does not judge the final vehicle speed but the agreement between these two measured sources. GM's 2019 hybrid tables set it as Type B, MIL after two trips, when the output shaft and the average from wheel and motor speeds differ by more than 50 or 60 rpm for 0.23 s. FCA uses the code widely: bulletin 21-031-14 updated the TCM of the 2014 Charger and 300 AWD with the 845RE gearbox because P215C set during braking, 21-022-23 reprograms the 2023 Charger 8HP50 for the same code, and on the 2014–2017 Jeep Cherokee a broken power transfer unit input spline produces P215C with P1720 and grinding noises, covered by a warranty extension. Shift quality or AWD functions may suffer.

causes.label: Transmission control software too sensitive, for example under braking (FCA bulletins)
Mechanical driveline fault such as a broken transfer unit spline (Jeep Cherokee)
Faulty output shaft speed sensor or wiring
Faulty wheel speed sensor or mismatched tyre sizes

symptoms: Grinding noise or loss of all-wheel drive (transfer unit damage)

P215D.title: Reductant Pump B Stuck On
P215D.description: P215D says the second DEF pump, called pump B or pump 2, keeps running or stays powered although the controller has commanded it off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Pump B itself is documented: Ford's 6.7L Super Duty trucks of 2023 can store pump B circuit codes P20FA, P20FC and P20FD (SSM 51891), and FCA names the same channel Reductant Pump 2 on 3.0L EcoDiesel models. California's OBD rule asks for functional checks of output components, and a stuck-on state is the logical opposite of P20FB, Performance/Stuck Off. A driver stage that no longer switches off, a control line shorted on the switched side or a welded relay could cause it. Effects can include pressure that cannot be released, lines not purged at shutdown and a drained battery. P201F is the same fault on pump A.

causes.label: Output stage in the control module no longer switching off
Pump control line shorted so the pump receives power permanently
Welded contacts in the pump supply relay

symptoms: Pump audible after switching off the engine
DEF system warning, possibly a flat battery after standing

P215E.title: Reductant Heater D Current Too Low
P215E.description: P215E says the fourth DEF heating element, heater D, drew less current than expected while it was switched on, so it is probably not warming the fluid. Which element carries the letter D depends on the maker; many SCR systems stop at three. No maker documents P215E publicly. GM's 2025 Duramax tables and Ford's 2023 diesel summary check only heaters A to C; GM flags their currents below 0.75 A across 40 readings, one per tenth of a second, as Type A; Ford watches power and current during each heating cycle. GM bulletin 21-NA-149 does show a heater D on the 3.0 L LM2, but only with circuit codes P20C5 and P20C8. The usual causes are an open or burnt element, high resistance at the connector or a missing heater feed. P215F is the high-current partner, P20C5 to P20C8 the control-circuit faults. In frost the fluid may thaw late.

causes.label: Heating element D open or burnt through, often inside a heated line or pump assembly
Corroded or loose pins at the heater D connector limiting current
Heater feed fuse or relay open, so the element gets no voltage
Weak heater output stage in the engine or DEF control module

symptoms: Check engine light together with a DEF or emission system message
Dosing starts late or not at all after cold starts in frost
Restart countdown or speed limitation if the fault stays active

P215F.title: Reductant Heater D Current Too High
P215F.description: P215F is set when heater D of the DEF system pulls more current than its design allows, which points to a partly shorted element or a leak path to ground in its wiring. The letter D is assigned by each maker, and many systems have only three heaters. No maker documents P215F publicly. As a guide, GM's 2025 Duramax tables trip the high-current codes of heaters A to C above 15 A in 40 samples of 0.1 s and treat them as Type A, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary detects an overloaded tank or line heater within 2.2 s. The controller usually switches the faulty element off to protect its driver, so the fluid in that area is no longer heated. Wet connectors, chafed leads and internal shorts are typical. The low-current partner is P215E; circuit faults are P20C5 to P20C8.

causes.label: Heating element D partly shorted internally
Moisture or DEF crystals in the heater D connector bridging pins
Chafed heater lead touching ground or a neighbouring circuit

symptoms: Check engine light with a DEF or emission system warning
DEF stays frozen in the affected area during cold weather
Blown heater fuse in some cases

P2160.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2160.description: P2160 reports that speed signal B shows little or no activity although the vehicle is plainly moving. Which pickup carries the letter B is the manufacturer's choice. GM assigns P2160 to the transfer case output speed sensor of its four-wheel-drive models (table 18OBDG04): with a gear engaged, moderate pedal and torque, no braking and the transmission output turning, a raw sensor reading under 25 rpm for 4.5 seconds stores the code as Type B, so the MIL follows after two trips. A broken wire, a short to ground or a dead sensor are the usual reasons. P2161 covers dropouts and erratic readings, P2158/P2159 the circuit and plausibility of the same sensor. Four-wheel-drive and speed-dependent functions may be restricted.

causes.label: Broken signal wire or short to ground between sensor B and the module
Speed sensor B itself delivers no pulses
Corroded or pushed-back pins at the sensor connector
Tone wheel loose or missing after transfer case or driveline work

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two drives
Speedometer or cruise control misbehaving on some models

P2161.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic/High
P2161.description: P2161 flags a speed signal B that behaves in ways no real vehicle can: it collapses for a moment, jumps or reads implausibly high. GM documents the code for the transfer case output speed sensor (18OBDG04). While the truck is driven in gear without braking, a drop of the sensor speed larger than a delta threshold starts a 3-second fail timer, and five such counts store the code as Type B. GM adds that one dropout can also start the P2160 timer, so whichever runs out first is recorded. Loose connector contacts, chafed wires, metal debris on the sensor tip or a cracked tone wheel are the typical culprits. P2160 means the signal is missing altogether; P2162 compares sensor B with sensor A.

causes.label: Connector contact opening briefly under vibration
Signal wire chafed against the transfer case or frame
Metal debris on the magnetic sensor tip
Chipped or cracked tone wheel

symptoms: Check engine lamp, often only on rough roads

P2162.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A/B Correlation
P2162.description: P2162 means two speed sources, A and B, disagree by more than the calibration permits although each circuit is electrically sound. Depending on the vehicle, A and B can be a transmission output sensor, a transfer case sensor or wheel sensors read through the ABS unit. No manufacturer documents P2162 publicly. GM shows how closely the sources are linked: when its transfer case sensor fails (P2160/P2161), the software substitutes driven-wheel speed multiplied by the axle ratio (18OBDG04). California's OBD rule names the vehicle speed sensor among inputs that must be checked for plausibility. Wrong tyre size or axle ratio, a damaged tone wheel or debris on one sensor are typical causes. Speedometer, shifting, cruise control and 4WD may suffer.

causes.label: Tyre size or axle ratio differs from the programmed values
Metal debris or damage on one of the two sensors
Damaged or wrong tone wheel on one shaft or hub
Wheel speed signal from the ABS unit faulty

symptoms: Harsh or mistimed shifts, possibly a fixed-gear fallback

P2163.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Maximum Stop Performance
P2163.description: P2163 concerns position signal A at the upper end of its travel: with the throttle or pedal resting on its maximum mechanical stop, the reading or the learned full-open value lies outside the band the calibration accepts. On Ford layouts A is the first throttle body sensor, while D to F belong to the pedal. Ford lists P2163 for the 2014 Boss 302S with MIL and wrench lamp. A Visteon patent shows the idea: the motor presses the plate onto its fully open stop for about 60 ms, the sensor value is stored, and a learned stop outside roughly 80 to 110 degrees is reported as a failure. Carbon, a bent stop or a worn sensor track are typical causes. P2109 is the matching closed-stop check; P2164-P2168 test the other letters. Reduced power is possible.

causes.label: Carbon or a bent stop keeps the plate from reaching full opening
Sensor A track worn at the full-open end
Replacement throttle body not matching or not relearned
Contact resistance in the sensor connector shifting the signal

symptoms: Check engine and throttle warning lamps on
Engine does not reach full power
Limp mode with limited throttle opening

P2164.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Maximum Stop Performance
P2164.description: P2164 is the full-travel test for position signal B. When the throttle or pedal is held at its upper stop, sensor B has to report a value inside a calibrated band; a reading or learned maximum outside that band sets the code. Ford and GM call their second throttle body sensor B, so on those designs the code points at the throttle body, yet no manufacturer documents P2164 publicly. The nearest evidence is Ford's listing of the A version P2163 and a Visteon patent that learns the open stop and rejects values beyond about 80 to 110 degrees. On many throttle bodies the second track runs opposite to the first, so comparing A and B at full opening helps to tell a sensor fault from a mechanical block. P2113 checks the closed stop of B; P0220-P0223 cover its circuit.

causes.label: Sensor B track worn or drifted at the full-open end
Deposits or a damaged stop limit the plate travel
Corroded contact on the sensor B signal or reference pin
End positions not relearned after part replacement

symptoms: Power limited at high throttle demand

P2165.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Maximum Stop Performance
P2165.description: P2165 belongs to the rarely used letter C. It is set when position signal C, at the upper stop of its throttle or pedal, reports a value the controller cannot accept as full travel. Since Ford gives A and B to the throttle and D to F to the pedal, C only appears on layouts with a third sensor track or a different naming scheme. No manufacturer documents P2165 publicly; the description follows the A version P2163, which Ford lists, and a Visteon patent on learning the throttle's open stop. Before replacing parts, confirm that the vehicle really uses a sensor C; an aftermarket throttle body or pedal with a different characteristic can also produce the code. P2114 tests the closed stop of C, P2136/P2137 compare C with A or B.

causes.label: Sensor C track worn at the end of travel
Replacement throttle or pedal with a different characteristic
Mechanical obstruction before the upper stop
Resistance in the sensor C wiring or connector

P2166.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor D Maximum Stop Performance
P2166.description: P2166 refers to position signal D, which on Ford designs is the first track of the accelerator pedal. The code means the reading with the pedal pressed all the way does not match the calibrated maximum, for instance because the pedal never reaches its stop or the track is worn at the far end. No manufacturer documents P2166 publicly; it applies the logic of the A version P2163 and of the open-stop learning in a Visteon patent to the pedal. A thick floor mat, a bent pedal arm or a worn pedal module are typical causes. The engine computer may then cap the torque request, so the car feels as if it never reaches full power. P2115 covers the rest position of D, P2120-P2124 its circuit, and P2138 the D/E correlation.

causes.label: Floor mat or object keeps the pedal from its stop
Pedal sensor track D worn at full travel
Bent pedal arm or damaged pedal bracket
Corroded pedal connector shifting signal D

symptoms: No kickdown or no full power with the pedal floored

P2167.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor E Maximum Stop Performance
P2167.description: P2167 checks position signal E at maximum travel; on designs that call the pedal tracks D, E and F, E is the second pedal sensor. The code sets when E, with the pedal fully down, reports a value outside the accepted band. Because the second track usually has a different characteristic from the first, checking D and E side by side at full pedal reveals whether only E is off or the pedal itself is blocked. No manufacturer documents P2167 publicly; the logic mirrors P2163, which Ford lists, and the open-stop learning in a Visteon patent. Wear near the far end of the E track, contact corrosion in the pedal connector or an obstructed pedal are likely causes. P2116 covers the rest position of E, P2125-P2129 its circuit, P2138 the D/E check.

causes.label: Pedal sensor track E worn at the full-travel end
Contact corrosion in the pedal connector
Pedal cannot reach its stop (mat, object, bent bracket)

symptoms: Limited power with the pedal fully pressed

P2168.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor F Maximum Stop Performance
P2168.description: P2168 covers position signal F at maximum travel. Letter F only exists where the pedal carries a third sensor track; GM's 2004 engine table, for example, runs a third pedal sensor under the F circuit codes, whereas most current cars make do with two tracks. The code sets when F, with the pedal at its upper stop, reports a value outside the accepted range. No manufacturer documents P2168 publicly; its logic follows P2163, which Ford lists, and the open-stop learning in a Visteon patent. Before ordering a pedal module, confirm that the car has a sensor F and compare all three tracks at full pedal. A worn track, a poor connector contact or a pedal that cannot reach its stop are typical. P2117 tests the rest position of F, P2130-P2133 its circuit.

causes.label: Third pedal track F worn at full travel
Poor contact on the sensor F pins
Pedal held short of its stop

P2169.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit/Open
P2169.description: The name points to a solenoid that lets an exhaust pressure regulator vent, but the only public, code-exact use found is on Jaguar Land Rover petrol models, where this code family belongs to the active exhaust valve: a solenoid in the tailpipe section switches a flap between quiet and sport sound. P2169 is the open or general fault of its control line. Land Rover documented P2169-13 (fault type 13 = open circuit) on the 2016 LR4 with the 3.0 supercharged V6 in bulletin SSM72392: the car configuration file enabled a valve that was never fitted, so the module saw an open circuit; reconfiguring cures it. Real cases mean a broken wire, loose plug or burnt-out coil. Exhaust pressure control valves, typical for diesels, have their own range P0475 to P0478. P2170 and P2171 cover the low and high faults.

causes.label: Vehicle configuration enables an active exhaust valve that is not fitted
Broken wire or loose connector at the exhaust valve solenoid, often from heat or road dirt
Solenoid coil burnt through

symptoms: Exhaust sound no longer changes with the drive mode

P216A.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216A.description: Injector group E exists only on engines with at least five cylinders or five separately fed injector groups. GM petrol direct injection uses one group per cylinder, and its 2024 tables (24OBDG07) state it plainly: injector E is cylinder 5. The code covers the high-side feed of that injector. Despite the word open in the title, GM uses it for shorts: the 2008 3.6 LLT sets P216A for the high side of cylinder 5 shorted to ground or battery and leaves open circuits to P0205; the 2024 tables flag less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off or to supply with it on, after two events above 9 V, one trip. GM bulletin PIP4924D lists P216A on 3.0 and 3.6 V6 engines whose injector harness rubbed through against the plenum, valve cover bolts or fuel line. Cylinder 5 misfires.

causes.label: Injector harness rubbed through at the intake plenum, valve cover bolts or fuel line
Cylinder 5 injector shorted internally
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp on, often with a cylinder 5 misfire code

P216B.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216B.description: P216B reports the feed of injector group E pulled toward ground. In GM petrol direct injection, group E means the injector of cylinder 5, so the code appears on V6 and V8 engines. GM's 2016 3.6 LGX V6 and 2018 6.2 LT4 V8 tables treat it as the injector 5 high-side line being grounded: while the driver is switched on, 25 A or more flows through it. With at least 11 V, 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms set the code, type A, so the MIL lights on the first trip. GM's preliminary information PI0631H for 2012 and 2013 Impala found the engine harness chafing against a transmission edge, which can ground a single circuit such as this one. The injector is shut off and cylinder 5 drops out. P216A is the general fault, P216C the short to voltage.

causes.label: High-side wire of injector 5 chafed through to ground, for example on the transmission
Cylinder 5 injector shorted to its housing
Engine control module output stage faulty

P216C.title: Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit High
P216C.description: P216C is the opposite fault of group E: the feed of the cylinder 5 injector carries voltage when it should not. GM tests it while the high-side driver is switched off; if 1 V or less remains between the signal and the controller supply, the line is treated as shorted to power. Its 2016 3.6 LGX V6 and 2018 6.2 LT4 V8 tables need at least 11 V and count 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms, type A with the MIL on the first trip. Typical sources are a chafed wire touching another powered circuit or an injector winding contacting a live conductor; GM's PI0631H lists this code with dozens of others for the Impala harness that wears on the transmission. Because the injector may stay energised, the module cuts it off and cylinder 5 drops out. P216B is the short to ground.

causes.label: Injector 5 feed chafed against a powered circuit
High-side driver in the engine control module leaking voltage
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the injector connector

P216D.title: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P216D.description: P216D is the general fault of injector group F, which GM petrol direct injection equates with cylinder 6; its 2024 tables (24OBDG07) call it injector F. GM uses this code for shorts on the high side rather than opens: the 2008 3.6 LLT sets it for cylinder 6 shorted to ground or battery, while an open on either side goes to P0206; the 2024 tables count two events of less than 0.5 ohm to ground or supply, above 9 V, one trip. Two bulletins name it. PIP4924D covers 3.0 and 3.6 V6 models such as Enclave, Traverse, CTS and Camaro with chafed injector harnesses. Bulletin 24-NA-106 for the 2023 and 2024 Corvette with the LT6 lists P216D as cylinder 6 alongside P2149, P2155 and P217D, all bank 2, caused by water in a wrong 12-way connector.

causes.label: Injector harness rubbed through on V6 engines
Water in the bank 2 injector harness connector (Corvette LT6)
Cylinder 6 injector shorted

symptoms: Check engine lamp on, cylinder 6 misfire
With the LT6 several bank 2 codes and fuel pressure faults at once

P216E.title: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P216E.description: P216E marks the feed of injector group F, the cylinder 6 injector on GM petrol direct injection, as shorted toward ground. It therefore concerns GM V6 and V8 engines with direct injection. The 2016 3.6 LGX and the 2018 LT4 tables use a current test: with the driver on, 25 A or more through the high side counts as a short, and 10 failures in 20 samples taken every 100 ms at 11 V or more store a type A code with the MIL on the first trip. GM's PI0631H for the 2012 and 2013 Impala includes P216E among the circuits that a harness rubbing on the transmission can damage; GM adds that usually only one circuit is hit. Diagnosis compares the resistance from the injector 6 feed pin to ground with the module unplugged. P216F is the high fault.

causes.label: Cylinder 6 feed wire chafed through to ground
Cylinder 6 injector shorted to ground
Engine control module output stage faulty

symptoms: Cylinder 6 misfire and loss of power

P216F.title: Fuel Injector Group F Supply Voltage Circuit High
P216F.description: P216F is set when the group F supply, on GM petrol direct injection the high-side line of cylinder 6, shows voltage while the driver is off. GM's criterion in its 2016 (16OBDG07A) and 2018 LT4 tables is 1 V or less between the line and the controller supply, which means the wire is practically at battery level. At 11 V or more, 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms store it as type A, MIL on the first trip. A short to power can keep current flowing through the injector or overload the driver, so the module disables that cylinder. Look for insulation damage where the harness meets brackets or the transmission, as described for the Impala in PI0631H, and for a connector bridged by moisture. Several high codes on different cylinders at once point to the module. P216E is the short to ground.

causes.label: Cylinder 6 feed shorted to another powered wire
Engine control module driver fault, especially with several high codes
Moisture in the injector connector

P2170.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P2170.description: P2170 reports the control line of the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid pulled toward ground. Jaguar Land Rover uses it for the solenoid of the active exhaust valve; its March 2018 shop foreman call lists P2170-11, meaning the line is grounded, on 2018 Discovery Sport and Evoque with active exhaust. On 2018 and 2019 Evoque, Discovery Sport and E-Pace with the 2.0 Ingenium petrol, MIL and sometimes a restricted performance message appear. JLR suspected high resistance while the valve is switched and asks for a circuit check, a check that the flap moves freely by hand and that the heat shield sits centred on the valve; a cold-soak test in a freezer can reproduce a sticking valve. New PCM software cured unexpected valve operation (JLRTB02020NAS2) and drops the power limitation.

causes.label: PCM software with an overly sensitive fault strategy, fixed by an update
Exhaust flap stiff, often from a misaligned heat shield or cold weather
Control wire chafed through to ground near the exhaust

symptoms: Restricted performance message on some models
Exhaust valve heard clicking at start-up

P2171.title: Exhaust Pressure Regulator Vent Solenoid Control Circuit High
P2171.description: P2171 means the module sees too much voltage on the control line of the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid, usually because the line touches battery voltage or the solenoid shorts internally. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The closest evidence comes from its sibling: Jaguar Land Rover assigns P2170 to the solenoid of the active exhaust valve on its petrol models, so on those cars P2171 belongs to the same part with the opposite electrical fault. CARB requires output components like this to be checked for circuit faults whenever they can affect emissions or other monitors. Checking means measuring the control wire with the solenoid unplugged for foreign voltage and the coil for a too low resistance. The driver mostly notices a MIL and an exhaust sound that no longer switches.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a battery-fed circuit
Solenoid coil shorted internally
Output stage in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Exhaust flap stays in one position

P2172.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden High Air Flow Detected
P2172.description: P2172 is set when the engine abruptly takes in far more air than the throttle opening can explain, as if a large leak had appeared behind the throttle plate. The controller compares measured airflow (MAF or MAP based) with the flow its throttle model expects and reacts to a quick jump in the difference. FCA uses the code widely under the name High Airflow/Vacuum Leak Detected (Instantaneous Accumulation) and lists it in many PCM reflash bulletins, among them 18-030-17 for the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia 2.0 turbo; a STAR case on the 2019 Ram 1500 traces it to spread MAP sensor terminals. A Ford patent describes how closed-throttle leak flow is estimated and corrected against measured airflow. A slipped hose or an open PCV line are typical. P2173 is the slow version.

causes.label: Hose, PCV line or brake booster line slipped off or split
Spread or pushed-out terminals at the MAP sensor connector
Engine software with oversensitive detection (reflash available)
Leaking throttle body gasket

symptoms: High or hunting idle, hissing noise from the engine bay

P2173.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P2173.description: P2173 reports an air surplus that builds up gradually: across a longer stretch of driving the engine receives more air than the throttle model predicts, which points to a small leak, a cracked vent hose or a plate that no longer seals. FCA calls it High Airflow/Vacuum Leak Detected (Slow Accumulation). Bulletin 09-010-20 replaces the oil vapour inlet tube on the 2017-2018 Jeep Renegade with the 1.4 MultiAir turbo after leaks there set P2173-00 with jerking or limp mode, while 18-006-23 cures it on the 2019 Renegade 1.3 turbo with new PCM software, listed next to P2110. A Ram STAR case ties it to loose MAP connector terminals. A Ford patent shows how modelled and measured throttle flow are aligned. P2172 is the sudden version, P2175 the opposite deviation.

causes.label: Cracked or loose crankcase ventilation or oil vapour tube
Small leak at an intake gasket or vacuum hose
Outdated engine software (FCA reflash)
MAP sensor connector with poor contact

symptoms: Check engine lamp after some driving
Start/stop system deactivated on some models

P2174.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden Low Air Flow Detected
P2174.description: P2174 means the airflow fell abruptly well below what the current throttle opening should deliver. The controller sees a fast negative gap between measured airflow and its throttle-model estimate, as happens when the intake is suddenly blocked, the plate jams or a hose collapses under vacuum. No manufacturer documents P2174 publicly. FCA's sibling codes P2172/P2173 for excess air show the same model comparison in practice, and a Ford patent explains how estimated and measured throttle flow are reconciled; California's OBD rule requires such air-handling inputs to be monitored. Look for a collapsed or kinked intake duct, snow, leaves or a bag over the air inlet, a sticking throttle or a faulty airflow sensor. Expect a sudden loss of power. P2175 is the slow variant.

causes.label: Air inlet suddenly blocked by snow, leaves or debris
Intake duct collapsed or kinked
Throttle plate sticking short of the commanded angle
Airflow or manifold pressure sensor reading too low

symptoms: Check engine and throttle warning lamps

P2175.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P2175.description: P2175 tracks an air shortfall that develops slowly: over many operating points the engine receives less air than the throttle position predicts, and the learned correction finally exceeds its limit. A clogged air filter, carbon narrowing the throttle bore, a partly blocked intake or an airflow sensor drifting low are the usual reasons. No manufacturer documents P2175 publicly. GM bulletin PIP4578B illustrates the mechanism: with growing carbon deposits in a high-mileage throttle body, the computer learns to open the plate further, and after cleaning an idle relearn is needed. FCA's P2173 is the slow deviation in the other direction, and a Ford patent describes matching modelled with measured throttle flow. Expect sluggish response and unsteady idle. P2174 is the sudden variant.

causes.label: Carbon build-up narrowing the throttle bore
Heavily clogged air filter or intake restriction
Contaminated airflow sensor reading low
Idle or airflow adaptation not reset after throttle cleaning

P2176.title: Throttle Actuator A Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P2176.description: P2176 says the closed rest position of throttle A could not be learned. At key-on or after shutdown the controller drives the plate onto its lower stop and stores the sensor values; if they stay outside the window after the permitted attempts, the code is set. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 aborts the learn when the plate misses the closed target by over 1.5 % or sensor 1 lies outside 0.33-0.58 V (sensor 2: 4.42-4.67 V), within one trip; GM's hybrid tables rate it Type A. Honda bulletin 13-042 cures false P2176 on 2013 Accord, Civic and Crosstour with software, GM PIP4573B blames frozen crankcase ventilation below -23 °C, and PIP4578B carbon. A Delphi patent describes repeated learn attempts. P218A is the throttle B code.

causes.label: Carbon on plate and bore preventing a clean closed position
Ice from a frozen crankcase ventilation holding the plate open
Engine software misjudging the sensor signals (update available)
Idle learn not performed after cleaning or module replacement

symptoms: Check engine lamp right after start
Reduced engine power after a cold start

P2177.title: System Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)
P2177.description: P2177 means bank 1's long-term trim has to add too much fuel once the engine is off idle, at part load and while accelerating. Bosch-type systems learn this as a multiplicative factor that scales with airflow, unlike the additive idle part behind P2187. GM's 2005 V6 and 2008 3.6 LLT set it above a factor of 1.23, GM's 2023 and 2024 tables above 1.27, both over two trips. Saab's 9-5 2.0T of 2010 checks at 6.9 to 41.7 g/s, 18 to 80 % load and 1280 to 4000 rpm and needs 4 s in a row or 50 s in total. VW's 2014 CC 2.0 TSI allows up to +28 %. Lean at load points to a weak fuel supply, an air mass sensor reading low or leaks under boost. Bulletins: Mazda CX-7 A/F sensor wiring, Audi RS 3 and TT RS software, Mercedes M254 fuel boiling.

causes.label: Fuel pressure too low under load, for example a weak pump or clogged filter
Air mass sensor reading too low or contaminated
Leak after the air mass sensor, often on the boost side
Calibration error or damaged A/F sensor wiring covered by bulletins

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Hesitation or lack of power when accelerating

P2178.title: System Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1)
P2178.description: P2178 is the rich-side limit of the bank 1 load adaptation: above idle the long-term trim has to take away more fuel than allowed. GM's Bosch-based V6 engines of 2005 and 2008 set it below a factor of 0.78, the 2023 and 2024 tables below 0.77, each after two trips. Saab's 9-5 2.0T uses the same window as for the lean code, 6.9 to 41.7 g/s, 18 to 80 % load and 1280 to 4000 rpm, and wants 4 s without break or 50 s in total. VW's 2014 CC 2.0 TSI accepts down to -21 %. A rich error that grows with load usually means an air mass sensor reading too high, excessive fuel pressure or injectors delivering too much. Mercedes saw it on the M254 with fuel boiling in the low-pressure side; Jaguar Land Rover lists P2178 with P0191 on Ingenium petrol engines and cured it with new PCM calibration.

causes.label: Air mass sensor reading too high
Fuel pressure too high or injectors over-delivering
Calibration error fixed by a software update
Fuel vapour from purge or boiling fuel in the low-pressure system

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after two trips

P2179.title: System Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 2)
P2179.description: P2179 is the bank 2 version of P2177 on engines with a front oxygen sensor for each cylinder bank: the load-dependent, multiplicative share of bank 2's long-term correction has reached its lean limit. GM's 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 and the 2008 3.6 LLT use a factor above 1.23, GM's 2024 tables above 1.27, both over two trips. VW's 2014 Touareg sets it for the 3.0 TSI hybrid and the 3.6 VR6 when bank 2 adaptation exceeds +30 %. If both banks are lean at load, look at what they share: fuel pressure, the pump, the air mass sensor. If bank 2 alone is affected, the cause lies on that side, such as a restricted injector, an intake leak at that bank's manifold or a front sensor reading lean. No bulletin naming this code was found.

causes.label: Low fuel pressure or air mass sensor fault, usually with P2177 too
Restricted injector on bank 2
Intake leak or front oxygen sensor fault on bank 2

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after two trips

P217A.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P217A.description: Group G only exists on engines with seven or more injector groups, in practice eight-cylinder engines with direct injection. GM's 2023 and 2024 summary tables (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07) name the cylinder 7 injector G and use P217A for a short on its high side: less than 0.5 ohm between the module pin and ground while the driver is off, or to the injector supply while it is on. Two such events with more than 9 V on the battery store the code within one trip. As with groups E and F, GM keeps open circuits on the separate per-cylinder injector codes, so the title's open wording is misleading on these engines. No bulletin naming this code was found. The injector is switched off, cylinder 7 misfires and the engine runs noticeably rough. P217B and P217C are the dedicated low and high codes.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 injector feed shorted to ground or supply in the harness
Cylinder 7 injector shorted internally
Engine control module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp on, cylinder 7 misfire

P217B.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P217B.description: P217B reports the feed of injector group G as grounded, which on GM's direct-injection V8 engines is the injector of cylinder 7, at the rear of bank 1. GM's 2016 table 16OBDG07A and the 2018 LT4 table of the supercharged 6.2 V8 measure it with the driver switched on: if 25 A or more flows through the high side, the line is grounded somewhere. The check runs every 100 ms as soon as the battery has 11 V; 10 failures in 20 samples set the code as type A, so the MIL comes on in the same trip. Check the harness routing at the rear of the engine and the injector connector before suspecting the module. The module stops firing the injector, which shows up as a cylinder 7 misfire. P217C is the high fault, P217A the general one.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 feed wire grounded at the rear of the engine
Cylinder 7 injector shorted to ground
Engine control module output stage faulty

P217C.title: Fuel Injector Group G Supply Voltage Circuit High
P217C.description: P217C means the group G injector supply, cylinder 7 on GM's direct-injection V8 engines, is pulled up to supply voltage. GM tests this while the high-side driver is off: if the line sits within 1 V of the controller supply, the module treats it as shorted to power. The tables 16OBDG07A (2016), 18OBDG03A for the 6.2 LT4 and 19OBDG03A apply the same counting of 10 failures out of 20 samples, 100 ms apart, at 11 V or more, and treat it as type A with immediate MIL. A wire rubbed against a powered circuit, a damaged injector connector and, more rarely, a faulty driver inside the module are the usual causes; a module fault often shows as several high codes at once. To protect the injector from staying open, cylinder 7 is shut off. P217B is the low counterpart, P217A the general code.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 feed shorted to a powered wire
Damaged or wet injector connector
Engine control module driver fault

P217D.title: Fuel Injector Group H Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P217D.description: Group H is the eighth injector group, on GM petrol direct injection the injector of cylinder 8, the last one on bank 2 of a V8. GM's 2023 and 2024 tables call it injector H and use P217D when its high side shows less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off or to the injector supply with the driver on; two events above 9 V store the code in one trip. GM's service texts refer to it as the high control circuit of the cylinder 8 injector. Bulletin 24-NA-106 for the 2023 and 2024 Corvette with the 5.5 LT6 shows how a common cause hits a whole bank: water getting into a wrong twelve-pin intermediate connector to the bank 2 injector harness set P2149, P2155, P216D and P217D, the even cylinders, together with rail pressure codes. The fix is a connector with the correct part number.

causes.label: Water in the bank 2 injector harness connector, Corvette LT6
Cylinder 8 injector feed shorted in the harness
Cylinder 8 injector shorted internally

symptoms: Check engine lamp on, cylinder 8 misfire
Several bank 2 injector codes at once if the connector is wet

P217E.title: Fuel Injector Group H Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P217E.description: P217E flags the supply of injector group H as grounded, on GM's direct-injection V8 engines the injector of cylinder 8. GM lists it for the 6.2 LT4 in 2018 and in its 2016 table 16OBDG07A. With the high-side driver switched on, a current of 25 A or more means the line has found a path to ground; at 11 V or more, 10 bad samples out of 20 taken at 100 ms set the code as type A and light the MIL right away. Since the per-cylinder low-side codes P0282 and P0283 cover the return line, this code points specifically at the feed wire, the injector body or the driver. A practical check is to unplug the module and the injector and measure the feed wire to ground before suspecting the module. The engine loses cylinder 8. P217F is the high fault.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 feed wire chafed to ground
Cylinder 8 injector shorted to its housing
Engine control module output stage faulty

P217F.title: Fuel Injector Group H Supply Voltage Circuit High
P217F.description: P217F is the last code of the injector group series: the feed of group H, cylinder 8 on GM's direct-injection V8 engines, shows supply voltage although the high-side driver is switched off. GM's tables 16OBDG07A, 18OBDG03A for the 6.2 LT4 and 19OBDG03A set it when the line stays within 1 V of the controller supply, counting 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms with 11 V or more, type A, MIL on the first trip. A short to power can hold the injector partly open or stress the driver, so the module cuts cylinder 8. Wiring that touches a powered conductor, moisture in the plug or a failing module output are the candidates; high codes on several cylinders together suggest the module. P217E is the short to ground, P217D the general fault.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 feed shorted to a powered wire
Moisture or corrosion in the injector connector
Engine control module output stage faulty

symptoms: Cylinder 8 misfire, possibly rich running on bank 2

P2180.title: System Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)
P2180.description: P2180 closes the series: bank 2's long-term trim must remove too much fuel above idle, so its multiplicative adaptation sits at the rich limit. GM's 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 and the 2008 3.6 LLT use a factor below 0.78, GM's 2024 tables below 0.77, both over two trips. VW's 2014 Touareg 3.0 TSI hybrid and 3.6 VR6 set it below -30 % on bank 2. Unlike P2190, which reacts to excess fuel at idle such as purge vapour, this code rises with load, so look at fuel delivered per injection: pressure regulator or high-pressure pump control, injectors leaking or over-delivering on bank 2, or a bank 2 front sensor reading rich. When P2178 is set as well, check the air mass reading and fuel pressure first. No bulletin naming this code was found.

causes.label: Injector on bank 2 leaking or over-delivering
Fuel pressure too high or air mass sensor over-reading, usually with P2178
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after two trips

P2181.title: Cooling System Performance
P2181.description: P2181 is the engine computer's verdict that the coolant warms up too slowly or settles below its target, almost always because the thermostat no longer closes. CARB requires the thermostat to be monitored and flags a failure when the warm-up stays more than 11.1 °C under the regulating point. GM (18OBDG03A) compares the block sensor with the radiator sensor during warm-up; if both rise together, the thermostat is open (Type B). VW's 2014 CC model expects 74–84 °C after a set amount of intake air; the Touareg with engine CNRB flags a gap of 7.5 K below the target. Audi, Bentley, Hyundai and Kia have bulletins tying P2181 to thermostats that stick or leak, Kia in part to software. Swapping the coolant sensor seldom helps. The heater stays lukewarm and fuel use climbs. P0128 is a similar thermostat code.

causes.label: Thermostat not closing fully because of wear, corrosion or debris on the seat
Engine control software too sensitive, fixed by a reflash on some models (e.g. Kia SA463)
Radiator fan running constantly and overcooling the engine
Low coolant level or air in the system distorting the temperature reading

symptoms: Check engine light, usually without any change in driving behaviour
Temperature gauge rises slowly or stays below normal
Weak cabin heating in cold weather
Higher fuel consumption on short trips

P2182.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
P2182.description: P2182 is the general circuit code for the second coolant temperature sensor: the module sees a fault in its wiring or signal but does not sort it into low, high or erratic. Where sensor 2 sits is up to the maker. Mazda fits it low on the radiator, VW calls it the radiator outlet sender, Ford's Escape plug-in hybrid uses it in the cabin heater loop, GM uses a second engine sensor. No maker documents P2182 itself publicly; GM, VW and others report the same sensor through the more specific P2184 to P2186. CARB demands that every coolant sensor be tested for broken circuits and readings beyond its valid span. Likely causes are an open signal wire, a loose connector or a dead sensor. Depending on the use of the sensor, fan control, thermostat diagnosis or cabin heating may run on substitute values.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at sensor 2
Signal or reference wire to sensor 2 open or damaged
Sensor 2 itself defective

symptoms: Radiator fan runs continuously as a precaution

P2183.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P2183.description: P2183 means sensor 2 delivers a voltage inside the valid band, yet the temperature does not fit the other readings. Most makers test this after a long cold soak, when all temperatures should match. The VW Touareg with engine CNRB sets it when the radiator outlet sensor differs by more than 35 K from intake air, ambient or fuel temperature at start-up. RAM 1500 models with the rear axle heater compare that loop with engine coolant and oil after 8 hours and allow 30 °C; a block heater can trip it falsely. Ford reflashes Escape and Corsair plug-in hybrids where an active cabin heater soak timer set P2183 wrongly. Mazda3 sensors at the radiator bottom let water in and read too low. Real causes are corrosion and drift; others need a software update. Low, high and erratic signals are P2184 to P2186.

causes.label: Water ingress or internal corrosion in sensor 2 shifting its reading
Control software misjudging soak time, block heater or cabin heater use
Coolant hoses at the sensor loop swapped or air trapped after service
Aged sensor element drifting out of tolerance

symptoms: Check engine light, often right after a cold start
Remote start disabled on some trucks
Engine overheat message without real overheating on some hybrids

P2184.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P2184.description: Coolant sensors are NTC thermistors: the hotter they get, the lower their resistance and voltage. P2184 therefore reports a signal from sensor 2 so low that it would mean an impossibly hot engine, typically a signal wire touching ground or a shorted sensor. GM's 2019 tables (19OBDG03D) set it when resistance drops below about 47.5 ohms, matching 150 °C, for 5 s within 6 s (Type B, MIL after two trips). VW's 2014 CC flags the radiator outlet sensor above 141 °C, the Touareg CNRB a voltage under 0.22 V. GM lists P2184 among the codes caused by a chafed engine harness in bulletin 21-NA-149. Because a hot reading is accepted as real at first, fans may run flat out. P2185 is the opposite fault, P2186 the erratic case.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor 2 chafed through and touching ground
Sensor 2 internally shorted
Coolant or water in the connector bridging signal and ground

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives on GM vehicles
Radiator fans running at full speed
Further codes and warnings if a harness is chafed

P2185.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
P2185.description: P2185 is the high end of the sensor 2 circuit check. With an NTC thermistor a high signal stands for extreme cold, so the usual reason is an open circuit: a broken wire, an unplugged or corroded connector, or a sensor with an interrupted element; a short to voltage is rarer. GM (19OBDG03D) watches for a resistance in the order of 300 kOhm, the value at -60 °C, after 10 s of engine running or above -20 °C intake air, 5 s within 6 s, Type B. VW sets it at below -43 °C on the 2014 CC and above 4.92 V or 4.94 V on the Touareg. Audi issued a 2025 bulletin for the A4 and A5 family on P2185 at the radiator outlet sender G83. In bulletin 21-NA-149 GM traces it to a chafed harness. Low and erratic signals are P2184 and P2186.

causes.label: Connector at sensor 2 unplugged, loose or corroded
Signal or ground wire of sensor 2 broken
Sensor element interrupted
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

symptoms: Fans run permanently as a safety measure
Low coolant or temperature warning without a real cause on some models

P2186.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2186.description: P2186 covers a sensor 2 signal that jumps instead of changing smoothly. Coolant temperature moves slowly because of the mass of the liquid, so a step faster than physics allows points to a loose contact rather than a real change. GM's 2019 tables (19OBDG03D) work out an upper and lower limit for each new reading from the previous value and the sensor's time constant, about 7.4 s for sensor 2 within a -60 to 150 °C window; a reading outside this corridor for 5 s within 6 s sets the code as Type B, MIL after two trips. GM also lists P2186 among the effects of the chafed engine harness in bulletin 21-NA-149. Typical causes are worn connector pins, a wire broken inside the insulation or a sensor with an intermittent element. Steady low or high signals are P2184 and P2185.

causes.label: Worn or loose pins in the sensor 2 connector
Wire broken inside its insulation or chafed harness making intermittent contact
Sensor 2 with an intermittent internal fault

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Fans switching on and off irregularly
Temperature-related messages that appear and vanish

P2187.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P2187.description: P2187 means the long-term fuel trim of bank 1 has to add more fuel than allowed in the idle and low-load range. Many systems, especially Bosch ones, split mixture adaptation into an additive part, which dominates at low airflow, and a multiplicative part for load. An air leak adds a fixed amount of unmeasured air, which matters most at idle, so it shows up in the additive part. GM's 3.6 V6 engines set the code above 7 % (2005) or 6.1 % (2008 LLT, at 520 to 1120 rpm, 1.7 to 7.8 g/s and coolant above 60 °C), and GM's 2024 tables above about 5.5 %, over two trips. On the Opel/GM 2.0 turbo in the Saab 9-5 (2010) the weighted long-term trim must exceed its limit for 4 s continuously or 50 s in total (Type B). Audi traced P2187 with P2279 on 2.0 TFSI engines to a crankcase ventilation valve that let boost into the crankcase; Mazda found A/F sensor wiring on the CX-7 2.3 turbo shorted after brake fluid was spilled on it.

causes.label: Air leak after the air mass sensor, often at the crankcase ventilation
Damaged front oxygen or A/F sensor wiring
Fuel pressure too low

symptoms: Rough or hunting idle, hissing from the engine bay

P2188.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P2188.description: P2188 means the long-term fuel trim of bank 1 has to remove more fuel than allowed in the idle and low-load range, the additive part of the mixture adaptation on Bosch-type systems. GM's 2008 3.6 LLT sets it below -6.0 % at 520 to 1120 rpm and 1.7 to 7.8 g/s, with closed loop and coolant above 60 °C. On the Opel/GM 2.0 turbo in the Saab 9-5 (2010) the weighted long-term trim must stay below its limit for 4 s or 50 s in total (Type B); Saab's test gives -22 to 0 % as normal trim and 19 to 42 kPa manifold pressure at idle. At idle the extra fuel typically comes from sources the ECM does not meter: Mercedes lists for the M132 engine a leaking PCV valve, leaking injectors or excessive fuel pressure, wrong intake pressure readings, a restricted or worn throttle and a contaminated oxygen sensor. A saturated charcoal canister purging at idle has the same effect. Stellantis found an airflow straightener in the air box clipped in wrong, which disturbed the air mass reading and set P2188 and P2190.

causes.label: Leaking injector or fuel pressure too high
Fuel vapour from the purge valve or oil-diluted crankcase gases
Air mass or manifold pressure reading wrong

P2189.title: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P2189.description: P2189 is the bank 2 version of P2187: on engines with a front oxygen sensor per bank, the long-term trim of bank 2 has to add more fuel than allowed at idle and low load. GM's 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 set it when the additive correction exceeds 7 %, the 2008 3.6 LLT above 6.1 % at 520 to 1120 rpm, airflow of 1.7 to 7.8 g/s, engine load of 11 to 45 % and coolant above 60 °C, and GM's 2024 tables above about 5.5 % over two trips. Because both banks share the throttle, crankcase ventilation and brake booster vacuum, a leak there normally lifts the idle trim on both banks, setting P2187 and P2189 together. A code on bank 2 alone points to something only that bank sees: an intake manifold gasket or runner leak on that side, an injector on that bank, or the bank 2 front sensor or its wiring. Comparing both banks' trims at idle and at 2500 rpm narrows it down.

causes.label: Intake gasket or runner leak on the bank 2 side
Shared vacuum leak, usually with P2187 present too
Bank 2 front sensor, its wiring or an injector on that bank

P218A.title: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P218A.description: P218A is the throttle B counterpart of P2176: on engines with a second electronic throttle, usually one per cylinder bank, that second unit failed to learn its closed rest position. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 runs the same three-step learn for bank 2 as for bank 1. First the plate must reach the closed target within 1.5 %, then the motor has to press it onto the stop with enough duty cycle, and finally the stored voltages must fall inside 0.33-0.58 V for sensor 1 and 4.42-4.67 V for sensor 2; any failed step stores the code within one trip. No other manufacturer documents P218A publicly. Ice, carbon, a weak motor or wiring faults at throttle B are typical causes, and engine power may be limited. Electrical motor faults of throttle B use P210A.

causes.label: Carbon or ice keeping throttle B off its closed stop
Weak motor or gear wear in throttle unit B
Position sensors of throttle B outside the learn window
Supply or signal wiring fault at throttle B

P218B.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit
P218B.description: P218B is a general electrical fault in the second throttle/fuel inhibit line, B. An inhibit line carries a signal with which another unit can tell the engine computer to keep the throttle closed or stop fuelling. No manufacturer documents the B line publicly. The only published use of this function concerns the A line: GM's 2005 table for the 3.5-litre V6 (L66) places it in the throttle valve control section, where the injection and throttle processors check each other, and monitors it with P2553-P2555 once per drive cycle after ignition off, lighting the MIL on the next drive cycle. California's OBD rule requires inputs of this kind to be checked for circuit faults. Open wires, corroded pins and module connector faults come first; reduced power is possible.

causes.label: Open or high-resistance inhibit B wire
Corroded or loose pins at the engine or throttle module connector
Fault in the unit that drives the inhibit signal

symptoms: Check engine lamp on the following drive

P218C.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Range/Performance
P218C.description: P218C means the inhibit B line is electrically within limits, yet its state or response does not fit what the controller expects: it may signal a lock when none is requested, or fail to react during a function test. No manufacturer documents P218C publicly. GM's 2005 table for the 3.5-litre V6 (L66) shows the analogous test on line A as P2553: a function check of the relay path, judged by a normal signal on the serial data link with battery voltage above 7 V, run once per drive cycle after ignition off and lighting the MIL on the next drive. California's OBD rule asks for plausibility checks of such inputs. Likely causes are a sticking relay, a slow-switching driver or software mismatch between the modules. P218D/P218E cover hard low and high faults.

causes.label: Relay in the inhibit path sticking or switching late
Software versions of the communicating modules do not match
Intermittent contact causing implausible line states

symptoms: Check engine lamp on the next drive
Occasional power reduction without obvious reason

P218D.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit Low
P218D.description: P218D reports that the voltage on inhibit line B sits below the lowest permitted value, which normally points to a short to ground, a missing supply from the sending unit or an open line pulled down by the input stage. No manufacturer documents P218D publicly. For the A line, GM's 2005 table for the 3.5-litre V6 (L66) gives a concrete limit: P2554 is set when the analogue throttle inhibit circuit reads under 0.498 V for 4 seconds, with the check running after ignition off and the MIL lit on the next drive cycle. California's OBD rule requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. Chafed insulation touching body ground, water in a connector or a failed driver in the sending module are the likely causes. P218E is the opposite fault, P218B the general circuit code.

causes.label: Inhibit B wire shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in a connector of the inhibit line
Output stage of the sending module failed

symptoms: Check engine lamp on the following drive

P218E.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit B Circuit High
P218E.description: P218E says the inhibit B line carries more voltage than the controller allows, typically because it touches a battery-fed wire or the sending unit's output stage is stuck high. No manufacturer documents P218E publicly. On the A line, GM's 2005 table for the 3.5-litre V6 (L66) uses two limits for P2555: more than 10 V with the ignition on, or more than 4.5 V once the ignition is off, each judged over 4 seconds; the check runs after shutdown and the MIL lights on the next drive cycle. The lower limit with the ignition off shows that the line should be nearly dead when the system sleeps. California's OBD rule requires such range checks. Look for chafing against supply wires, a backfeed through a faulty module or a shorted relay. P218D is the low-side counterpart.

causes.label: Inhibit B wire shorted to a battery-fed circuit
Voltage fed back through a faulty module after ignition off
Relay contacts welded, keeping the line energised

symptoms: Check engine lamp on the following drive

P218F.title: Reductant No Flow Detected
P218F.description: P218F means the SCR system is dosing on paper, but nothing reaches the exhaust: the expected link between dosing commands, pump effort and line pressure is missing. Ford's 2023 diesel summary, which calls the test a reductant delivery check for clogging, runs it while dosing with the pressure error inside 0.5 bar for 5 s. It fails when the pressure barely reacts to changes in the injection rate and the mix of rate and pump duty misses its model by more than 0.15. Ford also lists it for the 6.7 L Power Stroke (18-2127, PCM update). Nissan reflashed Titan XD trucks with the Cummins 5.0 L V8 when P218F appeared at 0 °C or below. VW says P218F can stay after repairs on 2.0 TDI cars until a leak in the DEF line is fixed. Pressure codes are P20E8/P20E9.

causes.label: Dosing valve or its nozzle crystallised and blocked
Leak in the DEF line between pump and dosing valve
Partly frozen line in frost or control software that needs an update
Worn DEF pump that cannot keep up delivery

symptoms: Check engine light with a DEF or emission system warning
Restart countdown or speed limitation if the fault persists
White crystalline deposits at the dosing valve or line joints

P2190.title: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P2190.description: P2190 is the bank 2 counterpart of P2188: the long-term trim of bank 2 has to remove more fuel than allowed at idle and low load. GM's 2008 3.6 LLT sets it below -6.0 % in the same window it uses for P2188 (520 to 1120 rpm, 1.7 to 7.8 g/s, closed loop, coolant above 60 °C, catalyst heating not active), and GM's 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 treat it in the same additive adaptation range. A rich fault on bank 2 only usually lies in that bank: a leaking injector, or a bank 2 front sensor reading lean so the ECM keeps leaning the mixture. Fuel pressure, purge vapour and air-mass errors act on both banks and tend to set P2188 and P2190 together. Stellantis is an example: an airflow straightener clipped in wrong in the air box upset the air mass reading and logged P2188 and P2190 together, sometimes with P0111 and an unstable idle; refitting it correctly cured it.

causes.label: Leaking injector on bank 2
Shared cause such as air mass error or purge vapour, usually with P2188 too
Bank 2 front sensor reading lean

P2191.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2191.description: P2191 sets once bank 1's long-term trim has run into its enrichment limit in the upper load range, so the engine would be lean there without the correction. It is the third load zone next to P2187 (idle) and P2177 (off idle), and it is where a supply that copes at cruise first falls short: a tired fuel pump, a clogged filter, poor pressure regulation, injectors that flow too little, or an air mass sensor that reads low at high airflow. CARB demands a fault once adaptive control has used up the adjustment the maker allows (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.2)). No manufacturer publishes its criteria for P2191; GM covers the load range with P2177 and a factor of 1.23 instead, and Kia lists only the rich sibling P2192 for the Rio and Soul 1.6 GDI. Drivers may feel hesitation when accelerating hard.

causes.label: Fuel pump or pressure regulation unable to hold pressure at high demand
Clogged fuel filter or strainer
Air mass sensor under-reading at high airflow
Partly blocked injectors on bank 1
Charge-air or intake leak behind the air mass sensor (turbo engines)

symptoms: Hesitation or flat spot under heavy throttle
Loss of power when climbing or towing
High positive long-term fuel trim at high load only

P2192.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2192.description: P2192 is the rich-side limit of the bank 1 trim in the upper load zone: the controller has pulled as much fuel as it may and the front sensor still reports excess fuel. Typical sources grow with demand, such as an air mass sensor reading high, fuel pressure above specification, or injectors that over-deliver or drip at high rail pressure; on direct-injection engines a leaking high-pressure injector is a prime suspect. Kia documents the code by name: bulletin ENG 146 (2015) lists P2192 with P2188 and other codes on 2012 to 2014 Rio and Soul with the 1.6 GDI engine and cures it with an ECM software upgrade rather than parts. GM handles the same load range as P2178 with a lower factor limit of 0.78. Expect higher consumption and possibly a fuel smell; P2188 is the idle counterpart, P2178 the off-idle one.

causes.label: ECM calibration issue covered by a software update (e.g. Kia 1.6 GDI)
Air mass sensor reading too high
Injector leaking or over-delivering at high rail pressure
Fuel pressure above specification

symptoms: Fuel smell or dark exhaust under load

P2193.title: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2193.description: P2193 reports for bank 2 what P2191 reports for bank 1: in the upper load zone the long-term trim of that bank sits at its enrichment limit.
