It only exists on engines with a separate front sensor per bank, such as V6, V8 and boxer engines. The useful question is whether bank 1 shows the same. Lean at high load on both banks (P2191 with P2193) points to something they share, chiefly fuel pump, filter, pressure regulation or the air mass sensor. Bank 2 alone narrows it to that side: injectors on bank 2, an intake gasket or runner leak there, or an exhaust leak ahead of the bank 2 sensor. No manufacturer documents P2193 publicly; GM monitors the comparable range as P2179, and CARB sets the general rule for exhausted fuel adaptation in 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.2).

causes.label: Weak fuel supply (pump, filter, pressure regulation), usually with P2191
Restricted injectors on bank 2
Intake gasket or runner leak on the bank 2 side
Exhaust leak ahead of the bank 2 front sensor

symptoms: Bank 2 long-term trim much higher than bank 1 at high load

P2194.title: System Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P2194.description: P2194 means bank 2 has reached the lower limit of its trim in the upper load zone: the ECM is removing as much fuel as permitted, yet that bank still runs rich. Because air mass, fuel pressure and canister purge feed both banks, a rich error caused by them usually brings P2192 along. When P2194 stands alone, look at bank 2 itself: a leaking or over-delivering injector, an injector of the wrong flow class after a repair, or a bank 2 front sensor that reads lean so the controller keeps adding fuel. Comparing the trims of both banks while holding a high load on the road or a dynamometer separates the two cases. No manufacturer publishes P2194 criteria; GM uses P2180 with a factor limit of 0.78 for the corresponding range. The driver mainly sees higher consumption.

causes.label: Leaking or over-delivering injector on bank 2
Bank 2 front sensor reading lean
Air mass sensor reading high or fuel pressure too high (usually with P2192)

symptoms: Bank 2 long-term trim strongly negative at high load

P2195.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2195.description: P2195 means the front oxygen or air-fuel sensor on bank 1 reports a lean mixture that the ECM does not believe, either because it stays lean or because it disagrees with other evidence. On GM's Bosch-based 2005 V6 the rear sensor has to read rich (above 0.85 V) while the front A/F sensor reads leaner than lambda 1.08 and the short-term trim sits at its maximum of 1.25, for about 100 s or 50 s in total. Ford checks narrow-band sensors for fewer than 5 switches in 30 s and wide-band sensors for 30 s at the short-term trim limit; from 2019 a sensor whose filtered lambda changes by less than 0.0001 for 30 s sets P2195 if the value is at or above 1. On the Opel/GM 2.0 turbo in the Saab 9-5 (2010) the code sets within 4 s continuously or 50 s in total. Ford replaced the heated oxygen sensors for P2195 and P2197 on 2015 to 2017 Explorer and F-150 3.5 GTDI. An exhaust leak ahead of the sensor can also make it read lean.

causes.label: Front oxygen or A/F sensor aged or contaminated
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor
Sensor signal or reference wiring fault

symptoms: Possible rough running or higher consumption from wrong fuelling

P2196.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P2196.description: P2196 means the front oxygen or air-fuel sensor on bank 1 reports a rich mixture that the ECM does not accept. On GM's Bosch-based 2005 V6 this is a cross-check with the rear sensor: the rear sensor reads lean (below 0.15 V) while the front A/F sensor reads richer than lambda 0.92 and the short-term trim has pulled to its minimum of 0.75, for about 100 s or 50 s in total. Ford sets it for a narrow-band sensor that hardly switches and stays rich, a wide-band sensor that sits 30 s at the short-term trim limit, or, from 2019, a filtered lambda below 1 that changes by less than 0.0001 for 30 s; Ford blocks the stuck-rich test while fuel is boiling off the oil after a cold start. On the Opel/GM 2.0 turbo in the Saab 9-5 (2010) the code sets within 4 s continuously or 50 s in total. Because the ECM leans the engine to follow the false signal, a rear sensor reading lean and a lean real mixture often accompany it.

causes.label: Front oxygen or A/F sensor contaminated or aged
Sensor signal shorted or reference circuit fault

P2197.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2197.description: P2197 is the bank 2 version of P2195 on engines with a front sensor per bank: the bank 2 front oxygen or A/F sensor keeps reporting lean in a way the ECM rejects. GM's Bosch-based 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 flag it when the bank 2 rear sensor reads rich (above 0.85 V) while the front sensor reads leaner than lambda 1.08 with short-term trim at its 1.25 maximum, a contradiction a real lean mixture would not produce. Ford applies its switching, trim-limit and, from 2019, stuck-lambda tests to bank 2 the same way, with a 30 s window. Ford's 2017 bulletin for 2015 to 2017 Explorer and 2015 to 2016 F-150 3.5 GTDI lists P2195 and P2197 with P2626 and P2629, the pumping-current trim circuits of the A/F sensors, and fixes them with new heated oxygen sensors. If only bank 2 is affected, an exhaust manifold leak on that side ahead of the sensor is worth ruling out before replacing the sensor.

causes.label: Bank 2 front oxygen or A/F sensor aged or contaminated
Exhaust manifold leak on bank 2 ahead of the sensor

symptoms: Possible rough running or higher consumption

P2198.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P2198.description: P2198 is the bank 2 counterpart of P2196: the bank 2 front oxygen or A/F sensor reports rich in a way the ECM does not accept. On GM's Bosch-based 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 the bank 2 rear sensor must read lean (below 0.15 V) while the front sensor reads richer than lambda 0.92 and the short-term trim has dropped to its 0.75 minimum; the code then sets after about 100 s, or 50 s cumulatively, over two trips. Ford uses the same lack-of-switching, trim-limit and stuck-lambda logic as on bank 1, sets the stuck-rich code when the frozen lambda value is below 1, and suspends the stuck-rich test during cold starts while fuel boils off the oil through the crankcase ventilation. A sensor contaminated by oil or coolant, or one whose signal or reference wiring has a fault, gives this pattern; since the ECM leans bank 2 to follow the false reading, the rear sensor of that bank usually shows lean at the same time.

causes.label: Bank 2 front oxygen or A/F sensor contaminated or aged
Sensor signal or reference wiring fault

P2199.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P2199.description: P2199 compares two intake air temperature readings that should be close, typically one in the air mass sensor and one further downstream in the intake manifold or a combined pressure and temperature sensor. Each circuit can be fine on its own; the fault is the disagreement. GM sets it when the two values differ by more than 55 °C in 40 of 50 samples taken every 100 ms, as a Type B code with MIL after two trips (2016 and 2018 tables). VW's 2014 Touareg uses a much tighter limit of 10 °C between the two manifold temperatures. CARB requires such rationality checks for input sensors under (e)(15). Stellantis lists it among the codes addressed by a PCM update for the 2020 RAM 1500 with the 3.0 EcoDiesel V6; there, check the software level first. Circuit faults are P0111 to P0114 (sensor 1) and P0096 to P0099 (sensor 2).

causes.label: One temperature sensor drifted or contaminated
Corroded connector or added resistance in one sensor circuit
Calibration issue fixed by a PCM update (e.g. RAM 1500 3.0 EcoDiesel 2020)
Strong heat soak or hot-air leak near one sensor

symptoms: Scan data shows two clearly different intake temperatures with the engine cold-soaked

P219A.title: Bank 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219A.description: P219A means the ECM sees mixture differences between the cylinders of bank 1 that are large enough to raise emissions, even if the bank average is fine. CARB phased this monitor in from 25 % of 2011 to all 2014 model-year petrol vehicles (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)). GM measures how much the upstream sensor signal varies per firing event, normalises the result against a map of a healthy engine and flags a ratio above 1.05 (one 2016 engine, 1100 to 3500 rpm, Type A, one trip). Mitsubishi counts rich and lean peaks at 1750 to 3250 rpm and 40 to 70 % volumetric efficiency. On inline engines bank 1 is the whole engine. Toyota traced P219A on 2012 to 2014 Corolla 2ZR engines to compression escaping into the exhaust; from 2014 the Corolla adds the cylinder codes P219C to P219F.

causes.label: One injector clogged, leaking or out of flow tolerance
Compression loss through an intake or exhaust valve
Air leak at one intake runner or gasket
ECM logic or sensor signal issue covered by software or wiring bulletins

symptoms: Slight rough running or misfire codes when one cylinder is far off

P219B.title: Bank 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219B.description: P219B is the bank 2 counterpart for V and boxer engines. Ford's 2012 summary shows one way to find it: the ECM watches the fast ripple of the bank's wide-band sensor over windows of roughly 50 revolutions and sets the code when more than 75 % of them fail, after 300 to 700 s of driving at 1000 to 3000 rpm and 20 to 60 % load. On one GM 2016 engine the bank 2 limit is 1.15 against 1.05 for bank 1. Bulletins name leaking direct injectors (Ford F-150 2.7 EcoBoost 2018; Explorer and Aviator 3.0 EcoBoost 2023 to 2025, injectors of the affected bank replaced), faulty or contaminated injectors (Honda Pilot 2016), electrical noise in the A/F sensor lines (Mazda CX-9 2011 to 2013) and, at Infiniti on the QX80, a warning not to swap the A/F sensor first. A code on bank 2 only points to a part on that side.

causes.label: Leaking or contaminated injector on bank 2
Interference or damage in the bank 2 A/F sensor wiring
Intake runner or gasket leak at one bank 2 cylinder
PCM calibration addressed by a software update

symptoms: Possible misfire codes on bank 2 cylinders

P219C.title: Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219C.description: P219C names cylinder 1 as the one whose mixture departs from the others. Not every system can do that: CARB lets the stored code point only as far as the monitoring method allows, so many engines just log P219A or P219B. Those that resolve single cylinders include Toyota (the 2014 Corolla 2ZR gained P219C to P219F) and VW, whose 2014 2.5 litre five-cylinder leans each cylinder in turn and judges the resulting roughness, flagging a ratio below 0.19 or above 1.50. Subaru reflashed 2019 to 2020 Crosstrek Hybrid ECMs because P219C to P219F set without a real fault. Where the fault is real, check the cylinder 1 injector, its intake port seal and valve tightness with a leak-down test, as Toyota prescribes for the 2015 Tacoma V6. Cylinder numbering differs between makers, so confirm which cylinder is number 1.

causes.label: Cylinder 1 injector clogged, leaking or out of tolerance
Valve leakage on cylinder 1 (leak-down test)
Intake runner or injector seal leak at cylinder 1
False detection fixed by ECM reprogramming (e.g. Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid)

symptoms: Possible P0301 or rough idle if cylinder 1 deviates strongly

P219D.title: Cylinder 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219D.description: P219D singles out cylinder 2. On engines with two banks, whether cylinder 2 sits on bank 1 or bank 2 depends on the maker's numbering, which decides whether P219A or P219B may appear alongside. Bulletins show three very different outcomes. Kia replaced the high-pressure injector and its clip plus the high-pressure and crossover fuel pipes on 2022 Carnival models with the 3.5 GDI V6 when any of P219C to P21A1 had set. Hyundai fixed P219C to P219F on the 2018 Sonata 2.0 turbo with ECM and TCM software and noted that drivers feel nothing. Stellantis found a charge-air cooler with a loose crimp on the 2025 RAM 1500 3.0 Hurricane, which set P219D among other cylinder codes along with a whistling noise and reduced boost. A real cylinder 2 fault is confirmed with an injector balance test and a leak-down test.

causes.label: Faulty high-pressure injector at cylinder 2 (direct injection)
Charge-air leak upsetting cylinder filling (e.g. RAM 3.0 Hurricane)
Detection logic corrected by software update (e.g. Hyundai Sonata 2.0T)
Compression loss at cylinder 2

symptoms: Reduced power or whistling noise if a charge-air leak is the cause

P219E.title: Cylinder 3 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219E.description: P219E points at cylinder 3. Two bulletins show that a mixture code does not always mean a fuel part. Audi stored P219C to P21A1, one code per affected cylinder, on 2010 to 2012 S4, S5 and A6 with the 3.0 TFSI because of an incorrect software setting; the fix was new engine software and, in a later revision, a new crankcase pressure regulating valve. Lexus traced P219A and P219C to P219F on the 2.0 turbo 8AR-FTS (NX, IS, RC, GS 2015 onward) to compression lost through exhaust valves with worn guides, sometimes with misfire codes and reduced engine power, and repaired the cylinder head. Toyota's 2015 Tacoma V6 bulletin also starts with a leak-down test. For a lone P219E, test the cylinder 3 injector and compression before replacing sensors; the bank sensor itself is shared by all cylinders.

causes.label: Exhaust valve leakage at cylinder 3 (e.g. worn guides on Lexus 8AR-FTS)
Cylinder 3 injector delivering the wrong amount
Incorrect ECM software setting (e.g. Audi 3.0 TFSI)
Faulty crankcase pressure regulating valve

symptoms: Reduced engine power in severe cases

P219F.title: Cylinder 4 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P219F.description: P219F singles out cylinder 4, the last cylinder on four-cylinder engines. Infiniti issued a bulletin for 2017 to 2018 QX60 with the direct-injection VQ35DD that stored only P219F without any driveability complaint; the remedy was ECM reprogramming followed by the idle air volume learn. Honda found the opposite case on 2023 to 2025 CR-V Hybrid and Accord Hybrid: a leaking injector made the mixture rich, fouled spark plugs and caused rattling and rough running, with P219C to P219F, P0172 and A/F sensor heater codes; all injectors and the fouled plugs were replaced and Honda warned against changing the A/F sensor first. Hyundai's 2018 Sonata 2.0 turbo also set P219F through software. Reading the spark plug of the flagged cylinder is a quick first check for rich or lean burning.

causes.label: Leaking injector at cylinder 4
Oversensitive detection fixed by ECM reprogramming (e.g. Infiniti QX60, Hyundai Sonata)
Fouled spark plug as a consequence of a rich cylinder

symptoms: Rough running or rattling noise when an injector leaks
No symptom when the cause is software

P21A0.title: Cylinder 5 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A0.description: P21A0 can only occur on engines with at least five cylinders. VW's 2014 specification books for the Golf, Jetta, Passat and Beetle with the 2.5 litre inline five list P219C to P21A0, one per cylinder, all judged the same way: the ECM briefly leans one cylinder, measures how much rougher the engine runs and derives an individual fuel correction; a result below 0.19 or above 1.50 is a fault. On a five-cylinder with a single front sensor, the bank code P219A belongs to the same engine. Six-cylinder users include Toyota's 2015 Tacoma 1GR-FE, Audi's 3.0 TFSI (software) and Kia's 2022 Carnival 3.5 GDI (injectors). Because the method uses roughness, a weak ignition coil or a compression problem in cylinder 5 can also influence the result.

causes.label: Cylinder 5 injector out of tolerance
Ignition or compression weakness at cylinder 5 affecting the roughness test
Software setting corrected by an update (e.g. Audi 3.0 TFSI)

symptoms: Possible P0305 or slight vibration at idle

P21A1.title: Cylinder 6 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A1.description: P21A1 marks cylinder 6, the last cylinder of an inline six or V6. The clearest example comes from the 2025 RAM 1500 with the 3.0 Hurricane twin-turbo inline six: the charge-air cooler housing had a loose crimp that let boost escape, the cylinders filled unevenly and P21A1 set together with other cylinder codes, accompanied by a whistle and lower boost; the cooler was inspected and replaced if needed. Toyota listed P219A, P219B and P219C to P21A1 for the 2015 Tacoma 1GR-FE and worked through a leak-down test to a valve job. Kia replaced high-pressure injectors and fuel lines on the 2022 Carnival 3.5 GDI, while Audi corrected a software setting on 2010 to 2012 3.0 TFSI models. A code for the last cylinder alone is no reason to suspect sensor or ECM before injector and compression are checked.

causes.label: Charge-air cooler or boost leak (turbo engines, e.g. RAM 3.0 Hurricane)
Faulty injector at cylinder 6
Valve leakage at cylinder 6
ECM software setting (e.g. Audi 3.0 TFSI)

symptoms: Whistling noise and reduced boost with a charge-air leak

P21A2.title: Cylinder 7 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A2.description: P21A2 places a mixture imbalance at cylinder 7, so it only exists on engines with eight or more cylinders. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the bulletin index of the US safety authority NHTSA contains no bulletin that names it. The requirement behind it is CARB's monitor for uneven mixture between cylinders (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)), which asks the code to identify the cause as far as the method allows. A V8 has four cylinders per front sensor, so the sensor signal alone separates them less clearly than on a four-cylinder; methods that work at the engine cycle frequency, as described in a Cummins patent, or VW's individual leaning test make cylinder-level codes possible. Check the cylinder 7 injector, its intake sealing and compression, and compare with misfire counts.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 injector clogged or leaking
Intake runner or injector seal leak at cylinder 7
Compression loss at cylinder 7

symptoms: Possible P0307 if the deviation is large

P21A3.title: Cylinder 8 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A3.description: P21A3 blames cylinder 8, on a V8 the last cylinder in the numbering. No manufacturer documentation of this code is publicly available, and no bulletin in the NHTSA index refers to it; the basis is the general CARB requirement for detecting cylinder imbalance, phased in for 2011 to 2014 model years with an emission threshold of 3.0 times the FTP standard (4.0 for SULEV II) until 2014 and 1.5 times from 2015. Whether cylinder 8 lies on bank 1 or bank 2 depends on the maker's numbering, which tells you whether P219A or P219B should accompany it. As Toyota and Lexus bulletins on cylinder codes show, leaking or restricted injectors, an intake leak at one runner and leaking valves are the usual causes. An injector balance test and a leak-down test on cylinder 8 come before any sensor work.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 injector out of tolerance
Valve leakage at cylinder 8
Intake leak at the cylinder 8 runner

symptoms: Possible P0308 with a strong deviation

P21A4.title: Cylinder 9 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A4.description: P21A4 is reserved for an imbalance at cylinder 9 and can therefore only appear on engines with ten or more cylinders, a small group of V10 and V12 petrol engines. No manufacturer documents the code publicly and no bulletin in the NHTSA index mentions it. CARB's rule (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)) still applies to these engines, and it allows a maker to store a bank code or even a misfire code instead when its hardware cannot single out a cylinder. With five or six cylinders feeding one front sensor, separating them needs extra effort, for example a frequency analysis tied to the engine cycle as in the Cummins patent, or an active test that changes the fuel of one cylinder at a time as VW does on its five-cylinder. Diagnosis follows the usual order: injector, intake sealing, compression of cylinder 9.

causes.label: Cylinder 9 injector clogged or leaking
Intake leak at cylinder 9
Compression loss at cylinder 9

symptoms: Possible P0309 with a large deviation

P21A5.title: Cylinder 10 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A5.description: P21A5 flags cylinder 10, which on a V10 is the final cylinder and on a V12 sits near the end of its bank. Public manufacturer material for this code does not exist, and the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry for it. CARB requires detection of any cylinder imbalance that lifts emissions above one and a half times the FTP limit (from 2015) and that the fault code point as precisely as the method allows; since a phase-in from 2019 to 2021, petrol vehicles must also log how often the check actually runs in daily use. Before chasing cylinder 10 specifically, confirm that the flagged number matches the manufacturer's numbering and that no other cylinder of the same bank also shows a misfire count or a deviating injector, because a correction on one cylinder can shift its neighbours. Then test the cylinder 10 injector and compression.

causes.label: Cylinder 10 injector out of tolerance
Fault in another cylinder of the same bank shifting the result
Compression loss at cylinder 10

P21A6.title: Cylinder 11 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A6.description: P21A6 assigns the imbalance to cylinder 11, which exists only on twelve-cylinder engines. No manufacturer has published how it detects this code, and no NHTSA bulletin names it, so it is a placeholder that J2012 provides for large engines. The legal frame is CARB's cylinder imbalance monitor (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)). A V12 or W12 feeds six cylinders into each front sensor, and exhaust pulses overlap, which makes a clean per-cylinder reading hard; the Cummins patent describes estimating the signal content at the engine cycle frequency and then trimming the fuel of the cylinder that causes it, an approach suited to many cylinders. In practice the work is mechanical: confirm the numbering, compare injector delivery across the bank and run a compression or leak-down test on cylinder 11.

causes.label: Cylinder 11 injector clogged or leaking
Valve leakage at cylinder 11
Intake leak at cylinder 11

symptoms: Possible P0311 with a large deviation

P21A7.title: Cylinder 12 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P21A7.description: P21A7 is the last code of the cylinder series that starts with P219C and points to cylinder 12 of a twelve-cylinder engine. There is no public manufacturer description and no NHTSA bulletin for it. Under CARB's rule (13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(6.2.1)(C)) the monitor had to be in all 2014 and later petrol vehicles, with limits of 3.0 times the FTP standard until 2014 and 1.5 times from 2015 for non-LEV III cars, so twelve-cylinder engines are covered as well; many simply report the bank code P219A or P219B. The causes do not differ from smaller engines: a single injector, a leaking intake seal or a valve that does not close properly. Because a V12 has two separate banks, check whether the bank code and the misfire counter P0312 agree with cylinder 12 before parts are replaced.

causes.label: Cylinder 12 injector out of tolerance
Intake seal leak at cylinder 12
Valve not sealing at cylinder 12

P21A8.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit
P21A8.description: P21A8 is the general circuit code for the second reductant level sensor, needed only where a DEF tank reports its fill level through more than one sensing element. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML/LGH) and the 2014 Cruze diesel read three discrete level sensors, numbered 1 to 3 in GM's tables, which corresponds to A to C. GM does not use P21A8 itself but splits the fault into P21AA (below 0.17 V after a test pulse) and P21AB (open load or short to battery). A maker using the umbrella code stores it for any wiring fault it cannot assign to one side. CARB requires such input circuits to be monitored (13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(15.2.1)). Expect a DEF warning message and, if left unrepaired, the usual SCR warning sequence.

causes.label: Damaged or corroded harness or connector at the DEF tank
Level sensor B in the tank assembly failed
Tank level evaluation electronics faulty

symptoms: DEF system warning message in the cluster
DEF level or range display missing or wrong

P21A9.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P21A9.description: P21A9 flags a level sensor B signal that stays inside its electrical limits but does not fit what else the system knows, such as the states of the other level sensors or the fluid consumed. GM's 2018 Cruze diesel (LH7) stores it in the module running the DEF system, under the name Level Sensor 2 Performance. Engineering bulletin PIE0453 asked dealers for freeze-frame data on ambient and fluid temperature, engine-off time and whether the car was parked outside, because the root cause was still unknown; cold soak is evidently under suspicion. On the 2014 Cruze GM still caught contradictory sensor states under P203B (5 s, Type B). Wiring faults of sensor B go to P21AA/P21AB. Drivers see the MIL and possibly a DEF message.

causes.label: Frozen or very cold fluid giving an implausible reading
Level sensor B fouled by crystallised urea or degraded
Control module calibration flagging the sensor too early

symptoms: DEF level shown wrongly or jumping
Fault appears mainly after cold nights

P21AA.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit Low
P21AA.description: P21AA means the second reductant level sensor reads too low a voltage, which GM takes as a short to ground. GM documents it for the 6.6L Duramax LML and the 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel: the tank level electronics apply a test pulse, and if sensor 2 then shows less than 0.17 V for more than 3 s with over 8 V supply, the ECM receives an error status over CAN. The LML treats it as Type A (MIL on the first trip), the Cruze as Type B (two trips). GM bulletin 12-06-04-002C lists P21AA among the DEF codes that must run and pass before the warning tests can clear the driver messages. Look for chafed or wet harness sections first; as the sensors belong to the tank assembly, a failed element usually means a new tank unit.

causes.label: Sensor 2 signal wire chafed through to ground
Fluid or water in the tank connector
Internal short in level sensor B (tank assembly)

symptoms: DEF warning message that stays on
DEF range or level display wrong

P21AB.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit High
P21AB.description: P21AB is the high-side counterpart: GM sets it when level sensor 2 shows an open load (between 3.56 and 4.74 V, read 1.5 ms after the test pulse) or a short to battery voltage (above 4.74 V), each for more than 3 s, as Type A on the 6.6L LML and the 2014 Cruze diesel. GM's preliminary bulletin PIP4887B for 2010–2011 Silverado, Sierra, Express and Savana with the LML or LGH engine names P21AB together with P203D and P21B0 and the message Service Exhaust Fluid System: inspect wiring, connectors and terminal tension also when the faults are merely stored, and replace the DEF tank only when the wiring is sound. For the 2011 model year GM sorted P21AB into its tamper-related group.

causes.label: Open signal wire or spread terminal at the tank connector
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
Level sensor B open inside the tank assembly

symptoms: Check engine light on at once
Several level sensor codes stored together

P21AC.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P21AC.description: P21AC reports that the level sensor B signal drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents criteria for this code publicly. GM's Duramax and Cruze diesel tables cover sensor 2 only with the steady faults P21AA and P21AB, both requiring an error lasting over 3 s, so an intermittent code points to contact losses shorter than that: a terminal that has lost its grip in the tank connector, a harness section that moves with the tank, or corrosion where fluid has crept in. GM's bulletin PIP4887B on related level sensor codes stresses checking terminal tension even when codes are only stored in history. CARB requires input circuits to be watched for such faults (13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(15.2.1)).

causes.label: Loose terminal in the tank connector
Harness flexing or rubbing near the tank mounting
Corrosion from fluid creeping into the connector

symptoms: DEF warning that comes and goes
Check engine light, sometimes only stored code

P21AD.title: Reductant Level Sensor C Circuit
P21AD.description: P21AD covers the electrical circuit of the third reductant level sensor, so it only exists on tanks with at least three level points. GM's 6.6L Duramax and 2014 Cruze diesel are such cases: the tank electronics test sensors 1 to 3 separately and pass each status to the ECM over CAN. GM uses the specific codes P21AF and P21B0 instead of this summary code. If P21AD shows up together with P21A8 and P203A, a shared supply, ground or the tank connector is far more likely than three failed sensors at once. Since the level information feeds the DEF range and refill warnings, drivers may see a missing or wrong range message besides the MIL. CARB asks for circuit monitoring of such inputs in 13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(15.2.1).

causes.label: Fault in a supply, ground or connector shared by the level sensors
Level sensor C in the tank assembly failed
Sensor C signal wire damaged

symptoms: DEF range message missing or implausible

P21AE.title: Reductant Level Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P21AE.description: P21AE stands for an implausible level sensor C signal whose voltage is still electrically valid. No manufacturer describes a separate check for this code in public material. GM shows how such plausibility testing can work: on the 2014 Cruze diesel the ECM compares the readings of all three discrete level sensors after the test pulse and flags combinations that cannot physically occur together, but files the result under P203B rather than under a code for the sensor concerned. For the 2018 Cruze, GM did assign P21A9 to sensor 2. A maker using P21AE would point to sensor C itself, for instance after urea crystal deposits or partial freezing. Electrical faults of this sensor are covered by P21AF and P21B0.

causes.label: Crystallised urea on level sensor C
Partly frozen fluid around the sensor
Level sensor C drifting or degraded

symptoms: DEF level display does not match the refill amount

P21AF.title: Reductant Level Sensor C Circuit Low
P21AF.description: P21AF is set when level sensor C, called level sensor 3 by GM, reads below 0.17 V right after the tank electronics apply their test pulse, which GM interprets as a short to ground. Supply must be above 8 V and the error must persist for more than 3 s. The 2014 Cruze diesel stores it as Type B, so the MIL lights after the second failing trip; on the 6.6L LML Duramax it appears in the same form, and GM bulletin 12-06-04-002C places it in the first group of DEF codes to be repaired before the warning tests can run again. When P203C or P21AA are present as well, several sensors reading low at once point to a common wiring or connector problem rather than to sensor 3 alone.

causes.label: Sensor 3 signal wire shorted to ground
Water or fluid bridging contacts in the tank connector
Level sensor C shorted inside the tank assembly

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips

P21B0.title: Reductant Level Sensor C Circuit High
P21B0.description: P21B0 means GM's level sensor 3 (sensor C) shows an open circuit or a short to battery: either 3.56 to 4.74 V or more than 4.74 V, measured 1.5 ms after a test pulse, for over 3 s. The 6.6L LML and the 2014 Cruze both rate it Type A, lighting the MIL on the first trip. PIP4887B names P21B0 next to P203D and P21AB on 2010–2011 Duramax trucks showing Service Exhaust Fluid System; when all three high codes appear together, GM directs technicians to wiring and terminal tension first and to the DEF tank assembly only afterwards. A tank connector left unplugged after other work would produce the same set of codes, so check that before ordering parts.

causes.label: Tank connector loose, unplugged or with spread terminals
Sensor 3 signal wire open or shorted to voltage
Level sensor C open inside the tank assembly

symptoms: Check engine light on at once
P203D and P21AB often stored as well

P21B1.title: Reductant Level Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P21B1.description: P21B1 marks level sensor C signals that come and go. Public manufacturer criteria do not exist; GM's diesel tables describe sensor 3 only through the steady faults P21AF and P21B0, each filtered over 3 s. A stored P21B1 therefore suggests interruptions too short for those monitors, typical of a connector that works loose under tank vibration, fluid seeping into the terminals, or a harness pinched under a tank strap. Moving the harness while watching the sensor data with a scan tool is the quickest way to reproduce it. If P21AC is present too, the cause probably lies in wiring both sensors share. Drivers mainly notice an unsteady DEF level display or a warning that appears and clears again.

causes.label: Tank connector loosening under vibration
Fluid seeping into the terminals
Harness pinched under a tank strap

symptoms: DEF warning that appears and clears

P21B2.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop NOx Adsorber Control
P21B2.description: P21B2 is set when the feedback control of a NOx adsorber (lean NOx trap) has not become active within the time the manufacturer allows once its enable conditions are met. CARB requires this check for vehicles with feedback control of the adsorber or its active injection (13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(8.2.3)(A)(i)). Cummins describes such a loop in patent US7594392: oxygen sensors before and after the adsorber, open-loop rich/lean cycling first, then a closed loop that holds the bed near 650 °C during regeneration. Ram 2500/3500 trucks with the 6.7L Cummins (2007–2011) carry a NOx absorber; Chrysler bulletin 25-001-13 links its P2000 to fouled oxygen sensors. No maker publishes criteria for P21B2; slow sensors or a cold exhaust are the usual suspects.

causes.label: Fouled or slow oxygen sensor before or after the adsorber
Exhaust not reaching control temperature (short trips, low load)
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensors
Exhaust temperature sensor reporting too low

symptoms: Regeneration of the NOx trap delayed or skipped
Higher NOx emissions, possible test failure

P21B3.title: Closed Loop NOx Adsorber Control At Limit - Too High
P21B3.description: P21B3 means the NOx adsorber feedback loop has reached its upper adjustment limit and still misses its target, the case CARB describes in 13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(8.2.3)(A)(iii). In practice the controller asks for more enrichment or longer rich phases than the calibration permits, because the downstream oxygen signal never shows the expected change or the bed stays below its target. Cummins patent US8065871 evaluates this upstream/downstream lambda difference to find the lean-to-rich transitions of the adsorber. Plausible reasons are a sulphur-loaded or aged adsorber, a lagging rear oxygen sensor, air leaks before the sensors, or fuel delivery that falls short. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P21B3; read it together with P2000 and oxygen sensor codes.

causes.label: NOx adsorber sulphur-loaded or thermally aged
Downstream oxygen sensor responding too slowly
Air leak in the exhaust ahead of the sensors
Too little fuel delivered for the rich phases

symptoms: Higher fuel consumption from long rich phases

P21B4.title: NOx Adsorber - Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P21B4.description: P21B4 reports that the NOx adsorber on bank 1 has run hotter than the manufacturer's protection limit. The risk is greatest during desulphation, when the adsorber is heated on purpose: Eaton patent US7251929 gives about 750 °C as the maximum desulphation temperature, beyond which the adsorber ages thermally, while Cummins aims for roughly 650 °C during regeneration (US7594392). Excess heat comes from too much fuel in rich phases, leaking injectors, unburnt fuel after misfires, or a temperature signal that reads wrong. No manufacturer documents its P21B4 limit publicly; the code can only occur on engines with such a catalyst, for instance the 2007–2011 Ram 6.7L Cummins. Act promptly: repeated overheating ruins the storage coating and leads to P2000.

causes.label: Too much fuel during regeneration or desulphation
Leaking or dribbling injector on bank 1
Misfire sending unburnt fuel into the exhaust
Exhaust temperature sensor reading too high

symptoms: Reduced power while the engine protects the catalyst
Strong smell or heat from the exhaust

P21B5.title: NOx Adsorber - Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P21B5.description: P21B5 is the bank 2 version of the adsorber over-temperature fault and therefore only exists where each cylinder bank feeds its own NOx storage catalyst, which in practice means V engines with two exhaust paths. If only bank 2 overheats, the cause most likely sits on that side: an injector delivering too much, misfire limited to that bank, or a faulty temperature sensor there. If P21B4 is stored as well, look instead for something both banks share, such as the regeneration strategy, fuel quality or a skewed air mass reading. Eaton patent US7251929 puts the ageing limit near 750 °C during desulphation. No manufacturer publishes its P21B5 limit; the duty to monitor adsorber performance comes from CARB (13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(8)). Driving on risks permanent damage.

causes.label: Injector on bank 2 delivering too much fuel
Misfire confined to bank 2
Regeneration overheating both banks (with P21B4)
Bank 2 exhaust temperature sensor reading too high

symptoms: Reduced power to protect the catalyst
Uneven exhaust temperatures between the banks

P21B6.title: Cold Start Cylinder 1 Injection Timing
P21B6.description: After a cold start, petrol direct-injection and diesel engines deliberately move the moment of injection – for example with an extra late pulse – so that more heat reaches the catalyst. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(11) wants every element of this strategy checked while it runs and reported apart from warm-engine faults. P21B6 pins such a deviation on cylinder 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM's 2025 diesel tables compare requested and scheduled start of injection on every cylinder but store only the system code P05EC. If cylinder 1 alone is flagged, a shared cause such as crank/cam synchronisation is unlikely; the injector, its wiring or its driver stage come first. Warm counterpart: P020A.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 1 responds late or inconsistently when cold
Corroded or loose connector or harness at injector 1
Injector driver stage in the engine control module faulty
Engine module software with an overly strict cold-start check

symptoms: Check engine light after one or more cold starts
Slightly rough idle in the first minute after a cold start
No noticeable fault once the engine is warm

P21B7.title: Cold Start Cylinder 2 Injection Timing
P21B7.description: P21B7 flags cylinder 2 during the cold-start phase only: the injection timing commanded for catalyst heating did not arrive as intended on that cylinder. The heating phase is brief and ends as coolant and catalyst warm up, so the monitor gets one chance per cold start and may need several cold starts before the code is confirmed. GM's 2025 diesel calibrations show the principle at system level: requested against scheduled start of injection, one sample per revolution, 88 failures out of 176 set P05EC with the lamp in the first trip. A cylinder-specific code like P21B7 appears in no public manufacturer document. If P020B (cylinder 2, warm) or P2B09 (cold-start pulse) are stored as well, the injector or its circuit is more likely than software.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 2 worn or coked, opening late at low temperature
Chafed or high-resistance wiring to injector 2
Weak battery lowering injector supply voltage during and after cranking

symptoms: Check engine light that appears only after cold starts
Uneven running or slight smoke shortly after starting a cold engine
Code may take several cold starts to return after clearing

P21B8.title: Cold Start Cylinder 3 Injection Timing
P21B8.description: Cylinder 3 is the last cylinder of three-cylinder engines such as Ford's 1.0-litre EcoBoost, a turbo direct-injection unit. There a single cylinder accounts for a third of all combustion events, so a cold-start fault on it tends to be felt more than on larger engines. P21B8 reports that while the cold-start heating strategy was active, the injection timing of cylinder 3 left its tolerance. The code belongs to a per-cylinder series made necessary by CARB's demand to keep cold-start faults apart from warm-running faults; no manufacturer documents its use publicly. On engines with four or more cylinders P21B8 simply marks cylinder 3. Neighbouring checks: P020C for the warm engine, P2B0A for the cold-start injection pulse, P0303 for misfire.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 3 with deposits or a weak coil
Moisture or corrosion in the plug of injector 3
Engine software update available for the cold-start calibration

symptoms: Noticeable shaking at cold idle, especially on three-cylinder engines
Check engine light after cold starts

P21B9.title: Cold Start Cylinder 4 Injection Timing
P21B9.description: Four-cylinder petrol direct injection is the most widespread engine type this code can apply to, and cylinder 4 is its last cylinder. Ford's 2011 OBD summary for its first turbo direct-injection engine explains the background: during catalyst heating the injection timing may be specific to that mode, possibly as two injections with one during the compression stroke, which in turn needs a rail pressure window (checked as P053F). P21B9 reports that this cold-start timing went wrong on cylinder 4 alone. No manufacturer lists the code publicly, so the description rests on CARB's cold-start rules and the documented system codes. Warm-engine counterpart: P020D; electrical injector fault: P0204; cold-start pulse: P2B0B.

causes.label: Deposits on the tip of injector 4 changing its opening behaviour
Harness fault on the injector 4 circuit
Rail pressure barely inside its window during cold start, affecting the last cylinder first

symptoms: Check engine light, usually without drivability complaints
Slightly longer catalyst warm-up and possibly higher cold-start emissions
Occasional hesitation right after a cold start

P21BA.title: Cold Start Cylinder 5 Injection Timing
P21BA.description: P21BA can only occur on engines with at least five cylinders – inline fives, V6, V8 and larger. GM's 4.3-litre V6 and 5.3/6.2-litre V8 direct-injection engines use a dual-pulse injection in open loop after a cold start; a GM bulletin explains that the module watches crankshaft speed in this mode and sets P050D (cold start rough idle) if it varies too much. A per-cylinder timing code such as P21BA goes a step further and names the cylinder whose cold-start injection timing missed its target. No manufacturer has published use of P21BA. On which bank cylinder 5 sits depends on the manufacturer's numbering, so check the engine's cylinder layout before testing. Related: P020E (warm), P2B0C (cold-start pulse), P0305.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 5 sticking or delivering late when cold
Repair on the wrong injector because of a misread cylinder numbering
Open or high-resistance circuit to injector 5

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
Rough idle during the first seconds after a cold start, possibly together with P050D

P21BB.title: Cold Start Cylinder 6 Injection Timing
P21BB.description: Cylinder 6 exists on six-cylinder engines and anything larger – inline sixes and V6 units such as Ford's 3.5-litre EcoBoost petrol or the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel in the Ram 1500. For that diesel FCA listed the warm-engine timing codes P020A–P020F together with the over-advanced and over-retarded codes in a 2021 bulletin whose fix was reprogramming the engine module. P21BB is the cold-start version for cylinder 6: during the heating phase after start, its injection timing did not match the target. Diesels adapt injection timing to coolant temperature after a cold start to hold emissions down before NOx sensors are working, as a GM patent describes. No manufacturer documents P21BB publicly; a software update is worth checking before replacing parts.

causes.label: Outdated engine module software (analogous timing codes were cured by reprogramming)
Injector of cylinder 6 worn, coked or with drifting opening delay
Damaged wiring or connector at injector 6

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
On diesels, more white smoke or knocking in the first minutes
Hard start or rough idle when cold

P21BC.title: Cold Start Cylinder 7 Injection Timing
P21BC.description: From cylinder 7 on, the code is limited to engines with at least seven cylinders – in practice V8, V10, V12 and W12. Common petrol V8 with direct injection are GM's 5.3- and 6.2-litre small blocks, which a GM bulletin describes with dual-pulse injection after a cold start, and Ford's 5.0-litre Coyote, which since 2018 combines port and direct injection. P21BC reports that during the cold-start heating phase the injection timing of cylinder 7 missed its target; on dual-system engines the direct injector is the part whose timing is shifted. No manufacturer publishes use of P21BC. If the code repeats on cylinder 7 only, test that injector cold and compare it with the others. Related: P021A (warm), P2B0E (cold-start pulse), P0207, P0307.

causes.label: Direct injector of cylinder 7 slow to open or leaking at low temperature
Chafed or heat-damaged wiring to injector 7
Fault in the high-voltage injector driver of the engine module

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
Rough cold idle, sometimes with P050D or a cylinder 7 misfire code

P21BD.title: Cold Start Cylinder 8 Injection Timing
P21BD.description: P21BD covers cylinder 8, the last cylinder of a V8. GM's 2025 diesel tables show how close an existing monitor comes to this code: during cold start the module compares requested and scheduled start of injection, with every cylinder from A to H included in the enable checks, and a deviation beyond ±4 in 88 of 176 samples sets the lamp in the first trip. Yet GM stores only the system code P05EC, which does not say which injector misbehaved. A per-cylinder code like P21BD would point straight at cylinder 8; no manufacturer documents its use publicly. GM's petrol V8 with direct injection likewise use a special dual-pulse cold-start mode. Related: P021B (warm), P2B0F (cold-start pulse), P0208, P0308.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 8 with slow or varying response
Connector or wiring fault at injector 8
Cold-start calibration in the engine module needing an update

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
Rough running or smoke in the first minute after a cold start

P21BE.title: Cold Start Cylinder 9 Injection Timing
P21BE.description: A ninth cylinder exists only on V10, V12 and W12 engines, so P21BE is limited to a handful of models. Petrol engines in this class with direct injection include the 5.2-litre V10 of Lamborghini and Audi (Huracán, R8, S6 and S8) and the 6.3-litre W12 FSI of the Audi A8, which feeds its injectors from two high-pressure pumps and two rails. Whether their engine modules use P21BE is not documented publicly, and no other manufacturer source names the code. Its meaning follows from the series: during the cold-start heating phase the injection timing of cylinder 9 deviated from its target, a fault CARB wants reported apart from warm-engine faults. There is no cold-start injection pulse code beyond cylinder 8. Related: P021C (warm), P0209, P0309.

causes.label: Direct injector of cylinder 9 with deposits or slow response
Low pressure on the rail feeding cylinder 9 (engines with two rails)
Wiring or connector fault at injector 9

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
Slightly uneven idle while the engine is cold

P21BF.title: Cold Start Cylinder 10 Injection Timing
P21BF.description: Cylinder 10 is the last cylinder of a V10 and exists otherwise only on twelve-cylinder engines. V10 engines are rare: Ford's 6.8-litre truck V10 (firing order 1-6-5-10-2-7-3-8-4-9, in the E-Series until 2019) and the 5.2-litre direct-injection V10 of Lamborghini and Audi. P21BF states that cylinder 10, during the cold-start heating phase, received its fuel at a different moment than targeted. No manufacturer documents the code publicly; the description rests on CARB's cold-start monitoring rules and on the system code P05EC, which GM checks across all cylinders of its diesels. If P021D (warm timing) or P0210 (injector circuit) are stored too, the cylinder 10 injector is the prime suspect; a cold-start pulse code does not exist for this cylinder.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 10 aged or contaminated
Wiring or connector problem at injector 10
Engine module software needing a cold-start calibration update

symptoms: Check engine light after one or more cold starts
Uneven idle until the engine warms up

P21C0.title: Cold Start Cylinder 11 Injection Timing
P21C0.description: P21C0 applies only to twelve-cylinder engines (V12 or W12), since passenger-car engines with exactly eleven cylinders do not exist. Examples with direct injection are BMW's N74 twin-turbo V12, found in the BMW 760i and in Rolls-Royce models such as Ghost, Wraith and Dawn, and the 6.3-litre W12 FSI. The code would report that cylinder 11 missed its cold-start injection timing, for instance when the extra injection for catalyst heating is shifted. Whether BMW, Rolls-Royce or Audi use P21C0 is not documented publicly. The legal basis is CARB's demand for separate cold-start diagnostics, allowing the module to tell such faults apart from warm-running timing faults (P021E). Related: P0211 (injector circuit), P0311 (misfire).

causes.label: Direct injector of cylinder 11 with changed opening behaviour
Heat-damaged wiring or connector at injector 11
Injector driver for cylinder 11 in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
Barely noticeable on the road; a twelve-cylinder engine masks a single cylinder well

P21C1.title: Cold Start Cylinder 12 Injection Timing
P21C1.description: Cylinder 12 is the last cylinder of V12 and W12 engines. Direct-injection V12 include Ferrari's F140 family (FF, F12berlinetta, 812 Superfast) and BMW's N74; among W engines there is the 6.3-litre W12 FSI. P21C1 reports that during the cold-start heating phase the injection timing of cylinder 12 deviated from its target. The code closes the series P21B6–P21C1, which exists because CARB requires cold-start faults to be kept apart from normal ones; the following code, P21C2, already belongs to the SCR reductant heater. No manufacturer publishes use of P21C1. Practical cross-checks: P021F (timing, warm engine), P0212 (injector circuit) and P0312 (misfire). Repairs on these engines are workshop jobs.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 12 with deposits or worn needle
Damaged wiring at the end of the cylinder bank (injector 12)
Cold-start calibration of the engine module out of date

symptoms: Check engine light after cold starts
Hardly any drivability change, at most a slightly uneven cold idle

P21C2.title: Reductant Heater Relay Control Circuit/Open
P21C2.description: P21C2 concerns the control line of the relay that supplies current to the DEF heaters. The control module drives the relay coil through an output stage and checks whether the circuit reacts; an open circuit means the coil, its wiring or a connector has lost continuity, so the heaters cannot be energised. Ford documents the code in its 2023 diesel summary: the check runs continuously while heating is requested, and with the relay stage on and every heater switched off, a heater current below 0.2 A sets P21C2 within at most 5 s. P21C3 and P21C4 are the low and high faults of the same line, P21C7 covers the power relay of the module itself. In frost the fluid may stay frozen, so dosing starts late and DEF warnings can follow.

causes.label: Relay coil burnt open or relay not seated in its socket
Broken control wire between module and relay
Corroded or loose terminals at relay box or module connector
Faulty output stage in the controlling module

symptoms: DEF system warning, especially at low ambient temperature
Frozen DEF thaws slowly, dosing begins late after a cold start

P21C3.title: Reductant Heater Relay Control Circuit Low
P21C3.description: P21C3 is the low-side fault on the control line of the DEF heater relay: the signal is pulled toward ground, for example by a chafed wire touching the frame or a shorted relay coil, so the relay no longer follows the command. Ford's 2023 diesel summary uses the same continuous check as for P21C2, but here the relay stage is on, every heater has been told to stay off, and still more than 6 A of heater current is measured; the fault is confirmed within 5 s. Such a reading means power reaches the heater circuit by a path the module never requested. Whether the heaters then stay dead or run without control depends on how the relay is wired. P21C2 is the open-circuit counterpart, P21C4 the high-side fault, P21C7 the module power relay.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Relay coil with internal short or welded contacts
Water or salt in the relay or heater connector
Output stage of the controlling module faulty

symptoms: DEF heating inactive or running when not commanded
Blown fuse in the heater supply

P21C4.title: Reductant Heater Relay Control Circuit High
P21C4.description: P21C4 means the control side of the DEF heater relay shows voltage when it should be dead. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it when the relay stage and all heaters are off and the heater circuit still carries more than 5 V, within at most 5 s; a short to the battery feed or contacts that no longer open are the classic reasons. FCA logs the code on Ram 2500 to 5500 trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins (2019 to 2024) with a title that names the line heater relay, often together with U11C1. Bulletin 25-008-24 traces this pairing to a replacement dosing control unit (68458603AB) and fixes it by reflashing; Stellantis case S1625000002 adds that new units ship without vehicle software and need programming. P21C2 and P21C3 cover the open and low faults.

causes.label: Replacement dosing control unit not programmed or with outdated software (FCA)
Control or heater wire shorted to battery voltage
Relay contacts welded closed
Internal fault in the controlling module

symptoms: Code appears shortly after a DEF control unit was replaced
Additional communication code such as U11C1 stored

P21C5.title: Reductant Level Sensor A Stuck
P21C5.description: P21C5 is a plausibility code: the level sensor A reports valid readings, yet they hardly move when the fluid in the tank should be sloshing. GM spells this out for the ultrasonic sensor in its 2025 diesel tables, where it is sensor 1. While the vehicle is above 5 km/h, accelerating by more than 0.1 m/s², the fluid is liquid and over 5 L remain, a level change below 0.3 mm within one second counts as a failed sample; after about 200 s of such samples the module sets the code as Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips. Jaguar issued SSM73632 for the 2017 to 2018 F-Pace with P21C5-64 and blamed a level sensor calibration, fixed by new engine software. Electrical faults of the same sensor are P203A to P203E, sensor B stuck is P21C6.

causes.label: Level sensor calibration in the engine software (update available, e.g. Jaguar)
Ultrasonic level sensor in the tank unit faulty
Crystal deposits or gas bubbles disturbing the echo
Fluid partly frozen or slush around the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on after two drives
DEF gauge stays at the same value while fluid is being used
DEF warning messages in the instrument cluster

P21C6.title: Reductant Level Sensor B Stuck
P21C6.description: P21C6 applies only to DEF tanks with a second level measurement, labelled B. It is stored when that second reading is electrically fine but stays frozen at one value although the module expects it to change. No manufacturer documents P21C6 publicly. GM's 2025 diesel tables show how such a check works for sensor 1 (P21C5): during driving with noticeable acceleration and liquid fluid, a level change of less than 0.3 mm per second over roughly 200 s is judged as stuck. Older GM tanks with three discrete level contacts would equate B with contact 2, but GM covers that one only with circuit codes P21AA and P21AB. CARB demands rationality checks for such inputs. Wiring faults of sensor B are P21A8 to P21AC; an untrustworthy level can trigger DEF warnings.

causes.label: Second level sensing element in the tank unit faulty
Float or contact held by crystals or debris
Calibration of the level evaluation needs a software update

symptoms: DEF gauge implausible or not moving
DEF warning in the instrument cluster

P21C7.title: Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit/Open
P21C7.description: P21C7 flags a break in the control line of the power relay, or group of relays, that supplies the DEF control module and the loads behind it. Ford's 2023 diesel summary evaluates it inside the same continuous heater relay check as P21C2 to P21C4, so on that design the relay also feeds the heating circuits. The code sets within 5 s if the output stage is on but the heater supply reads 0 V, or if the stage is off and voltage is still present, meaning the commanded and the actual relay state disagree. Without supply, DEF heating and possibly dosing stop, and SCR warnings follow. P21C8 and P21C9 are the low and high faults of this line; P20EA and P20EB judge when the relay drops out after the key is turned off.

causes.label: Relay defective or missing from its socket
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Blown fuse in the relay or module feed
Driver in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: DEF heating and dosing do not work
SCR warning and countdown to restricted starting or speed

P21C8.title: Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit Low
P21C8.description: P21C8 means the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, sits too close to ground. No manufacturer documents P21C8 publicly. Ford's 2023 diesel summary only shows the open-circuit sibling P21C7, judged by comparing the commanded relay state with the voltage on the switched side; a low-side code follows the same idea with a pin voltage below the expected window. What a short to ground does depends on the driver: if the module switches the coil on its ground side, the relay may stay energised and drain the battery after switch-off; if it switches the supply side, the relay never pulls in and the SCR system loses power. The engine module pair P0685/P0686 is the closest analogy. P21C9 is the high-side fault.

causes.label: Control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Shorted relay coil
Moisture in relay socket or module connector
Output stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: DEF system without power or permanently powered
Flat battery after the vehicle has been parked

P21C9.title: Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit High
P21C9.description: P21C9 is stored when the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, carries more voltage than the driver state allows, typically because the wire touches a battery feed or the driver can no longer pull it down. No manufacturer documents P21C9 publicly. The closest published logic is Ford's 2023 diesel summary for P21C7, which flags voltage on the switched side while the output stage is off; a high-side code adds the specific diagnosis of a short to supply on the control pin. Depending on the driver layout the relay then either never releases, keeping pump and heaters live with the engine off, or never closes. P0687 is the equivalent code for the engine module relay, and a late drop-out after key-off is reported as P20EB.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage circuit
Relay contacts welded, switched side stays live
Driver in the controlling module shorted

symptoms: DEF pump or module audible or active with the engine off

P21CA.title: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage Circuit
P21CA.description: P21CA is the general code for the supply feed of the DEF control module: the voltage arriving at the module is missing or unusable, without the module assigning it to the low or high case. Volvo and Mack trucks use it, as P21CA00, on the aftertreatment control module that runs the SCR system. Volvo article KC-2040 describes a typical pattern: a battery or ground connection slowly loosens, the module voltage sinks below about 8 V, the module cuts power to the NOx, particulate and DEF sensors, communication codes such as U029D and U02A2 follow, and the truck enters SCR inducement and derate. Volvo stresses that this rarely means a bad module and first checks terminals, batteries, charging and the in-line fuse. P21CB and P21CC are the specific low and high codes.

causes.label: Loose or corroded battery or ground connections of the module
Weak batteries or insufficient charging voltage
Faulty in-line fuse or damaged supply wire
Control module itself faulty

symptoms: Several sensor communication codes at the same time

P21CB.title: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage Low
P21CB.description: P21CB says the DEF control module receives too little supply voltage. GM measures it as a difference to system voltage: in the 2018 diesel tables a gap above 3 V between battery voltage and the supply of the SCR power module, seen in 40 of 50 samples taken every 100 ms with the powertrain relay in range and cranking excluded, sets the code; the 2025 tables apply the same 3 V gap to the permanent DEF supply against the gateway voltage for 3 s and classify it as Type B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary uses an absolute limit for its reductant pump controller, below 8.5 V within 5 s. Causes lie between battery and module: resistance in fuses, terminals or ground. P21CA is the umbrella code, P21CC the overvoltage case.

causes.label: Voltage drop at fuse, terminal or ground of the module feed
Weak battery or low charging voltage
Damaged or corroded supply wire to the module
Internal voltage measurement of the module faulty

symptoms: DEF dosing or heating drops out intermittently
Further undervoltage or communication codes from the SCR system

P21CC.title: Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage High
P21CC.description: P21CC is the overvoltage counterpart of P21CB: the DEF control module sees a supply above what its electronics are designed for. Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant pump controller in a continuous loop and sets P21CC once its supply exceeds 19 V, deciding within 5 s. On a 12 V vehicle such values usually come from a charging system whose regulator has failed, from a jump start with a 24 V source, or from load dumps on a loose battery terminal; less often the module measures its own input wrongly. To protect pump and heaters the module usually stops working, so dosing pauses. GM's published diesel tables list only the low case. P21CA is the general supply code, and P0563 shows whether the engine module sees the same excess.

causes.label: Alternator voltage regulator overcharging
Jump start or charging with excessive voltage
Loose battery terminal causing voltage spikes
Module's own voltage measurement faulty

symptoms: Battery or charging warning, bulbs unusually bright

P21CD.title: Reductant Quality Module Supply Voltage Low
P21CD.description: The DEF quality module measures the urea concentration in the tank and, on many tanks, shares a housing with the level sensor. P21CD reports that its supply voltage is too low. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets the code when the quality sensor supply falls below 10 V or rises above 20 V for 15 s, so on Ford the overvoltage case shares this code. Ford bulletin 19-2315 covers 2017 to 2019 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L diesel built up to 1 August 2018: water enters the four-pin connector C4851 at the level and quality module, corroding pins 1 and 4, and P21CD appears together with U02A2. The fix is a new tank harness, sometimes the tank. Without a valid quality reading the SCR system cannot verify the fluid, and P206B to P206D cannot run.

causes.label: Water and corrosion in the quality module connector (Ford C4851)
Damaged tank harness or supply wire
Low battery or charging voltage
Quality module internally faulty

symptoms: DEF quality or level warning in the instrument cluster
Communication code for the quality module stored as well

P21CE.title: Reductant Quality Module Performance
P21CE.description: P21CE says the DEF quality module as a unit is not working properly: it is supplied and talking to the controller, but its self-test or the plausibility of its output fails, so the controller cannot rely on the concentration it reports. This differs from P206B to P206D, which grade the measured concentration, and from P21CD, which concerns the module supply. Nissan uses P21CE on the 2019 Titan XD with the Cummins 5.0 L V8, often with P1349 for an erratic tank level, and a DEF system message may appear. Bulletin NTB20-005 has the technician follow the normal diagnosis and, if it leads to part replacement, first drain the tank and refill it with fresh fluid, reinstalling the pump with a new seal. Ford's 2023 diesel summary reports an internal quality sensor error as P206B instead.

causes.label: Contaminated or degraded DEF disturbing the measurement
Quality module internally faulty
Crystals or air bubbles on the sensing element
Poor contact at the module connector

symptoms: DEF system error message in the display

P21CF.title: Cylinder 1 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21CF.description: P21CF flags an open drive circuit of the second injector on cylinder 1. Which of the two injectors is B depends on the maker: Ford gives the letter to the port injector and keeps A, coded P0201, for direct injection, whereas Mitsubishi calls its direct injectors B and files open circuits under the low code P21DB. Ford's 2020 to 2025 gasoline summaries test the B circuits continuously above 11 V and need 5 s. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 judges it in a separate injection module: over 200 kOhm on the switched-off low side in 20 of 25 samples, Type A with the MIL in the first trip. Ford bulletin SSM 49996 lists it with P21D0 and P21D1 on 2021 Bronco Sport 1.5 models with a harness damaged at the transmission. With direct injection still working, rough idle or P0301 is the usual sign.

causes.label: Chafed or broken wire in the port injector harness (on the Bronco Sport near the transmission cover)
Open coil in the cylinder 1 port injector
Loose or corroded plug at the injector
Faulty driver stage in the engine module or separate injector module

symptoms: Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 1, often with P0301
Further harness codes stored at the same time

P21D0.title: Cylinder 2 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D0.description: P21D0 is the open-circuit code for the B injector of cylinder 2. Where that cylinder sits varies: GM's small-block V8 alternates odd and even numbers between the banks, so cylinder 2 opens the right bank, while Ford's V6 and V8 count one bank first and place it next to cylinder 1. Ford defines B as the port injector, the direct injector being A with P0202. Ford runs the check in every engine with combined port and direct injection, from the three-cylinder 1.5 to the 5.0 V8, continuously at 11 V or more for 5 s. GM's LT5 injection module samples the circuit every 100 ms once the powertrain relay supplies at least 11 V. On engines that run on port fuel alone at light load, like Ford's second 3.5 EcoBoost, the cylinder then misfires mostly at idle. Low and high faults are P21DE and P21DF.

causes.label: Port injector of cylinder 2 with an open winding
Broken wire or pushed-back terminal in the injector harness
Output stage in the engine or injection module failed

symptoms: Misfire on cylinder 2, mainly at idle and light load

P21D1.title: Cylinder 3 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D1.description: P21D1 concerns the B injector of cylinder 3, which on Ford's 1.5 EcoBoost three-cylinder is the last one in the block. That engine combines port and direct fuel, and Ford names the port injectors B. Bulletin SSM 49996 for the 2021 Bronco Sport describes P21CF, P21D0 and P21D1 appearing together with transmission and other codes, in some cases with a no-crank condition, because the harness was damaged at the transmission cover; when all three B codes show at once, a shared wiring fault is far more likely than three bad injectors. Ford's summary checks the B circuits continuously above 11 V within 5 s. GM's LT5 V8 module flags an open low side once 20 of 25 samples fail. The direct injector of the cylinder is coded P0203.

causes.label: Harness damage affecting several injectors at once (Ford Bronco Sport, transmission cover)
Open coil in the cylinder 3 port injector
Connector not latched or corroded

symptoms: Rough running or misfire on cylinder 3
With harness damage also transmission codes or no crank

P21D2.title: Cylinder 4 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D2.description: P21D2 reports an open in the drive circuit of the B injector on cylinder 4. On four-cylinder engines with dual injection it is the last of the set, for example Ford's 2.0 EcoBoost from 2022 or the 2.3 introduced for the 2024 Mustang, both of which added port injectors to direct injection. Ford tests it like its siblings, continuously with at least 11 V and a 5 s window, and assigns letter A to the direct injector (P0204). Mitsubishi, whose Eclipse Cross uses B for the direct injectors, has no open code here and files such faults under the low code P21E2. On Ford's 3.5 V6 cylinder 4 opens the second bank. In GM's 2019 LT5 module the check samples every 100 ms. Expect a misfire on cylinder 4.

causes.label: Open winding in the cylinder 4 port injector
Wire broken at a bend or clip near the intake manifold
Corroded or loose injector connector

P21D3.title: Cylinder 5 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D3.description: P21D3 can only appear on engines with at least five cylinders and two injectors per cylinder. Documented users are Ford's dual-injection V6 and V8 engines (2.7 and 3.5 EcoBoost of the second generation, 5.0 V8 from 2018) and GM's supercharged LT5 V8. Ford defines B as the port injector; the direct injector of this cylinder is A, coded P0205. GM stores it as Type A once 20 of 25 samples fail. Ford's check is continuous above 11 V with a 5 s window. GM's LT5 injection module rates an open by the impedance seen with the driver off, 200 kOhm or more. On a V6 one bank then runs with a single weak cylinder, which fuel trims and misfire counters can reveal.

causes.label: Open coil in the cylinder 5 port injector
Broken wire in the bank harness of the port injectors
Output stage in the engine or injection module failed

symptoms: Fuel trim of one bank shifted

P21D4.title: Cylinder 6 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D4.description: P21D4 is the last B injector code on a six-cylinder engine. Ford's second-generation 2.7 and 3.5 EcoBoost V6 combine port and direct injection, label the port injectors B and test this circuit together with P21CF to P21D3, continuously above 11 V within 5 s; on these engines cylinder 6 is the rear cylinder of the second bank. On the 3.5 the direct system is shut down at low speed and light load and the engine runs on port fuel alone, so an open cylinder 6 port injector is most noticeable at idle and in gentle driving. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 also covers cylinder 6 in its injection module, Type A after 20 of 25 failed samples. The A-side direct injector code is P0206, the misfire code P0306; P21E6 and P21E7 are the low and high faults.

causes.label: Port injector of cylinder 6 open internally
Damaged wire at the rear of the engine, hard to inspect
Connector not fully latched after earlier work on the intake

P21D5.title: Cylinder 7 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D5.description: P21D5 belongs to V8 engines with a second injector per cylinder. Two are documented: Ford's 5.0 V8, which gained direct injection alongside its port injectors in 2018, and GM's 2019 LT5, the supercharged Corvette ZR1 engine with primary direct and supplemental port injection. Ford's summary lists P21CF to P21D6 as port injector circuits, continuous above 11 V, 5 s. On the LT5 the B injectors hang on a separate injection module whose low-side driver flags an open at 200 kOhm or more with the output off, in 20 of 25 samples at 100 ms, Type A with MIL in one trip. Ford counts its V8 one bank after the other, so cylinder 7 lies on the second bank; GM alternates banks, making 7 the last cylinder on the left. The A-side code for cylinder 7 is P0207, the misfire code P0307.

causes.label: Open winding in the cylinder 7 port injector
Broken wire or terminal in the port injector harness of that bank
Separate fuel injection control module faulty (GM LT5)

symptoms: Misfire on cylinder 7, on the LT5 mostly under high load

P21D6.title: Cylinder 8 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D6.description: P21D6 is the highest B injector code that any manufacturer documents publicly: both Ford's port injector check (P21CF to P21D6) and GM's LT5 injection module list end here. On the LT5 the port injectors exist to add fuel under boost beyond what the direct system and its mechanical pump can deliver, so an open cylinder 8 injector shows up mainly at high load, where that cylinder can run lean and lose power; GM stores the fault as Type A from 20 failed samples out of 25 with at least 11 V on the powertrain relay. In GM's firing order cylinder 8 follows cylinder 1. On Ford's 5.0 V8 from 2018 it is the rear cylinder of the second bank and the check runs continuously for 5 s. The direct injector counterpart is P0208; P21D5 is cylinder 7.

causes.label: Port injector of cylinder 8 open
Wire damage at the rear of the engine near the firewall
Output of the engine or separate injection module failed

symptoms: Misfire or lean running on cylinder 8 under load

P21D7.title: Cylinder 9 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D7.description: P21D7 would mark an open drive circuit of the second injector on cylinder 9, which presupposes at least nine cylinders. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the published Ford and GM lists stop at cylinder 8 (P21D6). Engines with that many cylinders and two injection systems do exist, for example the V10 of the Lamborghini Huracán, which pairs direct with multipoint injection, but no source shows how its maker labels the two injectors. CARB requires that electrical output components such as fuel injectors be checked for circuit faults, so the logic would follow the documented siblings: a missing current or excessive impedance when the injector is switched. The direct injector of cylinder 9 would carry P0209 if it is the A side. A misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309) is the likely accompanying symptom.

causes.label: Open coil in the second injector of cylinder 9
Broken wire or terminal in the injector harness
Driver stage in the engine control module failed

P21D8.title: Cylinder 10 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D8.description: P21D8 covers the second injector of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A V10 with two injectors per cylinder is on record in the Lamborghini Huracán, whose engine combines direct and multipoint injection, yet which of them its software would call B is unknown. For comparison, Ford's eight-cylinder logic tests B circuits continuously above 11 V for 5 s, and GM's LT5 module rates an open by 200 kOhm or more with the driver off. CARB obliges makers to monitor injector output circuits whose failure can raise emissions. In practice the fault would show as a misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310) with that cylinder still fed by its other injector; the A-side equivalent would be P020A. Neighbours are P21D7 and P21D9.

causes.label: Second injector of cylinder 10 open internally
Wiring or connector fault at the cylinder 10 injector
Output stage in the engine control module failed

P21D9.title: Cylinder 11 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21D9.description: P21D9 is reserved for an open circuit of the second injector on cylinder 11 and therefore only makes sense on twelve-cylinder engines with dual injection. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no available source names a twelve-cylinder engine that uses it. Its meaning follows from the series: like P21CF to P21D6, it is an electrical check of the injector drive, not of fuel quantity. CARB requires such circuit monitoring for injectors whose failure affects emissions; Ford's documented B-injector check for up to eight cylinders runs continuously above 11 V and needs 5 s, which shows the typical scale. If it ever appears, check the injector coil resistance and the harness first. The direct counterpart in the A series is P020B, the misfire code for cylinder 11 is P0311.

causes.label: Open coil in the second injector of cylinder 11
Damaged injector harness or loose plug
Faulty driver in the engine control module

P21DA.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Circuit/Open
P21DA.description: P21DA closes the circuit/open series of the second injectors with cylinder 12. It requires a twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder; no manufacturer documents this code publicly and no available source names such an engine using it. The fault type is the same as for its documented siblings: the control unit switches the injector and sees no current or an impedance far above normal. GM's LT5 injection module, for example, treats 200 kOhm or more as open and stores a Type A fault after 20 of 25 samples. CARB demands this kind of electrical monitoring for injectors. Directly after this code the series continues with the low and high faults P21DB and P21DC for cylinder 1; the A-side open code for cylinder 12 is P020C, the misfire code P0312.

causes.label: Second injector of cylinder 12 with open coil
Wire or terminal fault in the injector harness
Output stage of the controlling module failed

P21DB.title: Cylinder 1 Injector B Circuit Low
P21DB.description: P21DB means the drive circuit of the B injector on cylinder 1 is pulled toward ground. Two makers document it, with opposite meanings of B. Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross uses B for the direct high-pressure injector (its port injector faults are P0261 ff.) and sets P21DB when an interruption or a grounded line persists for 2 s with 10 to 16.5 V battery and over 10 V on the injector driver supply. One faulty cylinder loses both its injectors; with several faults direct injection is switched off and the engine runs on port injection with limited torque. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 tests the low side of its supplemental B injector with the driver off: below 0.5 Ohm to ground in 20 of 25 samples, Type A. Ford covers B faults only with P21CF to P21D6, opens and shorts together. P21DC is the high counterpart, P21CF the open circuit.

causes.label: Injector wire chafed through to ground
Injector winding open or shorted to its housing
Damaged intermediate or injector connector
Engine or injection control module faulty

symptoms: Reduced torque when several cylinders are affected (Mitsubishi)

P21DC.title: Cylinder 1 Injector B Circuit High
P21DC.description: P21DC is the high-side fault of the cylinder 1 B injector: the line carries voltage where the control unit expects it to be low, typically from a short to supply or between the two injector wires. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 the FICM injection module looks at the low side of the supplemental injector while its driver is off; less than 0.5 Ohm toward power in 20 of 25 samples sets a Type A fault, so that injector can no longer be switched.
