Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross, where B is the direct high-pressure injector, needs a short circuit lasting 2 s and begins diagnosis on the negative DI line. Its manual warns against measuring the injector terminals, because the direct injection driver works with high voltage. Fail-safe, symptoms and codes P21DB (low) and P21CF (open) are closely linked.

causes.label: Injector control wire shorted to a supply wire
Both injector wires shorted together in the harness
Injector coil shorted internally
Driver stage of the control module damaged

symptoms: Torque limited if more cylinders fail (Mitsubishi)

P21DD.title: Reductant Heater A Current Too Low
P21DD.description: P21DD means heater A of the DEF system, which Ford and GM both assign to the tank heater (circuit 1), draws less current than expected while switched on, so it is likely open or barely heating. GM's 2025 diesel tables set it when heater 1 current stays below 0.75 A for 40 samples of 0.1 s during a positive command, Type A with MIL after one trip; the 2014 tables flagged an open tank heater when its conductance fell to 0.27 or 0.35 S (by table) or less at 11 V or more, evaluated a single time per drive, Type B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary tests once per heating cycle after a cold start: below 3 A or too little heater power. Ford bulletin 19-2315 links P21DD on 2017 to 2019 Super Duty 6.7 L trucks to water in connector C3613 at the pump and heater unit. P214F is the high-current partner.

causes.label: Tank heater element burnt open
Water and corrosion in the pump and heater connector (Ford C3613)
Missing heater supply due to relay, fuse or wiring fault
Heater driver in the control module faulty

symptoms: DEF stays frozen longer in winter, dosing starts late
DEF warning messages after cold starts

P21DE.title: Cylinder 2 Injector B Circuit Low
P21DE.description: P21DE is the low fault of the cylinder 2 B injector circuit. In Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross manual, B means the direct injector; the code covers both a break and a grounded wire on the two DI lines of cylinder 2, held for 2 s at 10 to 16.5 V, while the port injector of the same cylinder reports P0264. Diagnosis starts with the coil resistance at the intermediate connector, which should be 1.74 to 2.04 Ohm at 20 °C. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 cylinder 2 is the front cylinder of the right bank; there a low side shorted to ground on the supplemental injector, below 0.5 Ohm, sets a Type A fault from its separate module. GM runs this check while the driver is switched off; a grounded low side can energise the injector without a command. P21DF is the high fault, P21D0 the open.

causes.label: Injector line of cylinder 2 touching ground
Injector coil resistance outside specification
Fault at the intermediate connector of the injector harness

symptoms: Possible fuel smell or rich running if an injector stays open

P21DF.title: Cylinder 2 Injector B Circuit High
P21DF.description: P21DF is set when the cylinder 2 B injector circuit shows a short toward supply. Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross applies it to the direct high-pressure injector and stores it after a 2 s short with the ignition on and the driver supply above 10 V; troubleshooting first inspects the negative DI wire of cylinder 2 up to the engine module and names the injector, the harness and the ECM as possible causes. The fail-safe is graded: with one cylinder affected, both injectors of that cylinder stop; with several, the engine falls back to port injection and torque is limited. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 judges the same title on its supplemental injector by less than 0.5 Ohm toward power on the low side, Type A. The port injector high code of this Mitsubishi cylinder would be P0265; P21DE is the low fault.

causes.label: Negative injector line of cylinder 2 shorted to supply
Injector coil shorted
ECM or injection module driver defective

symptoms: Less pulling power with multiple faults

P21E0.title: Cylinder 3 Injector B Circuit Low
P21E0.description: P21E0 reports a low circuit state on the B injector of cylinder 3. Mitsubishi lists it for the 2022 Eclipse Cross as the direct injector code and does not use the open code P21D1, so an interrupted wire and a short to ground both end up here once they last 2 s. Its procedure measures the injector across its two DI terminals at the intermediate connector, then the harness on both sides of that connector, and only then suspects the ECM. Port injector faults on the same cylinder are P0267 and P0268. On GM's 2019 LT5 V8 cylinder 3 is the second cylinder on the left bank; its supplemental injector fails this test with less than 0.5 Ohm between low side and ground in 20 of 25 samples while the driver is off, Type A in one trip. Expect a cylinder 3 misfire; P21E1 is the high fault.

causes.label: Cylinder 3 injector wire broken or shorted to ground
Injector of cylinder 3 with open or shorted coil
Engine control module output faulty

P21E1.title: Cylinder 3 Injector B Circuit High
P21E1.description: P21E1 is the high fault on the cylinder 3 B injector circuit. In Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross that is the direct high-pressure injector, and the module reacts to a short circuit lasting 2 s, checked with 10 to 16.5 V battery voltage. To confirm a repair, the manual points to its OBD drive cycle pattern 1. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 monitors the low side of the supplemental cylinder 3 injector in its separate FICM module and flags under 0.5 Ohm toward power as Type A with the MIL in the first trip. A short to power keeps the low side from ever reaching ground, so the injector cannot open, and switching against the short can strain the driver stage. P21E0 covers the low fault and P0268 the port injector high fault on Mitsubishi; a cylinder 3 misfire often follows.

causes.label: Cylinder 3 injector line shorted to supply voltage
Shorted injector coil
Damaged driver in the control module

symptoms: Torque reduction if several injectors fail (Mitsubishi)

P21E2.title: Cylinder 4 Injector B Circuit Low
P21E2.description: P21E2 is the low fault of the B injector on cylinder 4, the last cylinder of an inline four. It is the final direct injector low code in Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross list, which uses B for the high-pressure injectors and sets it for an open or a short to ground lasting 2 s. If the engine has lost injectors on more than one cylinder, the control unit stops direct injection completely and limits torque, so a P21E2 stored together with other P21DB-series codes points to a shared cause such as the intermediate connector or the driver supply. The cylinder 4 port injector reports P0270 and P0271. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 uses P21E2 for the right-bank cylinder 4 supplemental injector, rating a low side under 0.5 Ohm to ground as Type A. P21E3 is the high fault.

causes.label: Cylinder 4 injector wire open or shorted to ground
Intermediate connector fault affecting several cylinders
Cylinder 4 injector coil defective

symptoms: Noticeably less power with several codes (port injection only)

P21E3.title: Cylinder 4 Injector B Circuit High
P21E3.description: P21E3 marks a high circuit state on the cylinder 4 B injector, normally a short to a supply line. On Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross, where B is the direct high-pressure injector, the fault must persist 2 s; it closes the manual's list of direct injector circuit codes for the four cylinders. Because the direct injector driver uses boosted voltage, Mitsubishi tells technicians not to probe the terminals with a voltmeter and to work with resistance and continuity checks instead. GM's 2019 LT5 V8 assigns the same code to the supplemental injector of cylinder 4, stored as Type A when the low side sits within 0.5 Ohm of power with the driver off. The low counterpart is P21E2, the port injector high code on Mitsubishi P0271; from P21E4 on, the series continues with cylinder 5.

causes.label: Cylinder 4 injector line shorted to a supply wire
Injector of cylinder 4 shorted internally
Driver stage in the ECM or injection module damaged

symptoms: Engine runs with reduced torque if further cylinders are affected

P21E4.title: Cylinder 5 Injector B Circuit Low
P21E4.description: P21E4 flags a low state on the circuit of the second (B) injector serving cylinder 5. The only public OBD summary that lists it is GM's for the 2019 Corvette ZR1, whose supercharged LT5 V8 pairs direct injectors with port injectors and drives the supplemental ones from a separate fuel injection control module (FICM). While that driver is off, a low side reading 0.5 Ohm or less toward ground in 20 of 25 samples, taken every 100 ms, is judged a short and becomes a Type A fault with the MIL in the first trip. On GM's V8 numbering cylinder 5 is the third cylinder of the left bank, i.e. bank 1. Because a grounded low side can let the injector flow uncommanded, a rich bank 1 may follow. Ford's dual-injection engines report B shorts on this cylinder only as P21D3.

causes.label: Low-side wire of the cylinder 5 B injector touching ground
Injector winding shorted to its housing
Moisture or corrosion in the injector connector
Driver stage in the injection control module faulty

symptoms: Rich running or fuel trim pulled back on bank 1
Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 5

P21E5.title: Cylinder 5 Injector B Circuit High
P21E5.description: P21E5 means the cylinder 5 B injector circuit is pulled toward supply voltage. GM documents it for the LT5 V8 of the 2019 Corvette ZR1: the FICM looks at the low side of that injector while its driver is off and treats 0.5 Ohm or less toward power as a short. The test needs a running engine and at least 11 V at the powertrain relay, runs continuously and sets a Type A fault. A low side held at supply potential can never be switched to ground, so the injector stays closed. On this engine the port injectors were added mainly to supply extra fuel under boost, so a dead unit tends to show at high load, where cylinder 5 may run lean. The low-side counterpart is P21E4; the A injector of the same cylinder reports P0274 for the same fault type.

causes.label: Low-side wire of the cylinder 5 B injector shorted to a supply wire
Supply and control wire of the injector bridged in the harness
Injector coil shorted across its terminals
Damaged output stage in the injection control module

symptoms: Cylinder 5 lean or hesitant at full load

P21E6.title: Cylinder 6 Injector B Circuit Low
P21E6.description: P21E6 reports that the B injector circuit of cylinder 6 has found a path to ground. In GM's 2019 tables for the Corvette ZR1 LT5, cylinder 6 is the third position on the right bank, which GM counts as bank 2. The FICM samples the switched-off low side every 100 ms and needs 20 bad readings out of 25, so a solid fault is confirmed within about two and a half seconds; the limit is 0.5 Ohm or less toward ground, Type A. A ground on the low side completes the injector circuit whenever its feed is live, so fuel can enter cylinder 6 without a command. Typical traces are a rich bank 2, fuel-wetted spark plug on that cylinder and fuel trims at their lean limit. P21E7 is the high fault of the same injector, P0276 the low fault of the A injector.

causes.label: Cylinder 6 B injector harness chafed against engine metal
Internal short to ground inside the injector
Injection control module output stuck low

symptoms: Rich condition on bank 2, possibly fuel smell
Fouled spark plug or misfire on cylinder 6

P21E7.title: Cylinder 6 Injector B Circuit High
P21E7.description: P21E7 is stored when the B injector of cylinder 6 shows a short toward power. GM's 2019 Corvette ZR1 with the LT5 V8 is the documented user; there the FICM checks the low side only in the driver-off state, flags 0.5 Ohm or less to power, and needs at least 11 V at the powertrain relay with the engine running. The result is a Type A fault after one trip. With the low side tied to supply, every switching attempt would push current straight into the driver, so the injector on the right-bank cylinder 6 delivers nothing. A useful check is to unplug the injector: if the voltage on the control wire stays, the harness is at fault; if it disappears, the injector coil is suspect. P21E6 is the matching low fault and P0277 the A injector high code.

causes.label: Cylinder 6 B injector control wire in contact with a live wire
Shorted turns in the injector coil
Output stage of the injection control module damaged by the short

symptoms: Lean condition on bank 2 under load

P21E8.title: Cylinder 7 Injector B Circuit Low
P21E8.description: P21E8 covers a low, ground-side fault on the cylinder 7 B injector. GM lists it for the 2019 Corvette ZR1, where the LT5 V8 carries a direct and a supplemental injector per cylinder and cylinder 7 is the rearmost cylinder of the left bank (bank 1). The supplemental injectors have their own control module, the FICM, and that module stores the code: below 0.5 Ohm between low side and ground while its driver is off, 20 failures in 25 samples, continuous monitoring, Type A with the MIL in the first trip. Since the limit is close to a dead short, a slowly corroding connector usually shows up as a misfire before it trips this code. Expect rich running on bank 1. The neighbours are P21E9 (high) and, for the A injector, P0279; an open circuit on other makes appears as P21D5.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 B injector wire grounded at the rear of the engine
Injector coil leaking to ground
FICM output faulty

P21E9.title: Cylinder 7 Injector B Circuit High
P21E9.description: P21E9 indicates that the low side of the cylinder 7 B injector carries supply voltage. On GM's 2019 Corvette ZR1 LT5, the FICM declares this when it sees 0.5 Ohm or less to power with the driver off, provided the engine runs and the powertrain relay delivers 11 V or more; Type A, one trip. The rear left cylinder then gets only its direct injector. As the extra port fuel on this engine is meant for boosted operation, the effect may be limited to full throttle, where bank 1 can turn lean. CARB demands that output components be checked for circuit faults, yet leaves it to the maker whether shorts to power get their own code; GM separates them, while Ford folds every B-injector short into the open code (here P21D5). Low fault: P21E8; A injector high: P0280.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 B injector control wire shorted to battery voltage
Injector coil with too low resistance
Injection control module driver defective

P21EA.title: Cylinder 8 Injector B Circuit Low
P21EA.description: P21EA is the ground-short code for the B injector of cylinder 8 and the last low code in GM's 2019 FICM table for the Corvette ZR1 LT5, because the V8 ends there. Cylinder 8 is the rearmost of the right bank (bank 2). The module flags 0.5 Ohm or less between the switched-off low side and ground in 20 of 25 samples of 100 ms, with the engine running and 11 V or more at the powertrain relay, as a Type A fault. Mitsubishi's four-cylinder dual-injection engine never reaches this code, and Ford treats a B-injector short on cylinder 8 as P21D6. A grounded low side can hold the injector open, so bank 2 runs rich and fuel can wash the cylinder wall. P21EB is the high fault; the A injector low fault is P0282.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 B injector wiring chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion in the cylinder 8 injector plug
Injector shorted to its body
FICM driver stuck on

symptoms: Hard hot start or misfire on cylinder 8

P21EB.title: Cylinder 8 Injector B Circuit High
P21EB.description: P21EB is set when the cylinder 8 B injector circuit is shorted toward power. It closes GM's run of B-injector codes for the 2019 Corvette ZR1 LT5: the FICM sees the switched-off low side within 0.5 Ohm of supply in 20 of 25 samples and stores a Type A fault, lighting the MIL in the first trip. The supplemental injector of the right-rear cylinder can then no longer be opened, while the direct injector keeps working, so the car usually drives normally until high boost, where bank 2 may lean out. If several of these high codes appear together, a common feed or a shared connector is more likely than eight bad injectors. P21EA is the matching low fault, P0283 the A injector high fault and P0308 the misfire counter of this cylinder.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 B injector control wire shorted to a feed wire
Shared harness connector shorted when several injectors are affected
Injector coil shorted
Injection control module damaged

P21EC.title: Cylinder 9 Injector B Circuit Low
P21EC.description: P21EC signals a low circuit state, usually a grounded wire or, depending on the maker, also a break, on the B injector of cylinder 9. It can only occur on an engine with at least nine cylinders and two injectors per cylinder. No manufacturer documents it publicly; GM's and Ford's lists stop at cylinder 8. The one such engine on record is Lamborghini's Huracán V10, which combines direct and multi-point injection; which of the two it calls B is not published. Its firing order alternates between cylinders 1 to 5 and 6 to 10, so cylinder 9 belongs to the second bank. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such output components. By analogy with GM's V8, a ground below about 0.5 Ohm on the switched-off low side would count. Open circuit: P21D7; high fault: P21ED.

causes.label: Cylinder 9 B injector wire shorted to ground
Broken wire, if the maker reports opens under the low code
Injector coil shorted to housing or open
Engine control module output faulty

symptoms: Misfire or rough running on cylinder 9
Mixture deviation on the bank of cylinder 9

P21ED.title: Cylinder 9 Injector B Circuit High
P21ED.description: P21ED is defined for a B injector circuit on cylinder 9 that reads high, meaning the control side is shorted to supply or, on some designs, the two injector wires touch. No manufacturer publishes thresholds or vehicles for it. Only engines with ten or more cylinders and dual injection could set it; Lamborghini's Huracán V10 with direct plus multi-point injection is the documented example, although its A/B naming is not public. CARB requires that an output component be flagged when it does not respond properly to commands, which is exactly the case here: the injector cannot be switched, so cylinder 9 depends on its other injector alone. Lean running at loads where both injectors work together is the likely result. Low fault: P21EC; A injector high fault: P0286.

causes.label: Control wire of the cylinder 9 B injector shorted to power
Both injector wires bridged in the harness
Injector coil shorted internally
Driver stage in the control unit faulty

symptoms: Cylinder 9 lean in mixed injection operation

P21EE.title: Cylinder 10 Injector B Circuit Low
P21EE.description: P21EE is the low-circuit code for the B injector of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. In practice that points to a ten-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder, of which only Lamborghini's Huracán is documented: its V10 pairs a direct injector with a port injector at each cylinder and was presented as the first V10 to combine both. Lamborghini does not publish which set is B or whether it uses this code. With cylinders 1 to 5 on one bank and 6 to 10 on the other, cylinder 10 is on the second bank. A short to ground is the core fault; CARB lets a maker report a broken wire under the same code instead of a separate open code. Before replacing parts, read the open code P21D8 and the A injector low code P0288 as well. High fault: P21EF.

causes.label: Cylinder 10 B injector wire grounded
Damaged or corroded injector connector on cylinder 10
Injector with internal ground fault
Engine control unit output defective

symptoms: Rough running or misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)
Fuel trim deviation on the second bank

P21EF.title: Cylinder 10 Injector B Circuit High
P21EF.description: P21EF stands for a high reading on the B injector circuit of cylinder 10. No public manufacturer document covers it, so the exact threshold is unknown; the closest documented model is GM's LT5 V8, where a switched-off low side within 0.5 Ohm of supply counts as a short and sets a Type A fault. A vehicle needs ten or more cylinders and two injectors each to use the code, which so far is documented only for Lamborghini's V10 in the Huracán. A short to power keeps the injector from ever opening, and switching against it strains the output stage, which may need replacement if the fault persisted. When P21EF shows up together with other high codes on the same bank, look for a common supply or connector. Low fault: P21EE; A injector high fault: P0289.

causes.label: Cylinder 10 B injector control wire touching a live circuit
Short inside a connector shared by several injectors
Injector coil shorted
Output stage overloaded by the short

symptoms: Cylinder 10 weak or misfiring under load
Lean mixture on the second bank

P21F0.title: Cylinder 11 Injector B Circuit Low
P21F0.description: P21F0 is reserved for a low state, typically a wire touching ground, in the B injector circuit of cylinder 11. Setting it requires at least eleven cylinders with two injectors each, so in practice a V12 or W12 with combined port and direct injection. No such engine could be confirmed: Lamborghini's V12 family uses multi-point injection only, as do Aston Martin's V12 and Mercedes-AMG's M279. Accordingly no manufacturer documents the code. If a scan tool still shows it, check the cylinder count and whether the maker uses the number for something else. The generic logic follows CARB's circuit monitoring of output components; GM's V8 shows how it is usually judged (short to ground below 0.5 Ohm with the driver off). Open circuit: P21D9; high fault: P21F1.

causes.label: Cylinder 11 B injector wire shorted to ground
Injector with internal short to ground
Code read on an engine without a cylinder 11 B injector (scan tool or maker-specific use)

P21F1.title: Cylinder 11 Injector B Circuit High
P21F1.description: P21F1 describes a cylinder 11 B injector circuit that sits too high, i.e. its switched side is shorted to supply. The code exists in SAE J2012 for completeness of the cylinder series, but no public manufacturer source uses it, and no twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder could be documented. CARB still requires an emission-relevant output to be checked for circuit faults, while allowing makers to combine fault types; a system could therefore report this short under the open code P21D9 instead. Electrically, a short to power keeps the injector from opening and loads the driver each time it switches. GM's LT5 V8 shows typical criteria for the same fault type, 0.5 Ohm or less to power in the driver-off state, Type A. Low fault: P21F0; A injector high: P0292.

causes.label: Control wire of the cylinder 11 B injector shorted to power
Injector coil shorted
Control module driver damaged

P21F2.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Circuit Low
P21F2.description: P21F2 is the generic code for a low circuit state, usually a grounded control wire, at the B injector of cylinder 12. It would need a twelve-cylinder engine with two injectors per cylinder, and none could be documented: the V12s from Lamborghini and Aston Martin inject into the ports only. No manufacturer publishes the code in this sense. One maker does use the number differently: McLaren bulletin KA-01931 lists P21F205 and P21F22F on the Artura, a V6 plug-in hybrid, as high-voltage battery faults (safety design current too low/high), repaired by replacing battery parts. On an Artura it is therefore a battery fault, not an injector fault. For a genuine injector fault, CARB's circuit monitoring applies, and GM's V8 criteria (ground short below 0.5 Ohm) are a guide. High fault: P21F3.

causes.label: Cylinder 12 B injector wire shorted to ground
Injector with internal ground fault
Manufacturer-specific use of the number (McLaren Artura high-voltage battery)

symptoms: Hybrid warning instead, if the code is a McLaren battery fault

P21F3.title: Cylinder 12 Injector B Circuit High
P21F3.description: P21F3 ends the B injector series of SAE J2012: a high signal on the cylinder 12 circuit, caused by a short to supply on the switched side. The series runs from P21CF to P21DA for opens and from P21DB to P21F3 for low/high pairs; the A injector equivalent here is P0295. Public manufacturer documents only reach cylinder 8 (GM's LT5 V8) or cylinder 4 (Mitsubishi), and no twelve-cylinder with dual injection could be documented, since Lamborghini's and Aston Martin's V12s use port injection alone. Should the code appear, the injector cannot open; cylinder 12 then relies on its other injector, and the driver stage takes the brunt of each switching attempt. GM's criteria for the same fault type serve as a guide: within 0.5 Ohm of power with the driver off. Low fault: P21F2.

causes.label: Control wire of the cylinder 12 B injector shorted to supply
Injector coil with shorted windings
Driver stage damaged by a lasting short

P21F4.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F4.description: P21F4 reports that the second fuel path on bank 1 needs more added fuel than its adaptation may supply once the engine has left idle, in the part-load range. Engines with port and direct injection learn a correction for each path; Ford calls its direct system A and its port system B. Audi documents the code on the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS with the 2.5 TFSI five-cylinder (DAZA), which pairs 250 bar direct with 7 bar manifold injection: bulletin 2059429/1 groups it with P21F5, P21F8, P2177, P2187 and P0087, reports MIL and weak performance, and prescribes ECM software 0005 instead of new parts. Without such a bulletin, suspect restricted port injectors or too little pressure in the low-pressure rail. The system A counterpart is P2177.

causes.label: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Port injectors of bank 1 restricted or delivering too little
Pressure in the low-pressure (port) fuel rail too low
Air mass sensor reading too low

symptoms: Weak performance or hesitation at part load
Often stored together with P2177 or P0087

P21F5.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 1)
P21F5.description: P21F5 is the rich limit for the second fuel path of bank 1 in the part-load zone above idle: the learned correction already removes as much fuel as allowed, yet the front sensor still sees surplus fuel. Audi lists the code for the 2.5 TFSI in the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS, whose manifold injectors run on a 7 bar rail beside the high-pressure system, and cures it by reprogramming the engine control module (bulletin 2059429/1). In other cases, a port injector that leaks or opens too long, excessive pressure in the low-pressure rail or an air mass reading that is too high are typical. An FCA patent for such engines clears a mode-specific fault only after the monitor passes again in the same injection mode. Expect higher consumption; P2178 is the system A partner.

causes.label: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Port injector on bank 1 leaking or sticking open
Pressure in the low-pressure rail above specification
Air mass sensor reading too high

P21F6.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F6.description: P21F6 is the bank 2 form of P21F4 and only exists on V or flat engines whose cylinder banks each have their own front oxygen sensor and two injection paths. Here the part-load correction of the second path on bank 2 has reached its lean limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford, whose 5.0 Coyote V8 gained direct injection on top of port injection for 2018, reports a lean port-injection fault on bank 2 as P2BF2 instead, without load zones, once long-term trim exceeds 25 % together with short-term trim above 1 % for 2 s. CARB demands a fault once adaptive control has used up its permitted range. If bank 1 stays clean, look at bank 2 alone: a clogged port injector or a wiring fault on that bank's injector harness.

causes.label: Restricted port injector on bank 2
Wiring or connector fault on the bank 2 injector harness
Low pressure in the shared port fuel rail (if bank 1 also lean)

P21F7.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)
P21F7.description: P21F7 sets when the second fuel path on bank 2 has to remove more fuel above idle than its rich limit permits. It needs an engine with two banks, separate front sensors and dual injection; inline engines such as Audi's 2.5 TFSI only have the bank 1 codes. No manufacturer publishes criteria for P21F7. An FCA patent for port plus direct injection engines explains the idea behind such split codes: a fault seen while only one path is fuelling is assigned to that path, whereas a fault during mixed operation goes to a general code such as P0175. When only this bank is affected, a leaking port injector on bank 2 or a bank 2 front sensor that reads rich is plausible; if both banks are rich, check what they share, such as pressure regulation. P2180 is the system A counterpart.

causes.label: Leaking port injector on bank 2
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Low-pressure regulation too high (if bank 1 also rich)

P21F8.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F8.description: P21F8 covers the idle zone: the second fuel path of bank 1 needs more extra fuel at idle than its adaptation allows. Airflow at idle is so small that a fixed amount of unmetered air or a slightly sluggish injector shifts the mixture a lot, which is why makers learn idle separately from part load. Audi is the only manufacturer naming the code publicly: bulletin 2059429/1 of May 2020 places it among the trim and fuel pressure codes of the 2017 to 2018 RS 3 and TT RS with the 2.5 TFSI and resolves them with new ECM software, stating that replaced parts are not reimbursed. On other engines, check for intake leaks behind the air mass sensor, a port injector delivering too little, or low pressure in the port fuel rail. P2187 is the matching code for system A.

causes.label: Outdated engine control software (Audi 2.5 TFSI, bulletin 2059429/1)
Unmetered air entering behind the air mass sensor
Port injector on bank 1 delivering too little
Low pressure in the port fuel rail

P21F9.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)
P21F9.description: P21F9 reports that bank 1's second fuel path runs rich at idle even though its correction has already reached the lower limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi's 2.5 TFSI bulletin lists only the lean idle code P21F8 and the off-idle pair. Ford's port injection monitor shows how such a check works: it runs in closed loop with purge switched off, coolant at 70 to 110 °C and at least 12 % load, and flags a rich fault when long-term trim passes 25 % in the rich direction while short-term trim agrees, for 2 s (P2BF1, without separate idle cells). Typical causes at idle are a port injector that drips after closing, low-pressure regulation that is too high, or fuel vapour reaching the intake via crankcase ventilation. P2188 is the system A partner.

causes.label: Port injector on bank 1 dripping after closing
Low-pressure fuel regulation holding too much pressure
Fuel vapour entering via crankcase ventilation (fuel-diluted oil)

P21FA.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FA.description: P21FA is the bank 2 version of the idle lean check for the second fuel path. It applies to engines with two cylinder banks, a front oxygen sensor per bank and dual injection, such as Ford's 5.0 V8, which has combined port and direct injection since 2018. No manufacturer publishes this code; Ford monitors its port system per bank without separate idle cells and would store the fault as P2BF2. At idle the per-bank correction reacts strongly to small absolute errors, so a leak at bank 2's intake runners or gasket, or a partly blocked port injector on that side, are the first suspects while bank 1 stays clean. Drivers may notice an uneven idle or nothing beyond the warning lamp. The system A equivalent is P2189.

causes.label: Intake leak at bank 2 runners or gasket
Partly blocked port injector on bank 2
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading lean

P21FB.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Idle (Bank 2)
P21FB.description: P21FB means bank 2's second fuel path is rich at idle while its correction already sits at the rich limit. The code requires an engine with a separate front sensor per bank and two injection paths; no maker documents it publicly. CARB section (e)(6.2.2) is the legal basis: once adaptive fuel control has used up the adjustment the manufacturer allows, a fault must be stored. Rich idle on one bank only typically comes from a port injector on that bank that leaks or sticks open, or from a bank 2 front sensor that reports too rich. If both banks show rich idle codes, look at shared items such as low-pressure regulation or fuel entering through crankcase ventilation. Fuel smell and a rough idle are possible; P2190 is the system A sibling.

causes.label: Port injector on bank 2 leaking or sticking open
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
Low-pressure regulation too high or fuel from crankcase ventilation (if both banks rich)

P21FC.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FC.description: P21FC is the lean check of bank 1's second fuel path in the upper load zone, the third cell next to idle (P21F8) and part load (P21F4). Under high load, delivery capacity matters most: a weak lift pump, a clogged filter or a low-pressure rail that sags at high flow show up here first. On engines combining both paths, the share of each depends on the operating point; Audi's 2.5 TFSI, for example, uses 95 % direct and only 5 % manifold injection at heavy load during warm-up, so the second path's share and its trim learning vary strongly. No manufacturer documents P21FC publicly; Audi's bulletin for that engine covers only the idle and off-idle codes. Hesitation under full load is possible. P2191 is the system A counterpart.

causes.label: Weak in-tank lift pump or clogged fuel filter
Port rail pressure dropping at high flow
Port injectors on bank 1 flowing too little
Charge air leak behind the air mass sensor

symptoms: Hesitation or power loss at full load

P21FD.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P21FD.description: P21FD sets when the second fuel path on bank 1 is still rich at higher load although its learned correction has already taken away the permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. The FCA patent for port plus direct injection engines describes three separate monitors, one per injection mode, so a rich error that appears only while the port system fuels alone can be pinned on that system rather than reported as a general P0172. Possible causes are an air mass sensor reading high at large airflow, a regulator in the low-pressure circuit holding too much pressure, or port injectors that over-deliver at long opening times. Higher fuel consumption and sooty tailpipes may follow. P2192 is the system A counterpart, P21FF the bank 2 code.

causes.label: Air mass sensor reading too high at large airflow
Low-pressure regulator holding too much pressure
Port injectors on bank 1 over-delivering

P21FE.title: Fuel Control System B Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FE.description: P21FE is the bank 2 counterpart of P21FC: in the upper load zone the second injection path on bank 2 needs more enrichment than its adaptation may supply. It can only appear on two-bank engines with per-bank sensors and dual injection. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and Ford, which uses port plus direct injection on V engines such as the 5.0 Coyote from 2018, reports port-side lean faults per bank as P2BF2 without load cells. If only bank 2 is lean at high load, suspect restricted port injectors or harness trouble on that bank; if both banks set high-load lean codes, the supply side they share is more likely, for example the lift pump, the filter or the low-pressure sensor. A loss of pull at full throttle may be felt. P2193 belongs to system A.

causes.label: Restricted port injectors on bank 2
Harness or connector fault on bank 2 injectors
Weak shared supply (lift pump, filter, low-pressure sensor) if both banks lean

symptoms: Loss of pull at full throttle

P21FF.title: Fuel Control System B Too Rich at Higher Load (Bank 2)
P21FF.description: P21FF closes the series: bank 2's second fuel path is rich in the upper load range although its correction already removes the largest reduction allowed. No manufacturer publishes criteria for it. Under CARB, a fuel system fault must be stored once adaptive control has exhausted the range the maker allows; threshold, load window and the number of trips are left to the manufacturer. On a V engine with dual injection, port injectors on bank 2 that over-deliver at long pulse widths, or excessive pressure in the shared low-pressure rail, would push this bank rich. If only bank 2 is affected, also compare the bank 2 front sensor signal with bank 1. Drivers rarely feel anything, but consumption rises. P2194 is the system A twin, P21FD the bank 1 code.

causes.label: Port injectors on bank 2 over-delivering at long pulse widths
Excessive pressure in the shared low-pressure rail
Bank 2 front oxygen sensor reading rich
